entries.text: aloo posto bengali potatoes cooked down in a nutty poppy seed paste, mild and quietly rich vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic potato poppy seeds (khus khus) green chilli mustard oil nigella seeds (kalonji) turmeric powder sugar salt water heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then take it off the heat for 30 seconds to lose its raw bite. return to medium heat, add the nigella seeds and let them sputter for 10 seconds. drain the potatoes, pat dry, and add them with the turmeric and salt. fry 6-7 minutes, turning, until the edges are pale gold. pour in 180ml water, cover, and simmer 10-12 minutes until a knife slides through the potato with slight resistance. stir in the poppy seed paste and the slit green chillies. cook uncovered on low for 6-8 minutes. the gravy is ready when it clings to the potatoes and you can see oil at the edge of the pan. add the sugar, check the salt, and finish with the remaining 1 tbsp raw mustard oil off the heat. rest 5 minutes before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Basanti Pulao
entries.snippet: sweet saffron-yellow ghee rice studded with cashews and raisins
entries.text: basanti pulao bengali sweet saffron-yellow ghee rice studded with cashews and raisins vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic basmati rice ghee turmeric powder saffron cashews raisins (kishmish) bay leaf green cardamom cinnamon cloves ginger sugar salt water heat the remaining 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy pan and fry the cashews until golden, about 90 seconds. lift out. fry the raisins in the same ghee for 20 seconds until they swell, then lift them out too. add the bay leaves, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves and let them puff for 20 seconds. add the grated ginger and stir for 30 seconds. tip in the marinated rice and fry very gently for 3 minutes, folding rather than stirring. pour in 500ml hot water with the sugar, the saffron and its soaking water, and the rest of the salt. bring to a boil, then cover tightly and cook on the lowest possible heat for 12 minutes. turn off the heat and leave it covered and undisturbed for 10 minutes. uncover, fork through the fried cashews and raisins, and serve with kosha mangsho or a dry vegetable.

entries.title: Begun Bhaja
entries.snippet: thick eggplant slices fried until the edges go dark and lacy
entries.text: begun bhaja bengali thick eggplant slices fried until the edges go dark and lacy vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic eggplant / brinjal turmeric powder red chilli powder sugar rice flour mustard oil salt heat the mustard oil in a wide tawa until it smokes, then lower the heat to medium. lay in the eggplant rounds in a single layer, leaving space between them. fry 3-4 minutes without touching them, until the underside is deep brown and the edge looks frilled. turn once with a flat spatula and fry the second side 3 minutes. press the centre lightly — it should give completely, with no firm core left. lift onto kitchen paper and fry the next batch, adding a little more oil if the pan looks dry. serve immediately alongside hot rice and dal, while the edges are still crisp.

entries.title: Chingri Malai Curry
entries.snippet: prawns in a sweet cardamom-scented coconut milk gravy
entries.text: chingri malai curry bengali prawns in a sweet cardamom-scented coconut milk gravy pescatarian gluten-free nut-free prawns coconut milk onion ginger turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder green cardamom cinnamon cloves bay leaf green chilli mustard oil ghee sugar garam masala salt heat the mustard oil to smoking, cool for 30 seconds, then sear the prawns 45 seconds a side until they just turn pink at the edges. lift them out immediately. add the bay leaves, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves to the same oil and let them puff for 20 seconds. add the onion paste and fry 7-8 minutes on medium until it turns pale gold and the oil begins to separate. stir in the ginger paste, the remaining turmeric and the kashmiri chilli and cook 1 minute. pour in the coconut milk with the sugar and salt, stirring as you go. simmer on low, uncovered, for 6-7 minutes until the gravy coats the back of a spoon. return the prawns with the slit green chillies and cook exactly 2 minutes. turn off the heat, stir in the ghee and garam masala, and cover for 5 minutes before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Cholar Dal
entries.snippet: bengal gram simmered sweet-spiced with coconut slivers and raisins
entries.text: cholar dal bengali bengal gram simmered sweet-spiced with coconut slivers and raisins vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic chana dal coconut (fresh or desiccated) raisins (kishmish) ghee cumin seeds bay leaf dried red chillies cinnamon green cardamom cloves ginger turmeric powder sugar garam masala salt water drain the soaked dal and pressure cook with 700ml water, the turmeric and half the salt for 2 whistles, then let the pressure drop naturally. open the cooker and mash lightly against the side with a spoon — about a quarter of the dal, no more. keep it on low heat while you make the tempering. heat the remaining 2 tbsp ghee in a small pan. add the bay leaves, dried red chillies, cinnamon, cardamom and cloves and let them swell for 20 seconds. add the cumin seeds and grated ginger and fry 20 seconds until fragrant. pour the whole tempering into the dal, stir, and simmer 8 minutes uncovered. add the sugar and raisins and cook another 3 minutes until the raisins plump. stir in the garam masala and most of the fried coconut. check the salt. scatter the last of the coconut over the top and serve hot with luchi.

entries.title: Dhokar Dalna
entries.snippet: diamonds of fried chana dal cake simmered in a gingery potato gravy
entries.text: dhokar dalna bengali diamonds of fried chana dal cake simmered in a gingery potato gravy vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic chana dal potato tomato ginger green chilli asafoetida (hing) cumin seeds nigella seeds (kalonji) bay leaf turmeric powder cumin powder (jeera) coriander powder red chilli powder garam masala mustard oil ghee sugar salt water heat 2 tbsp mustard oil in a kadhai, add 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, the nigella and half the asafoetida, and let them crackle for 15 seconds. add the dal paste with 1/2 tsp turmeric and salt. stir constantly over medium heat for 10-12 minutes. tip the hot mixture onto the oiled tray and press it flat to about 1.5cm with the back of a wet spoon. cool 30 minutes, then cut into diamonds. heat 3 tbsp oil and fry the diamonds in batches, 2-3 minutes a side, until crusted and deep gold, handling them with a flat spatula. drain and set aside. in the same pan fry the potato quarters with a pinch of turmeric for 5 minutes until golden. set aside. add the last 1 tbsp oil, the bay leaves, remaining cumin seeds and asafoetida, and crackle 15 seconds. add the remaining ginger paste and cook 1 minute, then the tomato puree and all the ground spices. fry this masala 6-8 minutes, sprinkling in a tablespoon of water whenever it sticks, until the oil separates at the edges. add the potatoes, 600ml water, the slit chilli, sugar and salt. simmer covered 15 minutes until the potato is tender. slide in the fried dhoka pieces and simmer uncovered 3-4 minutes only. finish with the garam masala and ghee, rest 5 minutes, and serve with rice.

entries.title: Dimer Dalna
entries.snippet: boiled eggs fried golden then simmered in a spiced potato gravy
entries.text: dimer dalna bengali boiled eggs fried golden then simmered in a spiced potato gravy vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free eggs potato onion tomato ginger garlic turmeric powder red chilli powder cumin powder (jeera) coriander powder cumin seeds bay leaf garam masala mustard oil sugar coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat the mustard oil to smoking in a kadhai, then reduce to medium. roll the pricked eggs in 1/2 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt and fry them 3-4 minutes, turning, until blistered and golden. lift out. fry the halved potatoes in the same oil for 6 minutes until browned on the cut sides. set aside. add the bay leaves and cumin seeds to the oil and let them crackle 15 seconds. add the chopped onion and fry 8-10 minutes until deep golden brown. stir in the garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute, then add the tomato and cook 4 minutes until it breaks down. add the spice paste and fry 5-6 minutes, splashing in water whenever it catches, until oil pools at the edge. return the potatoes with 500ml water, the sugar and salt. simmer covered 15 minutes until tender. add the fried eggs and simmer uncovered 5 minutes so they take on colour. stir in the garam masala, scatter the coriander leaves, and rest 5 minutes before serving with rice or luchi.

entries.title: Doi Maach
entries.snippet: fish poached in whisked yogurt with cardamom and ginger, tangy and pale gold
entries.text: doi maach bengali fish poached in whisked yogurt with cardamom and ginger, tangy and pale gold pescatarian gluten-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) yogurt / dahi onion ginger turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder green cardamom cinnamon cloves bay leaf green chilli mustard oil ghee sugar salt water heat the mustard oil to smoking, cool it slightly, then fry the fish steaks 2-3 minutes a side until just set. lift out. pour off all but 3 tbsp of the oil. add the bay leaves, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves and let them swell for 20 seconds. add the onion paste and fry 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until it is pale gold and no longer smells sharp. add the ginger paste and cook 1 minute more. take the pan off the heat entirely and let it cool for a full minute. add the spiced yogurt a spoonful at a time, stirring continuously, until it is all in and smooth. return to the lowest heat and cook 5-6 minutes, stirring in one direction, until the gravy thickens and gloss appears on the surface. add 150ml water, the sugar, salt and slit chillies and bring to the barest simmer. slide the fish back in, spoon the gravy over, and cook 5 minutes covered. finish with the ghee off the heat and rest 10 minutes before serving with rice.

entries.title: Kosha Mangsho
entries.snippet: Mutton slow-fried in its own masala until almost dry and very dark
entries.text: kosha mangsho bengali mutton slow-fried in its own masala until almost dry and very dark gluten-free nut-free mutton / lamb yogurt / dahi onion ginger garlic turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala bay leaf cinnamon green cardamom sugar mustard oil potato salt marinate the mutton with yogurt, turmeric and salt for an hour. heat the mustard oil to smoking, cool slightly, then caramelise the sugar until it darkens — this is where the colour comes from. add the whole spices and sliced onion and fry until genuinely brown, 12-15 minutes. add ginger, garlic and the powdered spices, then the marinated mutton. now begin koshano: fry over medium-low heat, stirring often, for 30-40 minutes. when the oil separates and the meat is deep brown, add just enough hot water to cover, cover the pan and simmer 30-40 minutes until tender. add the fried potatoes for the last 10 minutes, finish with garam masala, and reduce until the gravy clings.

entries.title: Labra
entries.snippet: a soft mixed vegetable torkari fragrant with panch phoron and ginger
entries.text: labra bengali a soft mixed vegetable torkari fragrant with panch phoron and ginger vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic pumpkin potato sweet potato eggplant / brinjal raw banana / plantain french beans cabbage panch phoron dried red chillies bay leaf ginger turmeric powder cumin powder (jeera) asafoetida (hing) mustard oil sugar garam masala salt water heat the mustard oil to smoking in a wide kadhai, then reduce the heat. add the bay leaves, dried red chillies and the remaining 1/2 tsp whole panch phoron. let them crackle 15 seconds. add the asafoetida and the grated ginger and stir for 30 seconds. tip in the potato and sweet potato and fry 4 minutes until the edges are translucent. add the pumpkin, raw banana, beans and cabbage with the turmeric, cumin powder and salt. fold gently for 3 minutes. add the eggplant last, along with 200ml water. cover and cook on low for 18-20 minutes. uncover: the pumpkin should have collapsed and be binding everything into a rough mash. cook uncovered 4-5 minutes to drive off the last of the water. stir in the sugar, garam masala and the crushed toasted panch phoron. rest 5 minutes and serve with khichuri or rice.

entries.title: Luchi
entries.snippet: small white maida puris that puff into balloons, the sunday-morning bread
entries.text: luchi bengali small white maida puris that puff into balloons, the sunday-morning bread vegetarian nut-free no-onion-garlic plain flour (maida) ghee salt sugar water neutral oil mix the maida, salt and sugar, then rub in the ghee with your fingertips for 2 minutes until it looks like damp sand. add the lukewarm water a little at a time and knead 6-8 minutes into a smooth, firm, non-sticky dough. cover and rest 20 minutes. divide into 20 balls the size of a large marble and roll each into a 9cm circle, greasing the board with a drop of oil rather than dusting with flour. heat the oil in a deep kadhai to 180c — a scrap of dough should rise to the surface within 2 seconds. slide in one luchi. it will sink, then float within 3 seconds. press the centre down gently with the back of a slotted spoon for 3-4 seconds and it will balloon. flip and fry the second side 15 seconds only. luchi should stay white and blond, never brown. drain upright in a colander rather than flat on paper so they stay puffed. serve straight away with cholar dal or aloo dum.

entries.title: Macher Jhol
entries.snippet: a thin turmeric and ginger fish broth built around fried rohu steaks
entries.text: macher jhol bengali a thin turmeric and ginger fish broth built around fried rohu steaks pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) potato tomato eggplant / brinjal turmeric powder red chilli powder cumin powder (jeera) ginger nigella seeds (kalonji) green chilli mustard oil coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then lower to medium-high. slide in the fish steaks and fry 3 minutes a side until the surface is firm and browned. lift the fish out onto a plate and leave the oil in the pan. fry the potato wedges in the same oil for 5 minutes until golden at the edges, then add the eggplant for 2 minutes. push the vegetables aside, add the nigella seeds to the clear space and let them pop for 10 seconds. stir in the spice paste and fry 2-3 minutes until it darkens and stops smelling raw. add the tomato, slit chillies, 700ml water and salt. bring to a boil and simmer 12 minutes until the potato is tender. return the fish steaks, spooning gravy over them, and simmer 4 minutes only. turn off the heat, scatter the coriander, and rest 5 minutes before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Mishti Doi
entries.snippet: milk boiled down with caramelised jaggery and set into a thick fudgy curd
entries.text: mishti doi bengali milk boiled down with caramelised jaggery and set into a thick fudgy curd vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic milk jaggery sugar yogurt / dahi green cardamom bring the milk to a boil in a heavy pan, then lower the heat and simmer 30-35 minutes, scraping the skin at the sides back in each time, until it reduces to about 900ml. meanwhile melt the 2 tbsp sugar in a small dry pan over medium heat until it turns the colour of dark honey, about 4 minutes. stir the caramel into the reduced milk — it will hiss — and cook 2 minutes more. add the chopped jaggery and cardamom and stir off the heat until fully dissolved. cool the milk to 45c — warm to a fingertip but not hot enough to sting. whisk the starter yogurt smooth in a cup, then whisk in a ladle of the warm milk. pour that back into the pan, stir twice only, and pour into the earthenware bowl or ramekins. cover and leave in a warm, draught-free place — a switched-off oven with the light on works well — for 6-8 hours without moving it. when it is set firm enough that the surface does not wobble as a whole, chill for at least 4 hours before serving.

entries.title: Payesh
entries.snippet: rice cooked slowly down in milk with cardamom and date palm jaggery
entries.text: payesh bengali rice cooked slowly down in milk with cardamom and date palm jaggery vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic milk rice (short/medium grain) jaggery sugar green cardamom bay leaf ghee cashews raisins (kishmish) salt bring the milk to a boil with the bay leaf and bruised cardamom, then lower to a bare simmer. simmer 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes and scraping the skin from the sides back in, until it has reduced by about a quarter. add the drained, ghee-coated rice and the pinch of salt. cook on low for 30-35 minutes, stirring every 3-4 minutes so nothing sticks, until the grains are completely soft and the milk has thickened to the consistency of pouring cream. fry the cashews and raisins in a dry pan for 90 seconds until the cashews are gold and the raisins swell. stir them into the payesh and cook 2 minutes more. take the pan off the heat and let it cool for 8-10 minutes — the surface should no longer be steaming hard. stir in the chopped jaggery and the sugar if using until fully dissolved. do not put the pan back on the heat. cool to room temperature, then chill at least 2 hours before serving.

entries.title: Peyaji
entries.snippet: crisp onion fritters shot through with nigella and green chilli
entries.text: peyaji bengali crisp onion fritters shot through with nigella and green chilli vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free onion besan (gram flour) rice flour nigella seeds (kalonji) green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder baking soda coriander leaves (cilantro) mustard oil salt squeeze the salted onions lightly with your hands to bring out their water, keeping the liquid in the bowl. add the besan, rice flour, nigella, green chilli, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander leaves and mix with your fingers. the mixture should just cling together in a ragged clump — add 1 tsp water at a time only if it is genuinely dry. heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then bring it down to a steady 170c. drop in irregular clumps the size of a walnut, six or seven at a time. fry 4-5 minutes, turning once at the halfway point, until deep amber and no longer bubbling hard. lift onto a wire rack, not paper, so the undersides stay crisp. fry the next batch, letting the oil come back up to temperature between batches, and serve hot with rice and dal or on their own with mustard.

entries.title: Rasgulla
entries.snippet: Chhena dumplings boiled in light syrup until they double and turn spongy
entries.text: rasgulla bengali chhena dumplings boiled in light syrup until they double and turn spongy vegetarian gluten-free nut-free milk lemon / lime sugar green cardamom rose water plain flour (maida) water bring the milk to a boil, take it off the heat, and add lemon juice a little at a time until the curds separate cleanly from greenish whey. strain through muslin and rinse under cold water to wash out the acid. hang 30 minutes — no longer. knead the chhena on a plate with the heel of your hand for 8-10 minutes, until it goes from grainy to smooth and slightly greasy. work in the maida if using. roll into 12 crack-free balls, smaller than you want them finished — they double. bring the sugar and water to a rolling boil with the cardamom. slide the balls in, cover, and boil hard for 15 minutes. cool in the syrup, add rose water, and chill at least 4 hours before serving.

entries.title: Sandesh
entries.snippet: fresh chhena kneaded with sugar into a soft barely-cooked milk sweet
entries.text: sandesh bengali fresh chhena kneaded with sugar into a soft barely-cooked milk sweet vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic milk lemon / lime sugar green cardamom saffron water bring the milk to a full boil in a heavy pan, then turn the heat off completely. wait 60 seconds, then add the diluted lemon juice a spoonful at a time, stirring slowly, until the curds separate and the whey runs pale green. pour into the muslin-lined colander and rinse the curds under cold water for 30 seconds to wash off the lemon and stop the cooking. gather the muslin, squeeze gently, and hang for 30 minutes. tip the chhena onto a clean surface and knead with the heel of your hand for 8-10 minutes until it goes from grainy to completely smooth and slightly greasy. work in the powdered sugar and cardamom and knead 2 minutes more. transfer to a non-stick pan and cook on the lowest heat for 6-8 minutes, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens and pulls away from the sides in a mass. spread on a plate and cool 15 minutes until it is comfortable to handle but still warm. divide into 12 while still warm, roll each into a ball and flatten slightly, pressing a strand of saffron or a thumbprint into the top. cool completely before serving.

entries.title: Shorshe Ilish
entries.snippet: Hilsa poached in a raw mustard paste, the dish Bengal argues about most
entries.text: shorshe ilish bengali hilsa poached in a raw mustard paste, the dish bengal argues about most gluten-free dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) mustard seeds green chilli turmeric powder nigella seeds (kalonji) mustard oil salt soak the mustard seeds 20 minutes in warm water, then grind with 2 green chillies and a pinch of salt to a smooth paste. strain if you want it silky. rub the fish with turmeric and salt and rest 10 minutes. heat the mustard oil until it just smokes, then take it off the heat for a moment — this removes the raw pungency. return to low heat, add the nigella, then the mustard paste thinned with half a cup of water, the remaining chillies and salt. simmer 3 minutes. slide in the fish in a single layer, spoon the sauce over, cover and cook 8 minutes. do not stir — shake the pan. finish with a tablespoon of raw mustard oil poured over, and rest 5 minutes before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Shukto
entries.snippet: a gently bitter mixed vegetable stew in milk, eaten first with rice
entries.text: shukto bengali a gently bitter mixed vegetable stew in milk, eaten first with rice vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic bitter gourd (karela) drumstick (moringa pod) raw banana / plantain sweet potato eggplant / brinjal radish (mooli) milk mustard seeds poppy seeds (khus khus) panch phoron fennel seeds (saunf) ginger bay leaf mustard oil ghee sugar salt water heat 2 tbsp mustard oil to smoking, cool slightly, then fry the bitter gourd rounds 3-4 minutes until browned at the edges. lift out and set aside. in the same oil, fry the eggplant and raw banana for 3 minutes until just coloured. set aside. add the remaining 1 tbsp oil, the bay leaf and the panch phoron, and let it crackle for 15 seconds. add the ginger paste and cook 30 seconds until it smells sweet rather than raw. add the drumstick, radish and sweet potato with the salt and 300ml water. cover and simmer 12 minutes. return the fried vegetables to the pan and simmer uncovered 5 minutes more. stir the mustard and poppy paste into the milk, then pour it in and bring to the barest simmer. cook 4-5 minutes until the gravy is the thickness of single cream. add the sugar and crushed fennel, taste for salt, and finish with the ghee off the heat. rest 10 minutes. shukto is served slightly warm, not piping hot, at the start of the meal.

entries.title: Aloo ki Bhujia
entries.snippet: dry potato fingers tempered with panch phoron and mustard oil, crisp at the edges and no onion in sight
entries.text: aloo ki bhujia bihari dry potato fingers tempered with panch phoron and mustard oil, crisp at the edges and no onion in sight vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic potato mustard oil panch phoron dried red chillies asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder green chilli amchur (dry mango powder) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes faintly, then drop the heat to medium. crackle the panch phoron and broken red chillies for 15-20 seconds, until the fenugreek seeds darken and the mustard seeds start popping. add the asafoetida, swirl once, then tip in the potato fingers and 3/4 tsp salt. toss to coat and spread the potatoes in one layer. fry undisturbed 4 minutes, then turn and fry 4 minutes more. sprinkle over the turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder and toss gently to coat every piece. cover and cook on low for 8 minutes, shaking the pan twice, until a potato finger crushes easily against the side. uncover, raise the heat and fry a final 3-4 minutes until the edges are golden and crisped. add the slit green chillies and amchur, toss, and finish off the heat with coriander leaves. serve with dal and rice or with hot puris.

entries.title: Dal Pitha
entries.snippet: steamed rice-flour dumplings filled with coarse spiced chana dal, tempered in mustard oil
entries.text: dal pitha bihari steamed rice-flour dumplings filled with coarse spiced chana dal, tempered in mustard oil vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice flour chana dal garlic ginger green chilli cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder mustard oil panch phoron dried red chillies coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water grind the drained chana dal with the garlic, ginger, green chilli, 1 tsp cumin seeds and 1 tsp salt to a coarse, sandy mixture with no added water. heat 1 tbsp mustard oil, add the asafoetida and turmeric, then the ground dal, and fry over medium heat for 6-8 minutes until it dries out and smells cooked. bring 450ml water to a rolling boil with 1 tsp salt and 1 tsp mustard oil. take the pan off the heat, tip in the rice flour all at once and stir hard with a wooden spoon until it comes together into a shaggy mass. cover and leave 5 minutes. knead the warm dough with oiled palms for 4-5 minutes until it is completely smooth and takes a fingerprint without cracking. pinch off walnut-sized pieces, roll each into a ball and press into a 8cm disc between oiled palms. place a heaped teaspoon of the dal filling in the centre, fold into a half-moon and press the edge shut, crimping it with your fingers. steam the pithas in a single layer over boiling water for 12-15 minutes, until the surface turns glossy and no longer looks chalky. heat the remaining mustard oil until it smokes faintly, then crackle the panch phoron, remaining cumin seeds and broken red chillies for 20 seconds. toss the steamed pithas in the temper for 2 minutes so they take on a light crust, scatter over the coriander leaves and serve hot with chutney.

entries.title: Ghugni
entries.snippet: dried white peas stewed soft with mustard oil, ginger and cumin, finished with lemon and black salt
entries.text: ghugni bihari dried white peas stewed soft with mustard oil, ginger and cumin, finished with lemon and black salt vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free dried white peas (safed matar) potato onion garlic ginger tomato mustard oil cumin seeds bay leaf turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala black salt (kala namak) green chilli lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water drain the soaked peas and pressure cook them with 600ml water, the turmeric and 1 tsp salt for 3 whistles, then 10 minutes on low. they should crush easily between finger and thumb but still hold their shape. heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes faintly, then lower the heat and let it settle for 30 seconds. crackle the cumin seeds and bay leaf for 20 seconds until the cumin darkens and smells toasted. add the chopped onion and fry over medium heat for 10-12 minutes until deep golden brown at the edges. stir in the garlic and grated ginger and cook 90 seconds, until the raw smell goes. add the tomato and cook 6-8 minutes, pressing it down, until it breaks up and the oil separates at the edges of the pan. add the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder with a splash of water and fry 1 minute so the spices do not burn. tip in the diced potato with 200ml water and cook covered 10 minutes, until the potato is just tender. add the cooked peas with their liquid and the slit green chillies. simmer uncovered 12-15 minutes, mashing a ladleful of peas against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy. stir in the garam masala, taste for salt, and finish off the heat with lemon juice, black salt, julienned ginger and coriander leaves.

entries.title: Kadhi Bari
entries.snippet: fried gram-flour dumplings soaked soft in a tart yogurt gravy with a mustard-oil temper
entries.text: kadhi bari bihari fried gram-flour dumplings soaked soft in a tart yogurt gravy with a mustard-oil temper vegetarian gluten-free nut-free besan (gram flour) yogurt / dahi neutral oil mustard oil onion garlic ginger green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder cumin seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) mustard seeds nigella seeds (kalonji) dried red chillies asafoetida (hing) baking soda coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water whisk 150g besan with 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp turmeric, the baking soda and about 120ml water into a thick batter, then beat hard for 5 minutes until it is pale and fluffy. heat the neutral oil to 170c and drop in walnut-sized spoonfuls of batter. fry 4-5 minutes, turning, until deep golden and hollow-sounding. drain the bari on paper, then soak them in warm water for 10 minutes and squeeze gently. whisk the sour yogurt with the remaining 50g besan, the rest of the turmeric, the chilli powder and 1.2 litres water until absolutely smooth. heat 2 tbsp mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then lower the heat and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds and the fenugreek seeds for 15 seconds. add the chopped onion, garlic, ginger and green chillies and fry 6-8 minutes until the onion turns golden. pour in the yogurt mixture and bring it to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly in one direction. once boiling, lower the heat and simmer uncovered 25 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the kadhi coats a spoon and the raw besan smell is gone. add salt and slip in the squeezed bari. simmer another 8 minutes so they drink up the gravy. in a small pan heat the remaining 1 tbsp mustard oil, crackle the mustard seeds, remaining cumin, nigella, broken red chillies and asafoetida for 20 seconds, and pour it over the kadhi. scatter with coriander leaves and serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Litti Chokha
entries.snippet: baked wheat balls stuffed with spiced roasted gram, dipped in ghee and crushed over smoky brinjal mash
entries.text: litti chokha bihari baked wheat balls stuffed with spiced roasted gram, dipped in ghee and crushed over smoky brinjal mash vegetarian nut-free atta (wholewheat flour) sattu (roasted gram flour) mustard oil ghee carom seeds (ajwain) nigella seeds (kalonji) garlic ginger green chilli lemon / lime eggplant / brinjal potato tomato onion coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water rub 2 tbsp mustard oil and 1 tsp salt into the atta until a squeezed handful holds its shape, then add water a little at a time to make a stiff, smooth dough. cover the dough and rest it 30 minutes. mix the sattu with the garlic, ginger, 4 chopped green chillies, the ajwain, nigella, juice of half the lemon, 3 tbsp mustard oil and 1 tsp salt, rubbing it through your fingers. divide the dough into 10 balls. cup each in your palm, press a hollow, pack in a heaped tablespoon of the sattu mix, then pinch the seam closed and roll smooth. bake at 200c for 25 minutes, turning once at the halfway mark, until the litti are dry, cracked across the top and pale brown. meanwhile rub the brinjal with a little oil and hold it directly over a gas flame, turning, for 10-12 minutes until the skin blisters black and the flesh slumps. char the tomatoes the same way for 5 minutes. boil the potatoes 15 minutes until a knife slides in without resistance, then drain and peel. peel the charred brinjal and tomatoes and mash them with the potato, chopped onion, remaining 2 green chillies, 1 tbsp mustard oil, the juice of the remaining lemon half and salt. fold in the coriander leaves and taste — chokha should be sharp with lemon and raw mustard oil, not bland. dip each hot litti in the melted ghee, holding it under for a few seconds so it soaks, then crush it open and serve over the chokha.

entries.title: Machhli ka Jhor
entries.snippet: river fish simmered in a thin, fiery mustard-oil gravy sharpened with ground mustard seed
entries.text: machhli ka jhor bihari river fish simmered in a thin, fiery mustard-oil gravy sharpened with ground mustard seed pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) mustard oil mustard seeds onion garlic ginger tomato turmeric powder red chilli powder kashmiri chilli powder coriander powder cumin seeds nigella seeds (kalonji) green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat 5 tbsp mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes and the sharp smell dies down, then lower the heat. fry the fish steaks in batches, 2 minutes a side, until the surface is set and pale gold. lift out and set aside. in the same oil add the remaining 2 tbsp, then crackle the cumin seeds and nigella for 20 seconds. add the onion paste and fry 8-10 minutes over medium heat until it loses its raw smell and turns light brown at the edges. stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and cook 2 minutes, until the oil starts to bead at the sides. add the chopped tomato and cook 6 minutes, mashing it down, until it collapses completely. mix the remaining 1 tsp turmeric, the chilli powder, kashmiri chilli and coriander powder with 3 tbsp water and fry this paste for 3-4 minutes until the oil separates and floats clear. stir in the ground mustard paste and cook exactly 1 minute, no longer. pour in 500ml water with the slit green chillies and 1 tsp salt and bring to a boil. the gravy should be thin, like a light broth. slide the fried fish back in, lower the heat and simmer uncovered 8-10 minutes, spooning gravy over the pieces rather than stirring. rest 5 minutes off the heat, scatter with coriander leaves and serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Malpua
entries.snippet: fennel-scented flour pancakes fried in ghee with lace-crisp edges, steeped in light sugar syrup
entries.text: malpua bihari fennel-scented flour pancakes fried in ghee with lace-crisp edges, steeped in light sugar syrup vegetarian nut-free plain flour (maida) milk khoya / mawa sugar water fennel seeds (saunf) green cardamom ghee saffron boil the 300g sugar with 150ml water for 5-6 minutes to a thin one-string syrup, stir in the saffron milk, and keep it warm over the lowest heat. whisk the maida with the grated khoya, 2 tbsp sugar, crushed fennel and ground cardamom. add the milk in three additions, whisking to a smooth, lump-free batter the consistency of thick pouring cream. cover and rest the batter 30 minutes, then check it — it should ribbon off the spoon and settle back in about 3 seconds. heat 2cm of ghee in a small kadhai over medium heat until a drop of batter rises at once with a fizz. pour in a ladleful of batter from a height of about 10cm so it spreads into a 10cm round with frilled edges. fry two at a time at most. fry for 2 minutes without touching it, until the edges turn golden and lift on their own. turn once with a slotted spoon and fry the second side 90 seconds, spooning hot ghee over the centre. lift out, drain for a few seconds, then slide straight into the warm syrup and soak 4-5 minutes a side. lift out of the syrup and serve warm, with rabri or on their own.

entries.title: Namkeen Sattu Sharbat
entries.snippet: savoury roasted gram drink with black salt, lemon and roasted cumin, drunk cold through the summer
entries.text: namkeen sattu sharbat bihari savoury roasted gram drink with black salt, lemon and roasted cumin, drunk cold through the summer vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free sattu (roasted gram flour) water black salt (kala namak) cumin seeds lemon / lime green chilli onion mint coriander leaves (cilantro) salt dry-roast the cumin seeds in the same pan for about 1 minute, until they darken and pop, then crush them coarsely. whisk the sattu with just 100ml of the chilled water to a completely smooth, thick paste. whisk in the remaining 400ml chilled water in a steady stream until the drink is thin and even. stir in the black salt, plain salt, roasted crushed cumin and the juice of the whole lemon. add the green chilli, onion, mint and coriander leaves and stir once. taste and adjust — it should be sour and salty first, with the roasted flour underneath. serve immediately in tall glasses.

entries.title: Sattu ka Paratha
entries.snippet: wheat flatbread packed with garlicky roasted gram flour, sharp with mustard oil and ajwain
entries.text: sattu ka paratha bihari wheat flatbread packed with garlicky roasted gram flour, sharp with mustard oil and ajwain vegetarian vegan dairy-free nut-free atta (wholewheat flour) sattu (roasted gram flour) mustard oil carom seeds (ajwain) nigella seeds (kalonji) garlic ginger green chilli onion lemon / lime amchur (dry mango powder) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water knead the atta with 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp mustard oil and enough water to make a soft, pliable dough, about 6 minutes. cover with a damp cloth and rest 20 minutes. mix the sattu with the garlic, ginger, green chilli, onion, ajwain, nigella, amchur, coriander leaves, lemon juice, 2 tbsp mustard oil and 3/4 tsp salt. divide the dough into 8 balls. roll one into a 10cm disc, mound 2 tbsp of filling in the centre, gather the edges over the top and pinch shut. flatten the sealed ball gently with your palm, dust with flour and roll out to about 18cm, pressing lightly and evenly from the centre. cook on a hot tawa for 1 minute until pale spots appear, flip, and cook the second side 1 minute. brush both sides with mustard oil and cook another minute a side, pressing the edges with a cloth, until brown blisters form. serve straight off the tawa with plain yogurt, chokha or a spoon of pickle.

entries.title: Thekua
entries.snippet: hard, jaggery-sweetened wheat biscuits fried in ghee, made in every home for Chhath
entries.text: thekua bihari hard, jaggery-sweetened wheat biscuits fried in ghee, made in every home for chhath vegetarian nut-free atta (wholewheat flour) jaggery water ghee fennel seeds (saunf) green cardamom coconut (fresh or desiccated) neutral oil salt heat the water with the jaggery over low heat for 4-5 minutes, stirring, until it dissolves completely, then strain and cool to lukewarm. rub the melted ghee into the atta with the salt for 3-4 minutes, until the flour looks damp and clumps when pressed. mix in the crushed fennel, ground cardamom and grated coconut. add the jaggery water a little at a time and bring it together into a very stiff dough. do not knead it smooth. pinch off lime-sized pieces, roll into balls, then flatten each to about 1cm thick. press each disc onto a thekua mould, or score a criss-cross pattern with the back of a fork. heat the frying oil to 150c — low, not hot. a piece of dough should rise slowly after a few seconds. fry in batches for 8-10 minutes, turning often, until the thekua are a deep even brown and float high in the oil. lift out and drain on a rack, not on paper, and let them cool completely — they harden as they cool.

entries.title: Chettinad Chicken Curry
entries.snippet: bone-in chicken in a freshly roasted masala of pepper, fennel and stone flower
entries.text: chettinad chicken curry chettinad bone-in chicken in a freshly roasted masala of pepper, fennel and stone flower gluten-free dairy-free nut-free chicken shallots (small red onions) tomato garlic ginger curry leaves sesame oil (gingelly / til) dried red chillies coriander powder black pepper cumin seeds fennel seeds (saunf) poppy seeds (khus khus) coconut (fresh or desiccated) cinnamon cloves star anise stone flower (dagad phool) bay leaf turmeric powder salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) dry-roast the red chillies, coriander powder, black pepper, cumin, fennel, poppy seeds, cinnamon, cloves, star anise and stone flower in a dry pan over low heat for 4-5 minutes. add the grated coconut to the same pan and roast a further 3 minutes until it turns the colour of weak tea. cool the mixture completely, then grind to a fine powder, add 100ml water and grind again to a smooth thick paste. heat the gingelly oil in a kadhai and add the bay leaf and curry leaves; they will spit for a few seconds. add the shallots and fry over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft and browning at the edges. grind the ginger and garlic to a coarse paste, add it to the pan and fry 2 minutes until the raw smell goes. add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes until they collapse and the oil starts to separate at the sides. stir in the ground masala paste and fry on low for 6-8 minutes, scraping the base, until the oil rises dark red around the edges. add the chicken and turn it in the masala for 5 minutes so every piece is coated and sealed. pour in 200ml water, season with salt, cover and simmer 20-25 minutes until the chicken is tender and the gravy clings. rest off the heat 5 minutes, then scatter the coriander leaves and serve with rice or dosai.

entries.title: Chettinad Kara Kuzhambu
entries.snippet: fiery tamarind gravy with drumstick, brinjal and whole shallots
entries.text: chettinad kara kuzhambu chettinad fiery tamarind gravy with drumstick, brinjal and whole shallots vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free drumstick (moringa pod) eggplant / brinjal shallots (small red onions) garlic tomato tamarind sambar powder red chilli powder turmeric powder black pepper fenugreek seeds (methi) mustard seeds cumin seeds fennel seeds (saunf) toor dal (pigeon pea) asafoetida (hing) curry leaves dried red chillies sesame oil (gingelly / til) jaggery salt water heat the gingelly oil in a kadhai and add the mustard seeds; when they pop, add the toor dal, fenugreek, cumin and fennel. fry 30 seconds until the dal is golden, then add the asafoetida, red chillies and curry leaves. add the whole shallots and garlic and fry 8 minutes over medium heat until browned and softening. add the tomato and cook 4 minutes until it breaks down into the oil. lower the heat, add the sambar powder, chilli powder, turmeric and cracked pepper and fry 1 minute. add the drumstick pieces and turn them in the masala for 2 minutes. pour in the tamarind extract and 150ml water, season with salt and bring to a rolling boil. simmer uncovered 12 minutes until the raw tamarind smell is gone and the gravy has darkened. add the brinjals and simmer a further 8 minutes until they are tender but still holding their shape. stir in the jaggery and simmer 2 minutes more, until the oil floats clear on top. rest 15 minutes off the heat and serve with rice and a spoonful of the oil from the top.

entries.title: Chettinad Meen Kuzhambu
entries.snippet: sharp tamarind fish curry with fenugreek and gingelly oil
entries.text: chettinad meen kuzhambu chettinad sharp tamarind fish curry with fenugreek and gingelly oil pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) tamarind shallots (small red onions) tomato garlic red chilli powder coriander powder turmeric powder black pepper fenugreek seeds (methi) mustard seeds fennel seeds (saunf) curry leaves coconut (fresh or desiccated) sesame oil (gingelly / til) salt water heat the gingelly oil in a clay pot or kadhai and add the mustard seeds; wait for them to pop. add the fenugreek and fennel seeds and fry 20 seconds until the fenugreek turns one shade darker. add the curry leaves, shallots and crushed garlic and fry 7 minutes until the shallots are soft and golden. add the tomato and cook 4 minutes until pulpy. lower the heat, add the chilli powder, coriander powder, remaining turmeric and cracked pepper, and fry 1 minute in the oil. pour in the strained tamarind water and 100ml plain water, season with salt and bring to a boil. simmer uncovered 12-15 minutes until the raw sourness has cooked off and the gravy has reduced by a third. grind the coconut with 50ml water and stir it in, then simmer 3 minutes. slide in the fish pieces in a single layer, spoon gravy over them and simmer 6-8 minutes without stirring. take it off the heat and leave it at least 2 hours before eating; the curry sets and sweetens as it stands.

entries.title: Chettinad Muttai Masala
entries.snippet: boiled eggs simmered in a roasted coconut and pepper masala
entries.text: chettinad muttai masala chettinad boiled eggs simmered in a roasted coconut and pepper masala vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free eggs shallots (small red onions) tomato garlic ginger coconut (fresh or desiccated) dried red chillies coriander powder black pepper fennel seeds (saunf) cumin seeds stone flower (dagad phool) cinnamon cloves star anise poppy seeds (khus khus) turmeric powder curry leaves sesame oil (gingelly / til) salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) dry-roast the red chillies, coriander powder, pepper, fennel, cumin, poppy seeds, stone flower, cinnamon, cloves and star anise over low heat for 4 minutes. add the coconut and roast 3 minutes more until it smells toasty and turns pale brown. cool completely and grind with 100ml water to a smooth paste. heat 2 tbsp of the gingelly oil in a kadhai, add the scored eggs with 1/4 tsp turmeric and a pinch of salt, and fry 3 minutes turning until the skins are blistered and golden. lift the eggs out and set aside; add the remaining oil and the curry leaves to the same pan. fry the shallots for 6 minutes until golden, then add the ginger and garlic pounded to a paste and fry 2 minutes. add the tomatoes and remaining turmeric and cook 5 minutes until pulpy and the oil shows at the edges. stir in the ground masala and fry on low for 6 minutes until it darkens and the oil separates. add 250ml water and salt, bring to a boil, then simmer 8 minutes until the gravy coats the back of a spoon. slip the fried eggs in, spoon gravy over them and simmer 5 minutes on the lowest heat. rest 5 minutes, scatter the coriander and serve with rice or chapati.

entries.title: Chettinad Mutton Kuzhambu
entries.snippet: slow-cooked goat in a dark coconut and roasted-spice gravy
entries.text: chettinad mutton kuzhambu chettinad slow-cooked goat in a dark coconut and roasted-spice gravy gluten-free dairy-free nut-free mutton / lamb shallots (small red onions) tomato garlic ginger coconut (fresh or desiccated) poppy seeds (khus khus) fennel seeds (saunf) black pepper dried red chillies coriander powder cumin seeds stone flower (dagad phool) star anise cinnamon cloves green cardamom curry leaves turmeric powder sesame oil (gingelly / til) salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) dry-roast the red chillies, coriander powder, pepper, cumin, fennel, poppy seeds, stone flower, star anise, cinnamon, cloves and cardamom over low heat for 5 minutes until aromatic. add the grated coconut and roast 4 minutes more until it is an even light brown. cool fully, then grind with 150ml water to a smooth paste. heat the gingelly oil in the pressure cooker base, add the curry leaves and let them splutter. add the shallots and fry 8 minutes until deep gold, then add the ginger and garlic ground to a paste and fry 2 minutes. add the mutton and brown it hard over high heat for 8 minutes, turning, until the pieces are seared all over. add the tomatoes and cook 4 minutes until they break down. stir in the ground masala and fry on low for 8 minutes until the oil separates and the paste darkens to brick. pour in 450ml water, season with salt, close the cooker and cook for 5 whistles, then on low for 12 minutes. let the pressure drop naturally, open, and simmer uncovered 10 minutes until the gravy thickens and glosses. finish with the chopped coriander and rest 10 minutes before serving with rice or idiyappam.

entries.title: Chettinad Nandu Masala
entries.snippet: crab in a thick roasted masala of pepper, fennel and coconut
entries.text: chettinad nandu masala chettinad crab in a thick roasted masala of pepper, fennel and coconut pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free crab shallots (small red onions) tomato garlic ginger coconut (fresh or desiccated) dried red chillies black pepper fennel seeds (saunf) cumin seeds coriander powder poppy seeds (khus khus) stone flower (dagad phool) star anise cinnamon cloves turmeric powder curry leaves sesame oil (gingelly / til) lemon / lime salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) dry-roast the red chillies, pepper, fennel, cumin, coriander powder, poppy seeds, stone flower, star anise, cinnamon and cloves over low heat for 4-5 minutes until fragrant. add the coconut and roast 3 minutes until light brown, then cool completely and grind with 100ml water to a coarse paste. heat the gingelly oil in a wide kadhai and crackle two sprigs of curry leaves. add the shallots and fry 7 minutes over medium heat until deep golden. pound the ginger and garlic to a paste, add it and fry 2 minutes until the raw edge is gone. add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes until they collapse and the oil shows. stir in the ground masala and fry on low for 8 minutes, scraping constantly, until it is thick, dark and oily at the edges. add 150ml water and salt, bring to a boil and simmer 3 minutes. add the crab pieces and claws, turn them through the masala, cover and cook 8-10 minutes on medium. uncover and cook 4 minutes on high, tossing, until the masala clings to every piece and there is almost no free liquid. fry the last curry leaf sprig in a spoon of oil, scatter it over with the coriander, squeeze on the lemon and serve hot with plenty of napkins.

entries.title: Chettinad Pepper Chicken
entries.snippet: semi-dry milagu kozhi varuval, hot with coarsely cracked black pepper
entries.text: chettinad pepper chicken chettinad semi-dry milagu kozhi varuval, hot with coarsely cracked black pepper gluten-free dairy-free nut-free chicken black pepper fennel seeds (saunf) cumin seeds shallots (small red onions) garlic ginger curry leaves dried red chillies turmeric powder coriander powder sesame oil (gingelly / til) lemon / lime salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) heat the gingelly oil in a kadhai until it shimmers, then add the fennel, cumin and broken red chillies. add two sprigs of curry leaves and stand back — they will crackle hard for 10 seconds. tip in the shallots and fry 6 minutes over medium-high heat until browned at the edges. add the garlic and ginger and fry 90 seconds until fragrant. stir in the coriander powder and cook 30 seconds, just until it darkens. add the marinated chicken and fry on high for 5 minutes, turning, until the pieces are opaque and catching colour. pour in 100ml water, cover and cook 10 minutes on medium until the chicken is done through. uncover, add the remaining 1 tbsp cracked pepper and stir-fry 5-6 minutes on high until the liquid has gone and the masala is a dark clinging coat. fry the last sprig of curry leaves in the residual oil at the side of the pan for 20 seconds until crisp. squeeze over the lemon, scatter the crisp curry leaves and coriander, and serve hot with rice or parotta.

entries.title: Kandarappam
entries.snippet: deep-fried jaggery and mixed-dal fritter from the festival kitchen
entries.text: kandarappam chettinad deep-fried jaggery and mixed-dal fritter from the festival kitchen vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) toor dal (pigeon pea) chana dal urad dal (black gram) moong dal jaggery coconut (fresh or desiccated) dry ginger powder (saunth) green cardamom sesame seeds rice flour salt water neutral oil drain the soaked rice and dals and grind to a slightly coarse batter with about 80ml water, thicker than dosa batter. melt the jaggery with 40ml water over low heat until it dissolves, then strain through a fine sieve into the batter. stir in the chopped coconut, crushed cardamom, dry ginger powder, sesame and salt. cover and rest the batter 1 hour at room temperature; it should be thick enough to drop slowly off a spoon. if it has loosened, beat in the rice flour a spoon at a time until it holds a soft mound. heat the oil in a kadhai to medium — a drop of batter should rise in about 4 seconds. slide in tablespoons of batter, 4 or 5 at a time, and fry 3 minutes until the undersides are deep brown. turn each one and fry a further 2-3 minutes until the edges are crisp and the centre puffed. lift onto a rack rather than paper so the crust stays crisp, and repeat with the rest of the batter. cool 10 minutes before eating — the inside is molten jaggery straight out of the pan.

entries.title: Kuzhi Paniyaram
entries.snippet: savoury batter dumplings with shallot and curry leaf, crisp outside and soft within
entries.text: kuzhi paniyaram chettinad savoury batter dumplings with shallot and curry leaf, crisp outside and soft within vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) urad dal (black gram) fenugreek seeds (methi) shallots (small red onions) green chilli ginger curry leaves coriander leaves (cilantro) mustard seeds chana dal asafoetida (hing) black pepper sesame oil (gingelly / til) salt water grind the urad dal and fenugreek with 120ml water to a light fluffy paste, then grind the rice with 130ml water to a slightly grainy batter. mix the two together by hand with the salt, cover and leave 8-10 hours in a warm place until risen and faintly sour. heat 2 tbsp gingelly oil in a small pan, pop the mustard seeds and fry the chana dal 40 seconds until golden. add the shallots, green chilli and ginger and fry 4 minutes until the shallots are translucent and just colouring. stir in the curry leaves, asafoetida and cracked pepper, cook 20 seconds and take off the heat. fold the tempering and the coriander into the fermented batter; it should be thick, like a dropping cake batter. heat the paniyaram pan on medium and put 1/4 tsp gingelly oil into each well. fill each well three-quarters full with batter, cover and cook 4 minutes until the tops are set and matte and the edges pull away. turn each ball with a skewer or the handle of a spoon and cook uncovered 3 minutes more until browned all round. serve straight from the pan with coconut chutney or a spoon of the day's kuzhambu.

entries.title: Vellai Paniyaram
entries.snippet: pale lacy rice-and-urad fritters, crisp at the rim and soft in the middle
entries.text: vellai paniyaram chettinad pale lacy rice-and-urad fritters, crisp at the rim and soft in the middle vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) urad dal (black gram) rice flour sugar salt water neutral oil coconut oil drain the soaked rice and dal and grind with 150ml water to a very smooth batter, stopping to scrape down twice. beat in the salt, sugar and coconut oil, then rest the batter 30 minutes covered. check the consistency: it should ribbon off the spoon and settle back in about 3 seconds. tighten with rice flour if it is thinner than that. heat the oil in a kadhai to a steady medium — a drop of batter should sink briefly, then rise within 3 seconds without browning. wet a small ladle, pour a ladleful of batter from about 10cm above the oil so it spreads into a disc. fry 2 minutes, spooning hot oil over the top, until the edges frill up and turn lacy. turn once and fry 90 seconds more until the fritter is puffed and set but still pale. lift onto a rack, salt lightly if you like, and fry the rest three or four at a time. serve hot with a thin coconut chutney or, in the chettinad way, alongside a peppery mutton kuzhambu.

entries.title: Ambot Tik
entries.snippet: a sharp coconut-free fish curry that is exactly what its name says, sour and hot
entries.text: ambot tik goan a sharp coconut-free fish curry that is exactly what its name says, sour and hot pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) kashmiri chilli powder dried red chillies tamarind vinegar kokum garlic ginger cumin seeds black pepper turmeric powder coriander powder onion neutral oil salt water grind the chillies, garlic, ginger, cumin, pepper, turmeric and coriander powder with the vinegar and 3 tbsp water to a fine paste. heat the oil and fry the chopped onion over medium heat for 8 minutes, until soft and pale gold. add the masala paste and fry 6-7 minutes until it darkens and the oil beads at the edge of the pan. pour in the tamarind water and the rest of the water, add the kokum and salt, and bring to a simmer. simmer uncovered 10 minutes so the gravy reduces slightly and turns glossy. taste and balance: it should be assertively sour and hot. add a pinch of salt or a splash of vinegar rather than sugar. slide in the fish, shake the pan to settle the pieces, and simmer 7-8 minutes until opaque through. rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Bebinca
entries.snippet: Goa's layered coconut and egg cake, one grilled layer at a time
entries.text: bebinca goan goa's layered coconut and egg cake, one grilled layer at a time vegetarian nut-free coconut milk eggs plain flour (maida) sugar ghee nutmeg green cardamom salt whisk the yolks with the sugar until pale, then beat in the coconut milk, flour, nutmeg, cardamom and salt to a smooth, pourable batter. rest 30 minutes. heat the oven to 180c with the grill element on. brush a deep tin generously with ghee and warm it. pour in a thin ladle of batter — about 5mm — and grill 8-10 minutes until the top is browned and set. brush the baked layer with ghee, pour the next ladle over, and grill again. repeat for at least seven layers. cool completely in the tin, then turn out. slicing warm will tear the layers apart. serve at room temperature in thin wedges.

entries.title: Chicken Cafreal
entries.snippet: chicken marinated green with coriander, chilli and vinegar, then fried dry
entries.text: chicken cafreal goan chicken marinated green with coriander, chilli and vinegar, then fried dry gluten-free dairy-free nut-free chicken coriander leaves (cilantro) green chilli garlic ginger cumin seeds black pepper cloves cinnamon turmeric powder vinegar lemon / lime sugar potato neutral oil salt grind the coriander with stalks, green chillies, garlic, ginger, cumin, pepper, cloves, cinnamon, turmeric, vinegar, lemon juice, sugar and 1 tsp salt to a thick green paste. use no water. rub the paste hard into the slashed chicken, working it into the cuts. cover and refrigerate 4 hours or overnight. heat the oil in a heavy kadhai and lay in the chicken in a single layer, scraping the marinade back into the bowl. fry 4 minutes a side over medium-high heat until the surface is seared and patchy brown. add the reserved marinade and 4 tbsp water, cover, and cook on low for 20 minutes, turning the pieces twice. meanwhile fry the quartered potatoes in a separate pan until gold and cooked through, about 12 minutes. uncover, raise the heat and cook 5-6 minutes more until the sauce has reduced to a thick coating that clings to the chicken. check with a knife at the thickest part of the thigh — the juices should run clear. squeeze over lemon and serve with the potatoes and pav.

entries.title: Goan Dodol
entries.snippet: a dark, dense coconut and palm jaggery fudge stirred until it leaves the pan
entries.text: goan dodol goan a dark, dense coconut and palm jaggery fudge stirred until it leaves the pan vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free coconut milk jaggery rice flour cashews green cardamom salt coconut oil melt the jaggery with 200ml water over low heat, then strain through a fine sieve to remove the grit. whisk the rice flour into 2 cups of the cold coconut milk until smooth, then combine with the rest of the coconut milk, the strained jaggery syrup and the salt in a heavy kadhai. bring to a simmer over medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a flat wooden spoon that reaches the corners. after about 25 minutes it will thicken to the consistency of a thick custard and turn light brown. keep stirring over low heat. at around 50 minutes it darkens to milk chocolate and starts to come away from the sides in sheets. at around 75-85 minutes the oil separates and glistens on the surface and the mass rolls as one lump behind the spoon. stir in the cashews and crushed cardamom and cook 2 minutes more. tip it immediately into the greased tray and press flat with a greased scraper to about 2cm thick. cool completely at room temperature, 4-6 hours, until firm enough to cut into diamonds.

entries.title: Goan Fish Curry
entries.snippet: the everyday coconut and kokum curry that gets eaten with rice twice a day
entries.text: goan fish curry goan the everyday coconut and kokum curry that gets eaten with rice twice a day pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) coconut (fresh or desiccated) kashmiri chilli powder coriander powder cumin seeds turmeric powder black pepper garlic ginger tamarind kokum onion green chilli okra / bhindi coconut oil salt water grind the coconut, kashmiri chillies, coriander powder, cumin, turmeric, pepper, garlic and ginger to a very smooth paste with about 150ml water. heat the coconut oil in a wide pan and soften the sliced onion over medium heat for 5 minutes, until translucent, not browned. pour in the ground masala and cook 4 minutes, stirring, until it darkens a shade and smells toasted rather than raw. add the remaining water, the tamarind extract, kokum, green chillies and salt. bring to a gentle simmer. simmer uncovered 8 minutes, until the surface carries a thin rim of orange oil. slide in the okra, if using, and cook 3 minutes until just tender. lower the fish in a single layer. do not stir — shake the pan instead. cook 6-7 minutes, until the flesh turns opaque and pulls from the bone when nudged. take it off the heat and leave it 10 minutes before serving with par-boiled rice.

entries.title: Goan Sausage Pulao
entries.snippet: smoky vinegary chouriço cooked through rice until every grain is stained red
entries.text: goan sausage pulao goan smoky vinegary chouriço cooked through rice until every grain is stained red gluten-free dairy-free nut-free pork basmati rice onion tomato potato green chilli bay leaf cloves cinnamon black pepper turmeric powder coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime water salt fry the chopped sausage in a dry heavy pot over medium heat for 6-8 minutes, until the fat runs out red and the edges crisp. lift out the sausage with a slotted spoon, leaving the fat behind. in the same fat, fry the bay leaves, cloves and cinnamon for 30 seconds until fragrant. add the sliced onion and cook 8 minutes, until deep gold. stir in the tomato, green chillies, pepper and turmeric and cook 4 minutes, until the tomato collapses. add the potato cubes and the drained rice and turn them through the fat for 2 minutes, until every grain is coated and glossy. return the sausage, pour in the water, taste for salt and bring to a hard boil. cover tightly, drop to the lowest heat and cook 12 minutes without lifting the lid. rest off the heat, still covered, for 10 minutes, then fork through the coriander and serve with lemon.

entries.title: Goan Xacuti
entries.snippet: Chicken in a dark roasted-coconut masala with poppy seeds and star anise
entries.text: goan xacuti goan chicken in a dark roasted-coconut masala with poppy seeds and star anise gluten-free dairy-free chicken coconut (fresh or desiccated) onion dried red chillies coriander powder cumin seeds poppy seeds (khus khus) star anise cinnamon cloves black pepper nutmeg turmeric powder ginger garlic tamarind neutral oil salt dry roast the grated coconut over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until deep brown and nutty, 10-15 minutes. be patient and do not walk away; it turns from brown to burnt in seconds. tip onto a plate to stop the cooking. in the same pan, roast the dried chillies, coriander seeds, cumin, poppy seeds, star anise, cinnamon, cloves and pepper separately until fragrant, about 2 minutes. cool. blend the roasted coconut and spices with the ginger, garlic, turmeric and enough water to make a very smooth, thick paste. take your time here; grittiness will not cook out. heat the oil and fry the sliced onion until well browned, 10 minutes. add the masala paste and cook, stirring, until it darkens and the oil separates, 8-10 minutes. add the chicken and salt and turn it in the masala over high heat until sealed all over. add about 2 cups of hot water, bring to a simmer, cover and cook 25-30 minutes until the chicken is tender. stir in the tamarind pulp and the nutmeg. simmer uncovered 5 minutes to balance the sourness. rest before serving; xacuti is better after an hour.

entries.title: Khatkhate
entries.snippet: the Saraswat temple stew of eight vegetables in coconut, no onion or garlic anywhere
entries.text: khatkhate goan the saraswat temple stew of eight vegetables in coconut, no onion or garlic anywhere vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic toor dal (pigeon pea) pumpkin yam (suran) raw banana / plantain sweet potato drumstick (moringa pod) french beans colocasia (arbi) coconut (fresh or desiccated) dried red chillies coriander powder black pepper tamarind jaggery coconut oil salt water boil the toor dal in 400ml water for 20 minutes, until soft enough to crush against the side of the pot. meanwhile grind the coconut, dried chillies and coriander powder with 150ml water to a coarse-ish paste — a little texture is right here. add the yam, colocasia and raw banana to the dal with the rest of the water and 1 tsp salt. simmer 10 minutes. add the sweet potato and drumstick and simmer 6 minutes. add the pumpkin and french beans and cook 5 minutes, until everything yields to a knife but still holds its shape. stir in the ground coconut paste, the tamarind extract and the jaggery. simmer gently 8 minutes, stirring only occasionally so the pieces stay whole. crush in the pepper, check the salt, and take it off the heat. it should be sweet, sour and mildly hot in that order. trickle over the raw coconut oil just before serving with rice.

entries.title: Patoleo
entries.snippet: steamed rice parcels of coconut and jaggery, made for the feast of the Assumption
entries.text: patoleo goan steamed rice parcels of coconut and jaggery, made for the feast of the assumption vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic rice flour coconut (fresh or desiccated) jaggery green cardamom sesame seeds salt water melt the jaggery with 4 tbsp water over low heat until it dissolves, about 3 minutes, then strain out the grit. return it to the pan with the grated coconut and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring, until the mixture pulls together and leaves the sides of the pan. stir in the crushed cardamom and roasted sesame and set the filling aside to cool completely. bring the water to a boil with the salt, pour it over the rice flour and mix with a spoon, then knead into a soft, smooth dough once cool enough to touch. rest the dough 10 minutes under a damp cloth. spread a thin, even layer of dough over half of each turmeric leaf with wet fingers, about 3mm thick, leaving a clear border. spoon 2 tbsp of the coconut filling along the centre and fold the leaf over to close the parcel. stack the parcels in a steamer, not too tightly, and steam over rolling water for 20-25 minutes. they are done when the leaf has darkened and the rice looks translucent and pulls away cleanly. rest 5 minutes before opening.

entries.title: Pork Vindaloo
entries.snippet: Vinegar-and-garlic pork, descended from Portuguese carne de vinha d'alhos
entries.text: pork vindaloo goan vinegar-and-garlic pork, descended from portuguese carne de vinha d'alhos gluten-free dairy-free nut-free pork dried red chillies vinegar garlic ginger cumin seeds black pepper cinnamon cloves green cardamom turmeric powder jaggery onion neutral oil salt grind the soaked chillies, garlic, ginger and whole spices with the vinegar to a smooth, thick paste. use no water. rub half the paste into the pork with salt and marinate at least 4 hours, ideally overnight refrigerated. fry the onion in oil until soft and golden, then add the remaining masala paste and cook until the oil separates. add the pork with its marinade and turn it over high heat until sealed and coated. add a cup of hot water, cover, and simmer 60 minutes until the pork is tender and the fat has rendered into the gravy. balance with jaggery and salt. rest overnight if you can — vindaloo is markedly better on day two.

entries.title: Prawn Balchao
entries.snippet: a fierce vinegar-and-chilli prawn pickle eaten a spoonful at a time
entries.text: prawn balchao goan a fierce vinegar-and-chilli prawn pickle eaten a spoonful at a time pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free prawns kashmiri chilli powder dried red chillies vinegar garlic ginger cumin seeds black pepper cloves cinnamon turmeric powder onion sugar neutral oil salt grind the soaked chillies, garlic, ginger, cumin, pepper, cloves, cinnamon and turmeric to a thick paste using only the soaking vinegar, no water. toss the prawns with 1/2 tsp salt and a pinch of turmeric and fry them in 2 tbsp of the oil over high heat for 2 minutes, until they just turn pink. lift them out. pour the rest of the oil into the same kadhai and fry the chopped onion over medium heat for 12-15 minutes, until dark gold and jammy. add the ground masala and fry 10 minutes, stirring often, until the oil separates and pools clearly at the edges. stir in the sugar and salt and cook 2 more minutes. return the prawns, stir to coat, and cook 3 minutes on low. take it off the heat and cool completely, uncovered, in the pan. pack into a dry jar, pressing down so the oil covers the surface. leave 2 days before eating.

entries.title: Prawn Rissois
entries.snippet: crisp half-moon pastries with a creamy prawn filling, the standard Goan party snack
entries.text: prawn rissois goan crisp half-moon pastries with a creamy prawn filling, the standard goan party snack pescatarian plain flour (maida) milk water butter prawns onion green chilli garlic black pepper coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime eggs sliced bread neutral oil salt for the filling, cook the onion, garlic and green chilli in 1 tbsp butter over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft and translucent. add the chopped prawns, pepper and salt and cook 3 minutes, until just pink, then stir in 2 tbsp of the flour and 1/2 cup of the milk. cook 3-4 minutes more, stirring, until it thickens into a stiff paste that holds a ridge. finish with lemon and coriander and chill 1 hour. for the dough, bring the water, remaining milk, remaining butter and 1 tsp salt to a rolling boil. tip in the rest of the flour all at once and beat hard with a wooden spoon until it forms a single ball that leaves the pan clean, about 2 minutes. turn it out, and as soon as you can bear the heat, knead 5 minutes until smooth and elastic. cover and rest 15 minutes. roll the warm dough thin, about 2mm, and cut 9cm rounds. place a heaped teaspoon of filling on each round, fold into a half-moon and seal the edge firmly, pressing out any air. dip each in beaten egg, then press into the breadcrumbs to coat evenly. chill 20 minutes. heat the oil to 175c — a crumb dropped in should sizzle and rise at once — and fry in batches of five for 3 minutes, until deep gold. drain on a rack, not paper, and serve hot.

entries.title: Recheado Mackerel
entries.snippet: whole mackerel stuffed with red vinegar masala and shallow-fried crisp
entries.text: recheado mackerel goan whole mackerel stuffed with red vinegar masala and shallow-fried crisp pescatarian dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) kashmiri chilli powder dried red chillies vinegar garlic ginger cumin seeds cloves cinnamon black pepper turmeric powder tamarind sugar rava / sooji (semolina) neutral oil salt lemon / lime grind the soaked chillies, garlic, ginger, cumin, cloves, cinnamon, pepper, turmeric, tamarind, sugar and 1 tsp salt with the vinegar to a thick, smooth paste. slit each mackerel along the belly and, with a small knife, open a second pocket along the backbone from the outside. pack 1.5 tbsp of paste into each fish, inside the belly and into the pocket, and smear a thin film over the skin. rest the stuffed fish 20 minutes on a plate in the fridge. spread the rava on a plate and press each fish into it on both sides, shaking off the loose grains. heat the oil on a flat tawa over medium heat until a grain of rava sizzles on contact. lay in the fish and fry 5-6 minutes without moving it, until the underside is crusted and deep red-brown. turn once with a wide spatula and fry another 4-5 minutes. drain briefly on paper and serve hot with lemon wedges, rice and a plain dal.

entries.title: Sanna
entries.snippet: soft spongy steamed rice cakes, faintly sweet, eaten with sorpotel
entries.text: sanna goan soft spongy steamed rice cakes, faintly sweet, eaten with sorpotel vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic rice (short/medium grain) coconut (fresh or desiccated) sugar eno / fruit salt salt water drain the soaked rice and grind it with the grated coconut, cooked rice and just enough water to a thick, smooth batter — thicker than pancake batter, like idli batter. stir in the sugar, cover loosely, and leave in a warm place for 8-10 hours, or overnight. by morning it should have risen by half, smell yeasty and sweet, and be full of small bubbles. stir in the salt gently, from the edges inwards, keeping as much air in as you can. if the batter never rose, fold in the eno now and steam immediately. grease small steel bowls or idli moulds and fill each two-thirds full. steam over rolling water for 12-15 minutes, with the lid wrapped in a cloth to stop condensation dripping back. test with a skewer at the centre — it should come out clean and the surface should spring back. rest 5 minutes, then run a knife around each and turn them out. serve warm with sorpotel or a pork curry.

entries.title: Sorpotel
entries.snippet: the vinegary pork and liver stew that gets cooked days before a Goan wedding
entries.text: sorpotel goan the vinegary pork and liver stew that gets cooked days before a goan wedding gluten-free dairy-free nut-free pork kashmiri chilli powder dried red chillies vinegar cumin seeds cloves cinnamon black pepper turmeric powder garlic ginger onion green chilli sugar salt water boil the pork and liver together in the water with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp turmeric for 25 minutes, until firm but not falling apart. keep the stock. cool the meat, then cut it into small 1cm dice. it should be knife-cut, never minced. fry the diced pork and liver in 3 tbsp of its own rendered fat over high heat, in batches, until the edges brown, about 5 minutes a batch. grind the soaked chillies, cumin, cloves, cinnamon, pepper, turmeric, garlic and ginger with the remaining vinegar to a fine paste. in the same pot, cook the chopped onion in the fat over medium heat for 10 minutes, until soft and gold. add the ground masala and fry 8-10 minutes until the oil separates and the raw vinegar smell has gone. return the meat, add the reserved stock, green chillies, sugar and salt. simmer uncovered 30 minutes, stirring now and then. stop when the gravy is thick enough to coat the meat and a distinct layer of red fat sits on top. cool completely and refrigerate. reheat and simmer 5 minutes each day for three days before serving with sanna or crusty pav.

entries.title: Tondak
entries.snippet: dried white peas in a roasted coconut and cashew masala, thick and faintly sweet
entries.text: tondak goan dried white peas in a roasted coconut and cashew masala, thick and faintly sweet vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free dried white peas (safed matar) cashews coconut (fresh or desiccated) dried red chillies kashmiri chilli powder coriander powder cumin seeds black pepper cloves cinnamon turmeric powder onion garlic tamarind jaggery coconut oil salt water pressure cook the drained peas with 400ml water and 1/2 tsp salt for 3 whistles, about 12 minutes, until soft but not split. keep the cooking water. dry-roast the grated coconut in a pan over medium heat for 6-8 minutes, stirring constantly, until it turns the colour of weak tea. add the dried chillies, coriander seeds, cumin, pepper, cloves and cinnamon to the pan and roast 1 minute more, until fragrant. grind the roasted coconut and spices with the soaked cashews, turmeric, garlic and 150ml water to a thick, smooth paste. heat the coconut oil and fry the chopped onion 8 minutes, until well browned at the edges. add the ground masala and fry 6 minutes, stirring, until it thickens and the oil shows at the sides. tip in the cooked peas with their water and the remaining water. simmer 12 minutes. stir in the tamarind and jaggery, check the salt, and simmer 5 minutes more until the gravy is thick enough to hold a spoon mark. rest 10 minutes and serve with rice or pao.

entries.title: Basundi
entries.snippet: milk reduced slowly to a thick grainy cream, scented with cardamom and saffron
entries.text: basundi gujarati milk reduced slowly to a thick grainy cream, scented with cardamom and saffron vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic milk sugar saffron green cardamom almonds pistachios nutmeg bring the milk to a boil in a wide heavy pan over medium heat, stirring so it does not stick. lower the heat and simmer, stirring every few minutes and scraping the base each time. as a skin forms at the edges, keep pushing it back into the milk. these layers are what make basundi grainy rather than smooth. crush the saffron into 2 tbsp of the hot milk and set it aside to bloom. continue reducing for 45-55 minutes, until the milk has come down to about half its volume and coats a spoon thickly. add the sugar and cook 8 minutes more; the milk will loosen briefly, then thicken again. stir in the saffron milk, ground cardamom and nutmeg, and take the pan off the heat. cool to room temperature, then chill 3 hours; it thickens noticeably as it cools. serve cold in small bowls with the almonds and pistachios scattered over, or warm alongside puris.

entries.title: Bataka Poha
entries.snippet: flattened rice tossed with potato, peanuts and lemon, ready in twenty minutes
entries.text: bataka poha gujarati flattened rice tossed with potato, peanuts and lemon, ready in twenty minutes vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free poha (flattened rice) potato onion peanuts green chilli curry leaves mustard seeds cumin seeds turmeric powder sugar lemon / lime neutral oil asafoetida (hing) coriander leaves (cilantro) coconut (fresh or desiccated) salt fry the peanuts in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes until they darken and smell toasted, then lift them out and set aside. in the same oil pop the mustard seeds, then add the cumin, curry leaves, green chilli and asafoetida. add the diced potato, cover, and cook on medium-low 8 minutes, shaking the pan, until tender and lightly golden. add the onion and fry 3 minutes until soft and translucent. tip in the seasoned poha and fold it through gently with a flat spatula, lifting rather than stirring. cover and steam on the lowest heat 3 minutes, until the poha is hot, plump and pale yellow throughout. turn off the heat, add the lemon juice and the fried peanuts, and fold once. scatter the coriander and coconut over and serve hot with a wedge of lemon.

entries.title: Bhinda Sambhariya
entries.snippet: whole okra stuffed with a peanut, coconut and sesame masala, cooked gently in a covered pan
