entries.text: bhinda sambhariya gujarati whole okra stuffed with a peanut, coconut and sesame masala, cooked gently in a covered pan vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free no-onion-garlic okra / bhindi peanuts besan (gram flour) sesame seeds coconut (fresh or desiccated) coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) turmeric powder red chilli powder sugar lemon / lime ginger green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil mustard seeds asafoetida (hing) salt top and tail the okra and slit each pod lengthways down one side, stopping short of both ends so it stays whole. mix the ground peanut, roasted besan, sesame, coconut, all the ground spices, sugar, salt, ginger, chilli, coriander leaves and lemon juice into a crumbly stuffing. press the stuffing into each pod with a small spoon or your fingertip, filling but not splitting them. heat the oil in a wide kadhai, pop the mustard seeds and add the asafoetida. lay the stuffed okra in a single layer and let them sit undisturbed 4 minutes to blister on the underside. turn each pod gently with tongs, cover, and cook on low heat 12 minutes. uncover, shake the pan and cook 5 minutes more until the okra is tender, the surfaces are lightly browned and no sliminess remains. scatter over any leftover stuffing, let it toast for a minute, and serve with rotli.

entries.title: Dal Dhokli
entries.snippet: spiced wheat diamonds simmered soft in sweet-sour toor dal, a one-pot supper
entries.text: dal dhokli gujarati spiced wheat diamonds simmered soft in sweet-sour toor dal, a one-pot supper vegetarian toor dal (pigeon pea) atta (wholewheat flour) besan (gram flour) carom seeds (ajwain) turmeric powder red chilli powder neutral oil jaggery tamarind peanuts ghee mustard seeds cumin seeds cinnamon cloves dried red chillies curry leaves asafoetida (hing) ginger green chilli water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt pressure cook the drained dal with the peanuts, 1/2 tsp turmeric and 800ml water for 4 whistles, then let the pressure drop naturally. meanwhile knead the atta, besan, ajwain, remaining turmeric, 1/2 tsp chilli powder, salt and 2 tbsp oil with about 70ml water into a stiff dough. cover and rest 20 minutes. whisk the cooked dal smooth, add the remaining water, tamarind, jaggery, ginger, green chilli, remaining chilli powder and salt, and bring to a simmer. roll the dough very thin, 2mm, and cut into 4cm diamonds. bring the dal to a rolling boil and drop the diamonds in a few at a time, stirring gently between additions. simmer uncovered 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the dhokli are cooked through and the dal has thickened around them. heat the ghee, pop the mustard and cumin seeds with the cinnamon, cloves and dried chilli. add the curry leaves and asafoetida, then pour the tempering over the pot. simmer 3 minutes more, thinning with hot water to a thick soup. scatter the coriander over and serve in bowls with a spoon of ghee and raw chopped onion on the side.

entries.title: Fafda
entries.snippet: crisp-chewy strips of fried gram flour dough, the classic sunday breakfast
entries.text: fafda gujarati crisp-chewy strips of fried gram flour dough, the classic sunday breakfast vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic besan (gram flour) baking soda carom seeds (ajwain) black pepper turmeric powder neutral oil water green chilli salt mix the besan, ajwain, black pepper and turmeric in a wide bowl. rub in the 3 tbsp oil until the mixture holds its shape when squeezed. add the soda-and-salt water gradually and knead 8 minutes into a smooth, firm, elastic dough. cover and rest 20 minutes. pinch off a walnut-sized piece, place it on an oiled surface, and press it away from you with the heel of your palm into a long strip about 12cm by 3cm. lift the strip with a flat scraper and lay it on an oiled tray while you press the rest. heat the frying oil to 175c — a scrap of dough should rise steadily, not violently. slide in 3-4 strips at a time and fry 2-3 minutes, turning once, until pale gold and no longer bubbling hard. drain on a rack, not paper, so both faces stay crisp. fry the slit green chillies for 30 seconds, salt them, and serve alongside with kadhi or papaya sambharo.

entries.title: Gujarati Dal
entries.snippet: thin toor dal balanced sweet with jaggery and sharp with tamarind
entries.text: gujarati dal gujarati thin toor dal balanced sweet with jaggery and sharp with tamarind vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic toor dal (pigeon pea) water turmeric powder jaggery tamarind peanuts tomato ginger green chilli curry leaves ghee mustard seeds cumin seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) cinnamon cloves dried red chillies asafoetida (hing) red chilli powder coriander leaves (cilantro) salt pressure cook the drained dal with the peanuts, turmeric and 700ml water for 4 whistles, then let the pressure drop naturally. whisk the cooked dal smooth and thin it with the remaining water until it pours easily from a ladle. add the tamarind pulp, jaggery, tomato, ginger, green chilli and salt and simmer 12 minutes. taste and adjust — it should read sweet, then sour, then salty, with heat arriving last. heat the ghee in a small pan and pop the mustard seeds. add the cumin, fenugreek, cinnamon, cloves and dried red chilli and let them darken 15 seconds. add the curry leaves, chilli powder and asafoetida off the heat, then pour the whole tempering into the dal. simmer 3 minutes more, scatter the coriander over and serve with rice and a spoon of ghee.

entries.title: Gujarati Kadhi
entries.snippet: thin sweet-sour yogurt and gram flour soup, drunk as much as eaten
entries.text: gujarati kadhi gujarati thin sweet-sour yogurt and gram flour soup, drunk as much as eaten vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic yogurt / dahi besan (gram flour) water jaggery ginger green chilli ghee cumin seeds mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) cloves cinnamon dried red chillies curry leaves asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder coriander leaves (cilantro) salt whisk the besan into the yogurt until completely smooth, then thin it with the water a little at a time. stir in the turmeric, jaggery, ginger, green chilli and salt, and set the pan over medium heat. bring it to a boil stirring constantly in one direction, about 8 minutes. it will foam up as it reaches the boil. drop the heat and simmer 10 minutes, until the raw besan smell is gone and the kadhi coats a spoon thinly. heat the ghee in a small pan and add the mustard seeds; wait for them to pop. add the cumin, fenugreek, cloves, cinnamon and dried red chilli, and let them darken for 15 seconds. add the curry leaves and asafoetida, stand back from the spatter, and pour the tempering straight into the kadhi. simmer 2 minutes more, scatter the coriander over and serve hot with plain rice or khichdi.

entries.title: Gujarati Khichdi
entries.snippet: soft rice and moong dal cooked to a porridge, eaten with kadhi and ghee
entries.text: gujarati khichdi gujarati soft rice and moong dal cooked to a porridge, eaten with kadhi and ghee vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic rice (short/medium grain) moong dal water ghee cumin seeds turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) ginger green chilli black pepper salt heat half the ghee in the pressure cooker and crackle the cumin seeds until they turn a shade darker. add the asafoetida, ginger and green chilli and let them sizzle 10 seconds. tip in the drained rice and dal and stir 2 minutes until every grain is glossed with ghee. add the water, turmeric and salt and stir well, scraping the base. close the cooker and cook for 4 whistles on medium heat, then let the pressure fall on its own. open, whisk briefly and thin with hot water if it has set firm — it should slump off a spoon. crack the black pepper over, pour the remaining ghee on top and serve with kadhi.

entries.title: Handvo
entries.snippet: savoury fermented rice and lentil cake with a crisp sesame crust
entries.text: handvo gujarati savoury fermented rice and lentil cake with a crisp sesame crust vegetarian gluten-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) chana dal toor dal (pigeon pea) urad dal (black gram) fenugreek seeds (methi) yogurt / dahi bottle gourd (lauki) ginger green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder sugar eno / fruit salt neutral oil mustard seeds cumin seeds sesame seeds curry leaves dried red chillies asafoetida (hing) salt coriander leaves (cilantro) grind the soaked, drained rice and dals with the yogurt to a coarse batter, thick enough to drop off the spoon in a lump. cover and leave in a warm place 8-10 hours to ferment. fold in the grated bottle gourd, ginger, chilli, turmeric, chilli powder, sugar, salt and coriander. heat 3 tbsp oil in a heavy 22cm pan, crackle the mustard and cumin seeds, then add the curry leaves, dried chilli and asafoetida. stir most of this tempering into the batter, leaving a spoonful and its oil in the pan. beat in the eno, pour the batter into the pan, level it and scatter the remaining sesame over the top. cover and cook on the lowest heat 25 minutes, until the top is set and a skewer comes out clean. drizzle the remaining oil around the edge, flip the cake or slide it under a hot grill, and cook 10 minutes more until the crust is deep brown and crisp. rest 10 minutes in the pan before cutting into squares.

entries.title: Khaman Dhokla
entries.snippet: Steamed, aerated gram flour squares with a sweet-sour mustard tempering
entries.text: khaman dhokla gujarati steamed, aerated gram flour squares with a sweet-sour mustard tempering vegetarian vegan gluten-free nut-free dairy-free besan (gram flour) rava / sooji (semolina) yogurt / dahi eno / fruit salt ginger green chilli turmeric powder lemon / lime sugar mustard seeds sesame seeds curry leaves asafoetida (hing) coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil salt set a steamer to boil and grease a shallow tin. whisk the besan, rava, yogurt, turmeric, ginger, chilli, salt, 1 tbsp oil and about 3/4 cup water into a smooth, thick-but-pourable batter. rest 10 minutes. stir in the juice of half a lemon. add the eno, whisk briskly for 20 seconds as it foams and visibly lightens, and pour immediately into the tin. steam covered on high for 15-18 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean and the surface springs back. cool 10 minutes, then cut into squares. for the tempering, heat the remaining oil, splutter the mustard seeds, add the sesame, curry leaves, asafoetida and any remaining slit chillies. take the pan off the heat and carefully add 1/3 cup water, the sugar and the remaining lemon juice. return to the heat and simmer just until the sugar dissolves. spoon the warm tempering evenly over the dhokla and leave it 15 minutes to soak in fully. scatter with coriander before serving.

entries.title: Khandvi
entries.snippet: silky gram flour sheets rolled tight and dressed with mustard seeds and coconut
entries.text: khandvi gujarati silky gram flour sheets rolled tight and dressed with mustard seeds and coconut vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic besan (gram flour) buttermilk (chaas) turmeric powder ginger green chilli asafoetida (hing) neutral oil mustard seeds sesame seeds curry leaves coconut (fresh or desiccated) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt whisk the besan, buttermilk, turmeric, ginger, chilli paste, asafoetida and salt to a completely smooth, lump-free batter. pour into a heavy pan and cook over medium heat, stirring without pause with a flat spatula. after 10-12 minutes it will thicken to a glossy paste that pulls away from the sides of the pan. test it: spread a teaspoon on an oiled tray, wait 30 seconds and try to peel it up. if it lifts clean, it is ready; if it smears, cook 2 minutes more and test again. working fast, pour the batter onto the oiled trays and spread it paper-thin with a flat scraper. let it cool 5 minutes until set and no longer tacky, then cut into strips about 6cm wide. roll each strip up tightly from one end and stand the rolls on a serving plate. heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds, add the sesame, slit chillies, curry leaves and a pinch of asafoetida, and pour it over the rolls. scatter the coconut and coriander over and serve at room temperature.

entries.title: Methi Muthiya
entries.snippet: steamed fenugreek dumplings squeezed by hand, then tossed in a sesame tempering
entries.text: methi muthiya gujarati steamed fenugreek dumplings squeezed by hand, then tossed in a sesame tempering vegetarian vegan dairy-free nut-free fenugreek leaves (methi) atta (wholewheat flour) besan (gram flour) jowar (sorghum) flour sesame seeds carom seeds (ajwain) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder sugar ginger green chilli lemon / lime baking soda neutral oil mustard seeds curry leaves asafoetida (hing) coconut (fresh or desiccated) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt mix the flours, sesame, ajwain, ground spices, sugar, salt, ginger, chilli and lemon juice in a bowl. add the squeezed methi and 2 tbsp of the oil and work it into a stiff dough, using the methi water only if needed. work in the baking soda, then divide the dough into four and roll each into a log about 4cm thick, squeezing it in your fist so it keeps the finger marks that give muthiya its name. steam the logs 20 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean and the surface is dry. cool completely, at least 20 minutes, then cut into 2cm slices. heat the remaining oil in a kadhai, pop the mustard seeds, and add the curry leaves and asafoetida. add the slices and pan-fry 6-8 minutes, turning occasionally, until the cut faces are golden and crisp. scatter the coconut and coriander over and serve hot with tea or masala chai.

entries.title: Methi Thepla
entries.snippet: soft fenugreek-flecked flatbreads that travel for days without going stale
entries.text: methi thepla gujarati soft fenugreek-flecked flatbreads that travel for days without going stale vegetarian nut-free no-onion-garlic atta (wholewheat flour) besan (gram flour) fenugreek leaves (methi) yogurt / dahi ginger green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder carom seeds (ajwain) sesame seeds neutral oil ghee salt water mix the atta, besan, chopped methi, all the spices, sesame and salt in a wide bowl. rub in the 2 tbsp oil until the flour looks like damp sand, then add the yogurt, ginger and chilli. bring it together with water added a spoonful at a time into a soft, pliable dough — softer than roti dough. cover and rest the dough 20 minutes. divide into 12 balls and roll each to a thin round about 15cm across, dusting lightly with atta. cook on a hot tawa 40 seconds, until small bubbles rise, then flip. smear ghee on the cooked side, flip again, and press the edges down with a cloth so it puffs and browns in spots. stack the cooked theplas in a cloth-lined box so they steam each other soft.

entries.title: Patra
entries.snippet: colocasia leaves layered with spiced tamarind gram paste, steamed then crisped
entries.text: patra gujarati colocasia leaves layered with spiced tamarind gram paste, steamed then crisped vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic colocasia (arbi) besan (gram flour) tamarind jaggery ginger green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) carom seeds (ajwain) sesame seeds asafoetida (hing) neutral oil mustard seeds coconut (fresh or desiccated) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water whisk the besan with the tamarind pulp, jaggery, ginger, chilli, all the ground spices, ajwain, asafoetida and salt, adding water slowly to a thick spreadable paste. taste the paste. it should be aggressively sweet-sour and salty; the leaves dilute it a great deal. lay a leaf vein-side up, spread a thin even layer of paste over it, and place a second leaf on top pointing the other way. build stacks of three or four leaves, pasting between each. fold the two long sides inward, spread paste on the fold, then roll up tightly from the base into a firm log. steam the logs 30 minutes, until a skewer slides in without resistance and the outside is dull and dry to the touch. cool completely, then cut into 1.5cm slices. heat the oil in a kadhai, pop the mustard seeds with the sesame, and lay the slices in a single layer. shallow-fry 3 minutes a side until the edges are crisp and browned. scatter the coconut and coriander over and serve warm with tea.

entries.title: Sev Tameta nu Shaak
entries.snippet: soupy sweet-sharp tomato curry finished with crisp gram flour sev
entries.text: sev tameta nu shaak gujarati soupy sweet-sharp tomato curry finished with crisp gram flour sev vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free tomato besan (gram flour) onion garlic green chilli neutral oil mustard seeds cumin seeds curry leaves asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder jaggery water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt heat the oil and pop the mustard seeds, then add the cumin, curry leaves and asafoetida. add the onion and garlic and fry 5 minutes until the onion is soft and translucent, not browned. stir in the turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder off the heat for 10 seconds so they bloom without burning. tip in the tomatoes, green chilli and salt and cook 8 minutes, pressing them down, until they collapse and the oil beads at the edges. add the jaggery and the water and simmer 6 minutes into a loose, pourable gravy. taste and balance: it wants to land sweet first, then sour, then hot. ladle into bowls, pile the sev over the top and scatter the coriander. serve at once with rotli or bhakri, while the sev is still crunchy.

entries.title: Shrikhand
entries.snippet: hung yogurt whipped with sugar, saffron and cardamom into a thick tart cream
entries.text: shrikhand gujarati hung yogurt whipped with sugar, saffron and cardamom into a thick tart cream vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic yogurt / dahi sugar saffron milk green cardamom pistachios almonds nutmeg crush the saffron between your fingers into the warm milk and leave it to steep 15 minutes until the milk is deep orange. tip the hung yogurt into a bowl and add the sugar. beat with a whisk for 4-5 minutes until the sugar has fully dissolved and the mixture is glossy and smooth. pass it through a fine sieve, pressing with a spatula, for a properly silken texture. fold in the saffron milk, ground cardamom and nutmeg. taste and adjust the sugar; it should be tart first and sweet second. chill at least 3 hours, until set firm enough to hold a peak. spoon into bowls, scatter the pistachios and almonds over and serve with hot puris.

entries.title: Undhiyu
entries.snippet: Surat's winter casserole of root vegetables and methi dumplings, cooked upside down
entries.text: undhiyu gujarati surat's winter casserole of root vegetables and methi dumplings, cooked upside down vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free yam (suran) sweet potato raw banana / plantain potato eggplant / brinjal cluster beans (guar) dried white peas (safed matar) besan (gram flour) fenugreek leaves (methi) coconut (fresh or desiccated) coriander leaves (cilantro) green chilli ginger sesame seeds peanuts carom seeds (ajwain) asafoetida (hing) jaggery lemon / lime groundnut oil salt blend the coconut, coriander, green chilli, ginger, sesame, peanut, jaggery, lemon and salt to a coarse green masala. make muthiya: knead the besan with chopped methi, a spoon of the masala, ajwain and a little water into a stiff dough; shape small dumplings and shallow fry until golden. set aside. stuff the slit eggplants and any halved potatoes with the green masala. in a heavy pot, heat the oil with asafoetida, then layer the vegetables hardest-first: yam and sweet potato at the bottom, then banana and potato, then beans and peas, stuffed eggplant on top. spoon over the remaining masala and a splash of water, cover tightly and cook on low heat 35-40 minutes. add the muthiya for the last 10 minutes so they soften without dissolving. fold once, very gently, at the end.

entries.title: Babru
entries.snippet: shimla-style fried breads packed with spiced ground urad dal, crisp outside and savoury through
entries.text: babru himachali shimla-style fried breads packed with spiced ground urad dal, crisp outside and savoury through vegetarian vegan dairy-free nut-free atta (wholewheat flour) plain flour (maida) urad dal (black gram) neutral oil mustard oil cumin seeds carom seeds (ajwain) asafoetida (hing) ginger green chilli coriander powder red chilli powder amchur (dry mango powder) fennel seeds (saunf) garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water mix the atta, maida, 1 tsp salt and the mustard oil, then add water gradually to a firm, smooth dough. knead 6 minutes. cover and rest 30 minutes. the dough should press back slowly when poked. grind the drained urad dal with the green chillies and ginger to a coarse, dry paste, using at most 2 tbsp water. heat 2 tbsp of the frying oil in a pan, crackle the cumin, ajwain and asafoetida, then add the dal paste. cook the dal on medium for 8 to 10 minutes, breaking up lumps, until it dries out and comes away from the pan in a single crumbly mass. stir in the coriander powder, chilli powder, amchur, crushed fennel, garam masala, salt and coriander leaves. cook 2 minutes, then cool completely. divide the dough into 10 balls. flatten each in your palm, cup it, put in a heaped tablespoon of cold filling, gather the edges over the top and pinch shut. press flat. roll each stuffed ball gently to about 10cm across, working from the centre out with light pressure. heat the oil to 175c. slide in two babrus at a time and press the centre lightly with a slotted spoon so they puff. fry 2 minutes a side until deep golden and blistered. drain and serve hot with kaddu ka khatta or a tamarind chutney.

entries.title: Bhatt Ki Churkani
entries.snippet: kumaoni black beans roasted in mustard oil and simmered into a dark, smoky, rice-thickened gravy
entries.text: bhatt ki churkani himachali kumaoni black beans roasted in mustard oil and simmered into a dark, smoky, rice-thickened gravy vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free whole urad (sabut urad) rice flour mustard oil garlic ginger green chilli dried red chillies cumin seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat 2 tbsp mustard oil in a heavy pan until it smokes, then cool it 20 seconds. add the drained beans and roast them on medium for 6 to 7 minutes, stirring, until the skins wrinkle and blister. transfer the beans to a pressure cooker with 800ml water and 1 tsp salt. cook for 6 whistles and let the pressure fall naturally. heat the remaining 2 tbsp mustard oil in a kadhai to smoking, then cool briefly. crackle the cumin and fenugreek seeds and the broken red chillies, 20 seconds. add the asafoetida, then the crushed garlic, and fry 1 minute to pale gold. stir in the ginger and green chillies, then the turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder. fry 30 seconds. tip in the cooked beans with all their liquid and bring to a boil. stir the rice flour slurry once more and pour it in slowly while stirring hard. the gravy will thicken visibly within a minute. simmer uncovered on low for 15 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes, until the gravy turns glossy and dark and coats a spoon thickly. check the salt, scatter over the coriander leaves and serve with plain rice and a spoon of raw mustard oil on top if you like it sharp.

entries.title: Chana Madra
entries.snippet: chickpeas simmered slowly in whisked yogurt until the gravy is silky, faintly sour and heavy with whole spice
entries.text: chana madra himachali chickpeas simmered slowly in whisked yogurt until the gravy is silky, faintly sour and heavy with whole spice vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic chickpeas (kabuli chana) yogurt / dahi ghee besan (gram flour) cumin seeds cinnamon black cardamom green cardamom cloves bay leaf asafoetida (hing) coriander powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder garam masala almonds raisins (kishmish) salt water pressure cook the drained chickpeas with 500ml water and 1 tsp salt for 4 whistles, then let the pressure drop by itself. they should crush easily between finger and thumb but still hold their shape. heat the ghee in a heavy kadhai until it thins and shimmers. add the cumin, cinnamon, black cardamom, green cardamom, cloves and bay leaves and let them swell and crackle, about 40 seconds. add the asafoetida, count to five, then take the pan off the heat entirely and let it cool for a full minute. pour in the whisked yogurt, return to the lowest possible flame and stir continuously in one direction for 8 to 10 minutes, until the yogurt loses its raw smell and thickens to the consistency of pouring cream. stir in the coriander powder, fennel powder, dry ginger, turmeric and kashmiri chilli. cook 3 minutes more - the gravy will turn glossy and the ghee will start to bead at the edges. add the drained chickpeas along with 150ml of their cooking water. season with salt. simmer uncovered on low for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the gravy coats the back of a spoon and a clear rim of ghee sits around the edge of the pan. fold in the almonds and raisins and cook 3 minutes so the raisins plump. finish with the garam masala, cover and rest off the heat for 10 minutes before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Kaddu Ka Khatta
entries.snippet: pumpkin cooked down with tamarind, pomegranate seed and jaggery into the sharp sour dish that cuts a dham
entries.text: kaddu ka khatta himachali pumpkin cooked down with tamarind, pomegranate seed and jaggery into the sharp sour dish that cuts a dham vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic pumpkin mustard oil fenugreek seeds (methi) cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) tamarind anardana (dried pomegranate seeds) jaggery turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder dry ginger powder (saunth) garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes faintly and the sharp smell drops away, about 2 minutes. take it off the heat for 20 seconds to cool slightly. add the fenugreek seeds and let them darken to a nut brown, no more than 15 seconds, then the cumin. stir in the asafoetida, then immediately add the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and dry ginger. fry 20 seconds. tip in the pumpkin and toss to coat every piece in the spiced oil. fry on medium for 5 minutes until the edges start to catch. pour in 300ml water, add salt, cover and simmer 12 to 15 minutes until a knife slides into a cube with no resistance. add the tamarind pulp, the ground anardana and the jaggery. stir gently - from here on you want the cubes intact. simmer uncovered 8 to 10 minutes, mashing four or five pieces against the side of the pan, until the gravy thickens to a loose chutney that clings to the pumpkin. finish with garam masala and coriander leaves. serve at room temperature alongside rice and madra.

entries.title: Mash Ki Dal
entries.snippet: whole black urad cooked down thick and buttery over a mustard oil base, the everyday hill dal
entries.text: mash ki dal himachali whole black urad cooked down thick and buttery over a mustard oil base, the everyday hill dal vegetarian gluten-free nut-free whole urad (sabut urad) chana dal mustard oil ghee onion garlic ginger tomato green chilli cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder dry ginger powder (saunth) garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water pressure cook the drained dals with 900ml water, the turmeric and 1 tsp salt for 5 whistles, then 15 minutes on the lowest flame. let the pressure drop naturally. heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes lightly, then cool it 20 seconds off the flame. crackle the cumin, add the asafoetida, then the garlic. fry 40 seconds until it just turns pale gold. add the onion and cook on medium, stirring, for 10 to 12 minutes until it is properly brown at the edges and sweet-smelling. stir in the ginger and green chillies, then the coriander powder, chilli powder and dry ginger. fry 30 seconds. add the tomatoes and cook 6 to 8 minutes, pressing them down, until they break completely and the oil pulls away to the sides. pour the cooked dal into the masala. simmer uncovered 15 to 20 minutes on low, stirring and mashing against the pan, until it thickens enough to hold a furrow behind the spoon. check the salt, sprinkle over the garam masala and take off the heat. stir in the raw ghee and the coriander leaves and cover for 5 minutes before serving with rice or a hot roti.

entries.title: Mittha
entries.snippet: saffron sweet rice studded with raisin, almond and apricot, the dish that closes every dham
entries.text: mittha himachali saffron sweet rice studded with raisin, almond and apricot, the dish that closes every dham vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic basmati rice sugar ghee saffron green cardamom cloves cinnamon raisins (kishmish) almonds dried apricots (khubani) dried coconut (copra) salt water heat 4 tbsp of the ghee in a heavy pot. fry the almonds until pale gold, about 90 seconds, then the raisins until they puff, 20 seconds. lift both out and set aside. into the same ghee add the cardamom, cloves and cinnamon and let them sizzle for 30 seconds until fragrant. add the drained rice and fry gently for 3 minutes, turning with a flat spoon, until every grain is glossy and a few have turned opaque white. pour in 550ml water with the pinch of salt and half the saffron liquid. bring to a hard boil. drop the heat to low, cover and cook 10 minutes until the water is absorbed and the rice is about three-quarters done - still firm at the core. sprinkle the sugar evenly over the surface, add the apricots, and do not stir. cover and cook on the lowest heat 8 minutes - the sugar will melt and be drawn down through the rice. uncover, drizzle over the last tablespoon of ghee and the remaining saffron water, and fold through once with a fork. fold in the fried almonds, raisins and the coconut slivers. cover and rest off the heat 10 minutes. fluff once more with a fork and serve warm, in small portions - it is richer than it looks.

entries.title: Rajma Madra
entries.snippet: red kidney beans in a thick soured-yogurt gravy, the dham version that eats richer than chana madra
entries.text: rajma madra himachali red kidney beans in a thick soured-yogurt gravy, the dham version that eats richer than chana madra vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic rajma (kidney beans) yogurt / dahi ghee besan (gram flour) cumin seeds black cardamom green cardamom cinnamon cloves bay leaf asafoetida (hing) coriander powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder garam masala salt water pressure cook the drained rajma with 700ml fresh water and 1 tsp salt for 6 to 7 whistles, then let the pressure fall naturally. a bean should collapse when pressed, with the skin still intact. heat the ghee in a heavy pan until it shimmers. add cumin, black cardamom, green cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and bay leaves; they will foam and smell sweet within 30 to 40 seconds. add the asafoetida, then pull the pan off the flame and let it cool a full minute. return the pan to the lowest heat and pour in the yogurt, stirring without pause for 8 to 10 minutes until it thickens and the raw sourness cooks off. stir in the coriander, fennel, dry ginger, turmeric and kashmiri chilli. cook 3 minutes until the gravy turns a deep ochre and glossy. tip in the rajma with about 200ml of its cooking liquor and season with salt. crush a small ladleful of the beans against the side of the pan and stir back in - this thickens the gravy without flour. simmer uncovered 25 minutes on low, stirring often, until the ghee separates and rises in a clear rim. sprinkle over the garam masala, cover and rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with steamed rice.

entries.title: Sepu Vadi
entries.snippet: fried urad dal dumplings soaked soft in a spinach and yogurt gravy, the dish that marks a proper kangra dham
entries.text: sepu vadi himachali fried urad dal dumplings soaked soft in a spinach and yogurt gravy, the dish that marks a proper kangra dham vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic urad dal (black gram) spinach yogurt / dahi besan (gram flour) ghee neutral oil cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) green chilli ginger coriander powder turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water grind the drained urad dal to a thick, coarse paste with the green chillies and grated ginger, using no more than 3 tbsp water. beat the paste vigorously for 4 to 5 minutes with salt until it lightens in colour and passes the float test. heat the frying oil to 170c. drop in flat spoonfuls of the batter, four or five at a time, and fry 4 to 5 minutes until deep gold and firm. drain on paper. cut each fried vadi in half through its thickness. this is what lets it drink up the gravy. boil the spinach in 200ml water for 4 minutes, then blend it to a smooth green puree with its liquid. heat the ghee in a kadhai, crackle the cumin, add the asafoetida and take the pan off the heat for a minute to cool. on the lowest flame pour in the yogurt-besan mixture and stir continuously for 8 minutes until it thickens and stops smelling raw. stir in the coriander powder, turmeric, kashmiri chilli, fennel and dry ginger, then the spinach puree and 200ml water. season and simmer 8 minutes. slide in the halved vadis, cover and simmer very gently 10 minutes until they swell and turn spongy but still hold together. finish with garam masala and coriander leaves and rest 5 minutes before serving with rice.

entries.title: Siddu
entries.snippet: steamed wheat buns risen slow and stuffed with crushed walnut and poppy seed, eaten swimming in ghee
entries.text: siddu himachali steamed wheat buns risen slow and stuffed with crushed walnut and poppy seed, eaten swimming in ghee vegetarian atta (wholewheat flour) yogurt / dahi baking soda ghee walnuts poppy seeds (khus khus) mustard oil green chilli ginger coriander leaves (cilantro) carom seeds (ajwain) cumin powder (jeera) red chilli powder black pepper salt water mix the atta, baking soda and 1 tsp salt. work in the yogurt, then the lukewarm water a little at a time, to a soft dough slightly stickier than roti dough. knead 8 minutes. oil the surface, cover with a damp cloth and leave in a warm spot for 3 hours. it should look puffed and feel airy, not doubled like bread. meanwhile mix the crushed walnuts, roasted poppy seeds, mustard oil, green chilli, ginger, coriander leaves, ajwain, cumin powder, chilli powder, black pepper and salt into a damp, crumbly filling. knock the dough back gently and divide into 8 balls. do not knead it hard again. roll each ball into a 12cm disc. put 2 heaped tbsp of filling on one half, fold over into a half moon and press the curved edge firmly, then pleat it shut with your fingers. rest the shaped siddus, covered, for 15 minutes while the steamer comes up to a rolling boil. grease the steamer plate, arrange the siddus with 2cm between them and steam on high for 18 to 20 minutes. test with a skewer through the thickest part: it should come out clean and dry. give them 3 more minutes if not. take them out, split the tops slightly and pour a tablespoon of melted ghee over each. serve hot with mash dal or a chutney.

entries.title: Tudkiya Bhath
entries.snippet: chamba pahari rice cooked through with chana dal, potato and yogurt until every grain carries the masala
entries.text: tudkiya bhath himachali chamba pahari rice cooked through with chana dal, potato and yogurt until every grain carries the masala vegetarian gluten-free nut-free basmati rice chana dal potato yogurt / dahi ghee mustard oil onion garlic ginger tomato green chilli bay leaf black cardamom cinnamon cloves cumin seeds turmeric powder coriander powder kashmiri chilli powder garam masala mint coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat the ghee and mustard oil together in a heavy pot until shimmering. add the bay leaves, black cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and cumin and let them crackle for 30 seconds. add the sliced onion and fry on medium-high for 10 minutes until brown at the edges and shrunken to a third of its volume. stir in the garlic, ginger and green chillies and fry 1 minute until the raw smell goes. add the turmeric, coriander powder and kashmiri chilli, then the tomato. cook 5 minutes until the tomato collapses and oil beads at the edge. take the pot off the heat for 30 seconds, then pour in the whisked yogurt on low and stir constantly for 4 minutes until it thickens and stops looking curdled. add the drained chana dal and potato cubes with 150ml water. cover and simmer 10 minutes - the dal should be half done, still with a bite. fold in the drained rice as gently as you can and fry 2 minutes so each grain is coated. pour in 450ml hot water, add salt generously and the mint, and bring to a hard boil. taste the water - it should be a shade saltier than you want the finished rice. cover tight, drop to the lowest flame and cook 12 minutes without lifting the lid. rest off the heat 10 minutes, then fork through with the garam masala and coriander leaves. serve with plain yogurt.

entries.title: Bagara Baingan
entries.snippet: small aubergines stewed whole in a sesame-peanut gravy sharp with tamarind
entries.text: bagara baingan hyderabadi small aubergines stewed whole in a sesame-peanut gravy sharp with tamarind vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free eggplant / brinjal peanuts sesame seeds dried coconut (copra) poppy seeds (khus khus) onion tamarind ginger garlic green chilli curry leaves cumin seeds mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) neutral oil water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) dry-roast the peanuts 5 minutes until blistered, then rub off the skins. roast the sesame, coconut and poppy seeds separately, each for about a minute, and cool everything. grind the roasted lot to a smooth paste with 120ml water. heat half the oil in a kadhai and fry the drained aubergines over medium heat for 6-7 minutes, turning, until the skins are blistered and the flesh has softened. lift out. in the same oil fry the sliced onion until deep golden, about 10 minutes, then cool and grind to a paste. add the remaining oil, crackle the mustard, cumin and fenugreek, then add the curry leaves and green chillies. stir in the ginger and garlic pastes, cook 1 minute, then add the onion paste with the turmeric, chilli, coriander and cumin powders. fry 3 minutes. add the ground nut-and-seed paste and cook on medium-low for 8 minutes until it thickens, darkens by a shade and oil beads at the edges. pour in the tamarind water and the rest of the water, season with salt and simmer 8 minutes until the gravy coats a spoon. lower the aubergines in, spoon gravy over them, cover and cook on low for 10 minutes until a knife slides through with no resistance. rest off the heat for 10 minutes and finish with coriander leaves. serve with bagara rice.

entries.title: Bagara Khana
entries.snippet: everyday whole-spice rice, the plain partner to salan and dalcha
entries.text: bagara khana hyderabadi everyday whole-spice rice, the plain partner to salan and dalcha vegetarian gluten-free nut-free basmati rice ghee onion ginger garlic green chilli cumin seeds bay leaf cinnamon cloves green cardamom black cardamom star anise stone flower (dagad phool) curry leaves mint water salt heat the ghee in a heavy pot and add the cumin, bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, black cardamom, star anise and stone flower. let them sizzle 30 seconds until fragrant. add the curry leaves and sliced onion and fry 7-8 minutes until light golden and just beginning to crisp at the edges. stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and the slit green chillies and cook 1 minute. add the drained rice and turn it gently through the ghee for 2 minutes until every grain is glossy. pour in the water, add the salt and the mint, and bring to a full rolling boil. boil uncovered until the water level drops to the surface of the rice and craters appear, about 5 minutes. cover tightly, drop the heat to the lowest setting and cook 10 minutes without lifting the lid. rest off the heat, still covered, for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork from the edges inwards and serve.

entries.title: Dalcha
entries.snippet: mutton and chana dal simmered with bottle gourd and a firm sour edge
entries.text: dalcha hyderabadi mutton and chana dal simmered with bottle gourd and a firm sour edge gluten-free dairy-free nut-free mutton / lamb chana dal bottle gourd (lauki) onion tomato tamarind ginger garlic green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder garam masala curry leaves cumin seeds mustard seeds dried red chillies neutral oil water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) heat 2 tbsp oil in the pressure cooker and brown the sliced onion for 8 minutes until golden at the edges. add the ginger and garlic pastes and fry 1 minute, then the mutton. sear on high for 5 minutes until the pieces lose their raw pink. stir in the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt, add the tomatoes, and cook 5 minutes until the tomatoes break down. add the drained chana dal and 1 litre of water. pressure cook 4 whistles, about 20 minutes, then let the pressure drop naturally. open, add the bottle gourd and the remaining water, and simmer uncovered 12 minutes until the gourd is translucent and yields to a spoon. pour in the tamarind water and the garam masala. simmer 10 minutes more, mashing some of the dal against the side of the pot to thicken it. taste for salt and sour; the balance should make you sit up. adjust with a little more tamarind water or a splash of plain water. for the tempering, heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in a small pan and crackle the mustard and cumin seeds, then add the dried red chillies and curry leaves and let them spit for 10 seconds. pour the tempering over the dalcha, stir once, and scatter with coriander leaves. rest 5 minutes before serving with bagara rice.

entries.title: Double ka Meetha
entries.snippet: fried bread soaked in saffron milk and cardamom syrup, the wedding-feast pudding
entries.text: double ka meetha hyderabadi fried bread soaked in saffron milk and cardamom syrup, the wedding-feast pudding vegetarian sliced bread ghee milk sugar water khoya / mawa condensed milk green cardamom saffron almonds cashews pistachios raisins (kishmish) boil the milk in a heavy pan and simmer on low for 20 minutes, stirring often, until reduced to about 450ml and noticeably thickened. stir the khoya, or the condensed milk, into the reduced milk along with half the saffron milk. take off the heat. in a separate pan, dissolve the sugar in the water and boil 5 minutes to a thin one-string syrup, then add the crushed cardamom and the rest of the saffron milk. heat the ghee in a kadhai and fry the nuts and raisins briefly until golden. remove and set aside. fry the bread triangles in the same ghee over medium heat, a few at a time, for about 2 minutes a side until evenly deep golden and crisp right through. drain the fried bread on a rack for a minute so the surface ghee runs off. dip each piece into the warm syrup for 5 seconds only, then arrange in a single overlapping layer in a serving dish. pour the warm thickened milk evenly over the bread and leave it to soak for 15 minutes. scatter the fried nuts and raisins over the top and serve warm or at room temperature.

entries.title: Haleem
entries.snippet: Wheat, lentils and mutton pounded together for hours into a smooth, savoury porridge
entries.text: haleem hyderabadi wheat, lentils and mutton pounded together for hours into a smooth, savoury porridge nut-free dalia (broken wheat) mutton / lamb chana dal masoor dal (red lentil) moong dal urad dal (black gram) onion ginger garlic red chilli powder turmeric powder garam masala mint lemon / lime ghee salt pressure cook the soaked dalia and the mixed dals with turmeric and plenty of water until collapsing, about 5 whistles. separately, cook the mutton with ginger, garlic, chilli powder, half the birista and salt until it falls off the bone. reserve the stock. pick the meat off the bones and shred it finely; discard the bones but keep every drop of stock. combine meat, grain and stock in a wide heavy pot. now beat and mash over low heat for 45-60 minutes, adding ghee in stages. when it pulls away from the sides of the pot in a single mass, stir in garam masala and mint. serve topped with birista, fried mint, ginger julienne and a lot of lemon.

entries.title: Hyderabadi Chicken 65
entries.snippet: twice-fried chilli chicken finished in a spitting curry-leaf and yogurt tempering
entries.text: hyderabadi chicken 65 hyderabadi twice-fried chilli chicken finished in a spitting curry-leaf and yogurt tempering gluten-free nut-free chicken yogurt / dahi ginger garlic kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder rice flour besan (gram flour) eggs garam masala black pepper lemon / lime curry leaves green chilli neutral oil salt coriander leaves (cilantro) mix the chicken with the 4 tbsp yogurt, ginger and garlic pastes, kashmiri chilli, chilli powder, garam masala, black pepper, lemon juice and salt. refrigerate at least 2 hours. half an hour before cooking, work the rice flour, besan and beaten egg into the marinade. it should coat each piece in a thin paste, not a batter. heat the frying oil in a kadhai to 170c. a cube of chicken should sizzle steadily and rise within 3 seconds. fry in three batches, 4-5 minutes each, until pale gold and just cooked through. drain on a rack, not paper. raise the oil to 190c and return all the chicken for a second fry of 1-2 minutes until deep red-gold and crisp at the edges. drain. pour off the frying oil, leaving 2 tbsp in the pan. drop in the curry leaves and slit green chillies and let them crackle for 20 seconds. whisk the remaining 3 tbsp yogurt smooth, take the pan off the heat and stir it in. return the pan to a low flame, add the fried chicken and toss for 1 minute until every piece is coated and the yogurt has almost dried onto it. finish with coriander leaves and serve hot with raw onion rings and lemon.

entries.title: Hyderabadi Dum Biryani
entries.snippet: Kachchi biryani: raw marinated mutton layered under rice and sealed from the start
entries.text: hyderabadi dum biryani hyderabadi kachchi biryani: raw marinated mutton layered under rice and sealed from the start gluten-free mutton / lamb basmati rice yogurt / dahi onion ginger garlic red chilli powder turmeric powder garam masala mint coriander leaves (cilantro) saffron lemon / lime green cardamom cinnamon cloves bay leaf ghee atta (wholewheat flour) salt marinate the mutton with yogurt, ginger, garlic, chilli, turmeric, garam masala, half the birista, half the herbs, lemon juice and salt. refrigerate 6 hours or overnight. bring the marinated meat to room temperature and spread it in a heavy pot with 3 tbsp ghee. boil the rice in well-salted water with the whole spices until 70% done, then drain immediately. layer the rice over the raw meat. top with the remaining birista, herbs, saffron milk and ghee. seal with a dough rope or tight foil. cook on high for 5 minutes to build steam, then on the lowest heat for 45 minutes. rest 15 minutes before opening. serve with mirchi ka salan and dahi chutney.

entries.title: Hyderabadi Kheema
entries.snippet: minced mutton with peas, dry and heavily spiced, the weeknight standby
entries.text: hyderabadi kheema hyderabadi minced mutton with peas, dry and heavily spiced, the weeknight standby gluten-free dairy-free nut-free mutton / lamb peas potato onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala cumin seeds mint coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime neutral oil water salt heat the oil in a kadhai and crackle the cumin seeds for 15 seconds. add the chopped onion and fry over medium heat for 10 minutes until golden brown and shrunk to a third of its volume. stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and the green chillies and cook 1 minute until the raw smell lifts. add the mince and break it apart with the back of a spoon. fry on high for 6-7 minutes until it is uniformly brown with no clumps. add the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder and salt and fry 2 minutes. add the chopped tomatoes and cook 6-7 minutes until they melt down and oil beads at the edges of the pan. pour in the water, add the diced potato if using, cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes. add the peas, cover and cook 8 minutes more until the mince is tender and the liquid has almost gone. uncover and fry on medium for 4 minutes, stirring, until the kheema is dry and glistening rather than saucy. stir in the garam masala, mint, coriander and lemon juice and rest 5 minutes before serving with roti or pav.

entries.title: Khatti Dal
entries.snippet: everyday toor dal made unapologetically sour with tamarind
entries.text: khatti dal hyderabadi everyday toor dal made unapologetically sour with tamarind vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free toor dal (pigeon pea) tamarind tomato green chilli onion garlic turmeric powder red chilli powder cumin seeds mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) dried red chillies curry leaves asafoetida (hing) neutral oil water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) pressure cook the dal with the turmeric, chopped tomato, green chillies and 700ml water for 4 whistles, about 12 minutes. let the pressure fall on its own, then whisk the dal hard for 30 seconds until it is smooth and creamy with no whole lentils left. return the pan to a low flame, add the remaining water and salt, and bring to a gentle simmer. stir in the tamarind water and simmer 8 minutes, until the raw sour smell has cooked off and the dal has thickened slightly. heat the oil in a small pan for the tempering. crackle the mustard seeds, then the cumin and fenugreek. add the crushed garlic and fry until it turns golden, about 1 minute, then the dried red chillies, curry leaves and asafoetida. it will spit hard. if using onion, add it to the tempering and fry 3 minutes until soft and translucent. pour the tempering into the dal, cover immediately for a minute to trap the aroma, then stir through. finish with coriander leaves and serve with plain rice and a wedge of lime.

entries.title: Lukhmi
entries.snippet: square flaky pastries filled with spiced mutton mince, the classic wedding starter
entries.text: lukhmi hyderabadi square flaky pastries filled with spiced mutton mince, the classic wedding starter nut-free plain flour (maida) ghee water mutton / lamb onion ginger garlic green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder garam masala black pepper lemon / lime mint coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil salt rub the melted ghee into the maida with your fingertips for 3 minutes until the flour holds its shape when squeezed in a fist. add the salt and cold water a little at a time and bring together into a firm, tight dough — firmer than a chapati dough. knead 5 minutes, cover and rest 30 minutes. for the filling, heat 2 tbsp oil and fry the chopped onion for 8 minutes until golden. add the ginger and garlic pastes and green chillies, cook 1 minute, then the mince. break it up with the back of a spoon and fry on high for 5 minutes until it loses its pink. add the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt and cook on medium for 12 minutes, stirring, until the mince is dry and the fat has separated out. stir in the garam masala, black pepper, lemon juice, mint and coriander. spread on a plate and cool completely. divide the dough into 12. roll each into a 12cm square about 2mm thick, keeping the rest covered. put 1.5 tbsp of filling on one half of each square, brush the edges with water, fold into a rectangle and press the edges firmly, then crimp with a fork. heat the frying oil to 160c. it should be moderate, not fierce: a scrap of dough should rise slowly over 4-5 seconds. fry 4 at a time for 6-7 minutes, turning once, until pale biscuit-gold and blistered. drain on a rack. serve hot with sliced onion and lemon.

entries.title: Marag
entries.snippet: thin white mutton soup enriched with cashew and yogurt, drunk before a biryani
entries.text: marag hyderabadi thin white mutton soup enriched with cashew and yogurt, drunk before a biryani gluten-free mutton / lamb yogurt / dahi cashews almonds poppy seeds (khus khus) onion ginger garlic green chilli black pepper green cardamom cinnamon cloves bay leaf mace (javitri) mint coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime ghee cream water salt heat the ghee in a pressure cooker and add the cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaf and mace. let them puff for 30 seconds. add the sliced onion and cook 8 minutes until soft and pale gold — stop before it browns, or the broth loses its whiteness. stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and the slit green chillies and cook 1 minute. add the mutton and sear on high for 5 minutes until the outside is sealed and no pink shows. take the pot off the heat, wait a minute, then fold in the whisked yogurt in three additions, stirring continuously. return to a low flame and cook 5 minutes until the yogurt tightens around the meat and no longer smells raw. add the water, salt and half the mint. pressure cook for 5 whistles, about 25 minutes, and let the pressure fall on its own. open, and stir in the ground cashew and almond paste. simmer uncovered 12 minutes until the broth thickens just enough to coat a spoon. add the crushed black pepper and the cream, if using, and simmer 3 minutes more. marag should stay drinkable, not stew-thick; loosen with hot water if needed. finish with the remaining mint and the coriander leaves, and serve in cups with lemon wedges to squeeze in.

entries.title: Mirchi ka Salan
entries.snippet: long green chillies in a thick peanut, sesame and tamarind gravy
entries.text: mirchi ka salan hyderabadi long green chillies in a thick peanut, sesame and tamarind gravy vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free green chilli peanuts sesame seeds dried coconut (copra) tamarind onion ginger garlic cumin seeds mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) nigella seeds (kalonji) curry leaves turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder jaggery neutral oil water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) dry-roast the peanuts in a kadhai over medium heat for 5 minutes until the skins blister and loosen, then rub off the skins in a cloth. roast the sesame in the same pan for 1 minute until it pops, then the dried coconut for 1 minute until it smells nutty and turns pale gold. cool completely. grind the peanuts, sesame and coconut with 150ml water to a fine, smooth paste. set aside. heat 3 tbsp of the oil and fry the slit chillies for 2-3 minutes, turning, until the skins blister and go khaki. lift them out and reserve. in the same oil, fry the chopped onion until soft and light brown, about 8 minutes, then cool and grind to a paste. add the rest of the oil to the pan and crackle the cumin, mustard, fenugreek and nigella, then throw in the curry leaves. add the ginger and garlic pastes and fry 1 minute until the raw smell goes, then the onion paste, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder. cook 3 minutes. stir in the ground peanut-sesame paste and fry on medium-low for 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until the mixture darkens and oil rises around the edges. pour in the tamarind water and the remaining water, add salt and the jaggery, and simmer uncovered 12 minutes until glossy and the thickness of pouring cream. slide the fried chillies back in, cover and simmer 5 minutes more, then rest off the heat 10 minutes and scatter with coriander leaves.

entries.title: Murgh do Pyaza
entries.snippet: chicken cooked with onions twice over, once browned to a paste and once in chunks
entries.text: murgh do pyaza hyderabadi chicken cooked with onions twice over, once browned to a paste and once in chunks gluten-free nut-free chicken onion yogurt / dahi ginger garlic green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala black pepper cinnamon cloves green cardamom bay leaf neutral oil mint coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime salt water heat 3 tbsp oil and fry the sliced onions over medium heat for 12-14 minutes until evenly deep brown. lift out half and reserve for the finish. cool the remaining browned onions and grind to a paste with a splash of water. in the same pan, add the whole spices — cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, bay leaf — and let them puff for 30 seconds. add the remaining ginger and garlic pastes and cook 1 minute until the raw edge disappears. add the marinated chicken and sear on high for 6 minutes, turning, until the yogurt has tightened around the pieces and the base looks dry. stir in the browned onion paste, chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder. fry on medium for 6-8 minutes until oil separates at the sides. pour in the water, add the green chillies, cover and simmer 15 minutes until the chicken is tender and pulling from the bone. heat the last 2 tbsp oil in a separate pan and sear the onion petals on high for 3 minutes until charred at the edges but still crunchy inside. fold the seared petals, the reserved browned onions, garam masala and black pepper into the curry and cook uncovered 3 minutes to thicken. take off the heat, stir in the lemon juice, mint and coriander, and rest 5 minutes before serving with roti.

entries.title: Qubani ka Meetha
entries.snippet: Dried apricots stewed to a glossy compote, served with cream and blanched kernels
entries.text: qubani ka meetha hyderabadi dried apricots stewed to a glossy compote, served with cream and blanched kernels vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free dried apricots (khubani) sugar green cardamom lemon / lime cream almonds water soak the apricots in water overnight until plump. keep the soaking water. pit them, reserving the stones. crack the stones and blanch the kernels; the skins slip off. simmer the fruit in its soaking water with the sugar and cardamom over low heat, 30-40 minutes, until it collapses into a thick glossy compote. sharpen with lemon if the apricots were very sweet. cool. serve at room temperature or chilled, topped with cream and the blanched kernels.

entries.title: Sheer Khurma
entries.snippet: eid morning milk pudding heavy with dates, roasted vermicelli and nuts
entries.text: sheer khurma hyderabadi eid morning milk pudding heavy with dates, roasted vermicelli and nuts vegetarian milk vermicelli (semiya) dates dried apricots (khubani) sugar ghee almonds pistachios cashews raisins (kishmish) khoya / mawa green cardamom saffron rose water melt the ghee in a heavy pan and fry the almonds, pistachios and cashews for 2 minutes until golden. lift them out with a slotted spoon. add the raisins to the same ghee and fry 20 seconds until they swell and turn glossy, then remove. add the broken vermicelli to the remaining ghee and roast on low for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly, until evenly reddish-brown and fragrant. pour in the milk and bring to a gentle boil, stirring to keep the vermicelli from clumping on the base. simmer on low for 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes and scraping the bottom, until the milk has reduced by about a quarter and coats the spoon. add the sugar and stir until fully dissolved, about 2 minutes. stir in the soaked dates with their milk, the apricots and the grated khoya. simmer 5 minutes until the khoya melts in with no lumps. add the saffron milk and crushed cardamom and cook 2 minutes more; the pudding should be pourable, a little looser than you want it. take off the heat, stir in the rose water, and fold through most of the fried nuts and raisins. rest 10 minutes and serve warm in small bowls, scattered with the remaining nuts. it is equally good chilled.

entries.title: Tala Hua Gosht
entries.snippet: mutton boiled tender then fried dry with black pepper until the masala clings
entries.text: tala hua gosht hyderabadi mutton boiled tender then fried dry with black pepper until the masala clings gluten-free dairy-free nut-free mutton / lamb onion ginger garlic green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala black pepper curry leaves cinnamon cloves green cardamom lemon / lime neutral oil water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) pressure cook the marinated mutton with 1 sliced onion, the whole spices and 400ml water for 5 whistles, about 25 minutes. let the pressure fall naturally, then check: the meat should give completely to a fork. if not, cook 5 minutes more. strain, keeping the stock. boil the stock down separately to about 100ml of concentrated liquid. heat the oil in a wide kadhai and fry the remaining sliced onions for 10 minutes until deep golden brown. add the green chillies and curry leaves and let them crackle for 20 seconds. add the coriander powder and cumin powder and fry 30 seconds, then tip in the drained mutton pieces. fry on medium-high for 12-15 minutes, turning the pieces every couple of minutes, until they are browned on all sides and the masala has dried onto them. pour in the reduced stock a spoon at a time, letting each addition dry off before adding the next, until the pan is dry and glossy. add the crushed black pepper and garam masala and toss for 2 minutes off the direct heat. finish with lemon juice and coriander leaves and serve with roti or bagara khana.

entries.title: Tomato Kut
entries.snippet: thick sour-hot tomato gravy thickened with gram flour and eggs poached in it
entries.text: tomato kut hyderabadi thick sour-hot tomato gravy thickened with gram flour and eggs poached in it vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free tomato besan (gram flour) eggs tamarind garlic green chilli curry leaves dried red chillies cumin seeds mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder asafoetida (hing) neutral oil water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) simmer the tomatoes with 350ml water and the turmeric for 15 minutes until completely collapsed and pulpy. cool slightly, blend smooth, then push through a sieve to leave the skins and seeds behind. heat 3 tbsp oil in a heavy pan, crackle the mustard, cumin and fenugreek, then add the curry leaves, dried red chillies and green chillies. add the crushed garlic and fry 1 minute until it smells sweet and turns pale gold, then take the pan off the heat and stir in the asafoetida. return to the heat, add the chilli powder and coriander powder, and fry 20 seconds before pouring in the sieved tomato. whisk the standing besan slurry once more and pour it in slowly, stirring constantly. simmer 12 minutes until the gravy is thick, glossy and no longer tastes of raw flour. add the tamarind water and salt and simmer 5 minutes more; it should be thick enough to hold a channel behind the spoon. crack the eggs one at a time onto the surface, spacing them apart. cover and poach on low for 6 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still soft. heat the last 2 tbsp oil, sizzle a few extra curry leaves in it, and pour it over the top. scatter with coriander leaves and serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Aab Gosht
entries.snippet: mutton chops poached in fennel-scented milk, pale and delicate
entries.text: aab gosht kashmiri mutton chops poached in fennel-scented milk, pale and delicate gluten-free nut-free mutton / lamb milk ghee garlic fennel seeds (saunf) fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) green cardamom black cardamom cloves cinnamon bay leaf white pepper water salt bring the chops, water, garlic, bay leaf, both cardamoms, cloves, cinnamon, the muslin bag of fennel seeds and 1 tsp salt to a boil, then skim off the foam. simmer covered 45 minutes, until the meat is tender and pulling from the bone, then uncover and boil the liquid down to about 150ml. remove the muslin bag and squeeze it out into the pan. add the milk in three additions, letting each come back to a bare simmer before the next goes in. stir in the fennel powder, dry ginger and white pepper. simmer uncovered on low for 25 minutes, stirring the base every few minutes with a flat spoon, until the gravy thinly coats the back of it. heat the ghee separately until it is nut-brown and pour it over the pan, giving it one stir. check the salt, rest 10 minutes off the heat and serve with plain rice or with a girda.

entries.title: Chaman Qaliya
entries.snippet: fried paneer in a thin turmeric-yellow gravy, mild and milky
entries.text: chaman qaliya kashmiri fried paneer in a thin turmeric-yellow gravy, mild and milky vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic paneer mustard oil milk water turmeric powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) asafoetida (hing) green cardamom cloves cinnamon bay leaf black pepper ghee salt heat the mustard oil until it just smokes, then take it off the flame for 30 seconds to settle. fry the paneer in batches over medium heat, 2 minutes a side, to a pale gold — no darker. slip each fried piece into the warm salted water and leave it there while you make the gravy. pour off all but 3 tbsp of the oil, add the hing, bay leaf, cloves, cinnamon and cardamom and let them crackle for 20 seconds. off the heat, stir in the turmeric, fennel powder and dry ginger. add the water and 1 tsp salt, bring to a boil and let it bubble 5 minutes so the spices lose their raw edge. lower the heat, pour in the milk and let it come back to a bare simmer. drain the paneer and slide it in. simmer 8 minutes, until the gravy is the thickness of pouring cream and pale yellow. finish with the black pepper and the spoon of ghee, and serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Choek Wangun
entries.snippet: fried aubergine in a sharp tamarind gravy, sour before it is hot
entries.text: choek wangun kashmiri fried aubergine in a sharp tamarind gravy, sour before it is hot vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic eggplant / brinjal mustard oil tamarind kashmiri chilli powder turmeric powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) asafoetida (hing) cumin seeds jaggery water salt heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then drop the flame to medium. fry the aubergine quarters in batches, 4 minutes a side, until the skin is blistered and the flesh is collapsing. lift out onto paper. pour off all but 3 tbsp of the oil, add the cumin seeds and let them crackle for 15 seconds. add the hing, wait 10 seconds for it to foam, then take the pan off the heat. stir in the chilli powder, turmeric, fennel powder and dry ginger off the flame for 20 seconds. return to low heat, add the water, tamarind pulp, jaggery and 1 tsp salt, and simmer 6 minutes until the gravy darkens and thickens slightly. slide the fried aubergine back in and simmer uncovered 6 minutes, spooning gravy over rather than stirring. rest 10 minutes off the heat — it is better warm than hot — and serve with rice.

entries.title: Gushtaba
entries.snippet: pounded mutton meatballs poached in a white yogurt gravy, the closing course of wazwan
entries.text: gushtaba kashmiri pounded mutton meatballs poached in a white yogurt gravy, the closing course of wazwan gluten-free nut-free mutton / lamb shallots (small red onions) yogurt / dahi ghee fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) green cardamom black cardamom cloves cinnamon black pepper mint baking soda milk water salt work the mince with 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp of the fennel powder, 1/2 tsp dry ginger, the ground green cardamom, black pepper, baking soda and 1 tsp salt for a full 10 minutes, until it turns pale, tacky and springy. chill the mix 20 minutes, then wet your palms and roll 8 balls the size of a small orange, smoothing away every crack. heat the remaining ghee in a wide pan and cook the shallot on low for 6 minutes until soft and translucent. add the black cardamom, cloves and cinnamon, then the remaining fennel powder and dry ginger, and stir for 30 seconds. off the heat, whisk in the yogurt and the water, then return to a low flame and stir constantly until it reaches a bare simmer, about 8 minutes. slide the meatballs in one at a time. do not stir for the first 10 minutes — swirl the pan by its handle instead. simmer uncovered on low for 40 minutes, spooning gravy over the balls now and then, until they are firm and the gravy is the thickness of single cream. stir in the milk and crushed mint, season, and give it 5 minutes more. rest 10 minutes off the heat and serve one gushtaba per person with plain rice.

entries.title: Haak
entries.snippet: kashmiri greens boiled whole in mustard oil, chilli and hing, served in their own broth
entries.text: haak kashmiri kashmiri greens boiled whole in mustard oil, chilli and hing, served in their own broth vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic mustard greens (sarson) mustard oil green chilli asafoetida (hing) water dry ginger powder (saunth) baking soda salt heat the mustard oil in a wide pan until it just begins to smoke, then take it off the heat for 20 seconds. add the hing and the slit chillies and let them sizzle for 15 seconds. pour in the water, add the salt and dry ginger, and bring to a hard boil. push the leaves in a handful at a time, letting each batch wilt before the next goes in, about 2 minutes in all. boil uncovered on high for 12 minutes, stirring twice, until the leaves are tender but still hold their shape. stir in the baking soda if using, and taste — the broth should be well salted, since it is eaten with rice. serve immediately in a deep bowl with plenty of its broth, alongside plain rice.

entries.title: Kashmiri Dum Aloo
entries.snippet: Fried baby potatoes finished in a yogurt gravy with fennel and dry ginger, no onion or garlic
entries.text: kashmiri dum aloo kashmiri fried baby potatoes finished in a yogurt gravy with fennel and dry ginger, no onion or garlic vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic potato yogurt / dahi kashmiri chilli powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) green cardamom black cardamom cinnamon cloves asafoetida (hing) ghee neutral oil salt fry the pricked potatoes in hot oil until deep golden and crusted all over, 8-10 minutes. drain. they should be cooked through but firm. whisk the yogurt with the kashmiri chilli, fennel powder and dry ginger until there are no lumps. keep it beside the stove. heat the ghee in a heavy pan, add the asafoetida, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves, and let them bloom for 20 seconds. take the pan off the heat. pour in the yogurt mixture, stirring without stopping. return to low heat and keep stirring until it comes to a bare simmer and thickens slightly, about 5 minutes. add the potatoes and salt with about half a cup of hot water. cover tightly and cook on the lowest possible heat for 15-20 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally. uncover; the gravy should cling to the potatoes and the fat should show at the edges. rest 10 minutes before serving.

entries.title: Kashmiri Pulav
entries.snippet: Mildly sweet saffron rice with fruit and nuts, served alongside the wazwan
entries.text: kashmiri pulav kashmiri mildly sweet saffron rice with fruit and nuts, served alongside the wazwan vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic basmati rice milk saffron green cardamom cinnamon cloves bay leaf fennel powder almonds cashews raisins (kishmish) pomegranate sugar ghee salt warm the milk and steep the saffron in it. fry the nuts and raisins in ghee until the nuts colour and the raisins puff. lift out and reserve. in the same ghee, bloom the whole spices, then add the drained rice and turn it gently for 2 minutes. add the saffron milk, 2.5 cups water, sugar and salt. bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat 12 minutes. rest, covered and off the heat, a further 10 minutes before lifting the lid. fork through the fried nuts and raisins and scatter pomegranate over the top.

entries.title: Kashmiri Rajma
entries.snippet: small dark kidney beans simmered with fennel and dry ginger, without an onion in sight
entries.text: kashmiri rajma kashmiri small dark kidney beans simmered with fennel and dry ginger, without an onion in sight vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic rajma (kidney beans) mustard oil kashmiri chilli powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder black cardamom cloves cinnamon bay leaf garam masala water salt boil the drained beans in the water with the bay leaf, black cardamom, cloves and cinnamon. simmer covered 60 minutes, or pressure-cook 20 minutes at full pressure, until a bean crushes to paste between finger and thumb. heat the mustard oil in a second pan until it just smokes, then lower the flame. add the hing and let it foam for 10 seconds. off the heat, stir in the chilli paste, turmeric, fennel powder and dry ginger, then return to low heat and fry for 2 minutes until the oil separates at the edges. pour the tempering into the beans along with their cooking liquid and add salt to taste. crush a ladleful of the beans against the side of the pot and stir them back in to thicken the gravy. simmer uncovered 15 minutes, until the gravy is red-brown and coats the beans rather than pooling around them. stir in the garam masala, rest 5 minutes and serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Modur Pulav
entries.snippet: sweet saffron rice with milk, ghee and dried fruit, made for pandit feast days
entries.text: modur pulav kashmiri sweet saffron rice with milk, ghee and dried fruit, made for pandit feast days vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic basmati rice ghee milk water sugar saffron green cardamom cinnamon cloves bay leaf almonds cashews raisins (kishmish) dried apricots (khubani) salt heat 3 tbsp of the ghee and fry the almonds and cashews until pale gold, about 90 seconds, then lift them out. fry the raisins in the same ghee for 15 seconds, until they puff up, and lift them out too. add the remaining ghee, then the cinnamon, cloves, cardamom and bay leaf, and let them scent the fat for 30 seconds. tip in the drained rice and turn it gently for 2 minutes, until every grain is coated and looks glassy at the edges. pour in the water, milk, salt and the saffron milk, and bring to a boil. as soon as it boils, lower the flame to its minimum, cover tightly and cook 12 minutes without lifting the lid. uncover, scatter over the sugar, fried nuts, raisins and apricot, and fold through with two strokes. cover again and leave on the lowest heat for 5 minutes, then rest off the heat for 10 before serving warm.

entries.title: Muji Gaad
entries.snippet: winter fish and radish in a red chilli gravy, sour and warming
entries.text: muji gaad kashmiri winter fish and radish in a red chilli gravy, sour and warming pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic fish (firm fillets or steaks) radish (mooli) mustard oil kashmiri chilli powder turmeric powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) asafoetida (hing) anardana (dried pomegranate seeds) water salt heat the mustard oil in a wide pan until it smokes, then lower the flame to medium. fry the fish steaks in a single layer, 3 minutes a side, until crusted and deep gold. lift them out and set aside. add the radish batons to the same oil and fry 5 minutes, until the edges brown and the sharp raw smell fades. add the hing and let it foam for 10 seconds. off the heat, stir in the chilli paste, remaining turmeric, fennel powder and dry ginger. pour in the water, add 1 tsp salt, and simmer covered 12 minutes until the radish is tender and the gravy has turned deep red. return the fish, add the crushed anardana, and simmer uncovered 8 minutes, spooning gravy over rather than stirring. rest 5 minutes off the heat and serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Mutton Yakhni
entries.snippet: pale yogurt and fennel mutton curry, aromatic rather than hot
entries.text: mutton yakhni kashmiri pale yogurt and fennel mutton curry, aromatic rather than hot gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic mutton / lamb yogurt / dahi ghee fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) asafoetida (hing) black cardamom green cardamom cloves cinnamon bay leaf mint black pepper water salt bring the mutton, water, bay leaves, black cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and 1 tsp salt to a boil, then skim off every bit of grey foam. cover and simmer 40 minutes, until the meat gives easily to a fork. lift the pieces out and keep the strained stock. heat the ghee in a heavy pan and add the hing — it foams and smells sharp for about 10 seconds. pull the pan off the heat and stir in the fennel powder and dry ginger for 20 seconds. return to a low flame, add the drained mutton and turn it in the spiced ghee for 3 minutes until every piece is glossy. take the pan off the heat again, pour in the whisked yogurt and stir without stopping for 2 minutes before setting it back on the lowest flame. add 450ml of the reserved stock, the crushed mint and the black pepper, and simmer uncovered 20 minutes until the gravy thinly coats a spoon. crush the green cardamom over the top, check the salt and rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Nadru Yakhni
entries.snippet: lotus stem rounds in a gentle fennel and yogurt gravy, the meatless yakhni
entries.text: nadru yakhni kashmiri lotus stem rounds in a gentle fennel and yogurt gravy, the meatless yakhni vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic lotus stem (nadru/bhee) yogurt / dahi ghee fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) asafoetida (hing) green cardamom cloves cinnamon bay leaf mint black pepper water salt boil the rounds in the water with the bay leaf, cloves, cinnamon and 1/2 tsp salt for 12 minutes, until a knife goes in with slight resistance. drain, keeping every drop of the cooking water. heat the ghee in a heavy pan and add the hing, letting it foam for 10 seconds. off the heat, stir in the fennel powder and dry ginger for 20 seconds. return to low heat, add the drained rounds and turn them for 3 minutes until coated. take the pan off the heat, pour in the yogurt and stir continuously for 2 minutes before setting it back on the lowest flame. add 350ml of the reserved cooking water, the cardamom, mint and black pepper, and simmer uncovered 15 minutes until the gravy just coats the rounds. check the salt and rest 5 minutes off the heat before serving with rice.

entries.title: Phirni
entries.snippet: chilled ground-rice pudding set in earthenware, scented with cardamom and rose
entries.text: phirni kashmiri chilled ground-rice pudding set in earthenware, scented with cardamom and rose vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic basmati rice milk sugar green cardamom saffron rose water kewra water pistachios almonds bring the milk to a boil in a heavy-based pan, then lower the heat to a bare simmer. mix the ground rice with 4 tbsp cold milk to a smooth slurry with no lumps. pour the slurry into the simmering milk in a thin stream, whisking the whole time. cook on low for 20 minutes, stirring constantly and scraping the base and corners, until the mixture coats the back of a spoon and the rice has no bite left. add the sugar and cook 5 minutes more, until it thickens again to the consistency of pouring cream. stir in the saffron milk and the ground cardamom, and take the pan off the heat. let it cool for 5 minutes, then stir in the rose water or kewra. pour into the chilled bowls while still pourable; it thickens a great deal as it sets. scatter with the slivered pistachios and almonds and refrigerate at least 4 hours until firm and cold.

entries.title: Rista
