entries.snippet: the red twin of gushtaba, meatballs poached in a chilli and fennel gravy
entries.text: rista kashmiri the red twin of gushtaba, meatballs poached in a chilli and fennel gravy gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic mutton / lamb ghee kashmiri chilli powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) asafoetida (hing) black cardamom green cardamom cloves cinnamon bay leaf black pepper baking soda water salt work the mince with 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp fennel powder, 1/2 tsp dry ginger, the ground green cardamom, black pepper, baking soda and 1 tsp salt for 10 minutes until pale and springy. wet your palms and roll 8 smooth balls, slightly flattened, then chill them 20 minutes. heat the remaining ghee in a wide pan, add the hing and let it foam for 10 seconds. add the bay leaf, black cardamom, cloves and cinnamon and let them crackle for 30 seconds. off the heat, stir in the soaked chilli paste along with the rest of the fennel powder and dry ginger. pour in the water, add 1 tsp salt and bring to a gentle boil, then let it bubble 5 minutes so the raw chilli taste cooks out. lower the balls in one by one and leave the pan alone for 10 minutes, swirling rather than stirring. simmer uncovered on low for 35 minutes, basting the balls with gravy, until the fat rises red on the surface and the gravy has reduced by a third. rest 10 minutes off the heat and serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Rogan Josh
entries.snippet: Kashmiri lamb in a red gravy coloured by ratan jot and Kashmiri chilli, without onion or garlic
entries.text: rogan josh kashmiri kashmiri lamb in a red gravy coloured by ratan jot and kashmiri chilli, without onion or garlic gluten-free no-onion-garlic mutton / lamb yogurt / dahi kashmiri chilli powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) asafoetida (hing) black cardamom green cardamom cinnamon cloves bay leaf ghee salt heat the ghee and bloom the asafoetida and whole spices until fragrant. add the mutton and sear over high heat until browned on all sides. take the pan off the heat. stir the kashmiri chilli, fennel and dry ginger into the whisked yogurt, then add it to the meat, stirring constantly. return to low heat and cook, stirring, until the gravy thickens and the fat begins to show, about 10 minutes. add a cup of hot water and salt, cover, and simmer 60-70 minutes until the meat is tender and the gravy is deep red and glossy. rest 15 minutes. serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Tabak Maaz
entries.snippet: lamb ribs simmered soft in spiced milk, then fried crisp in ghee
entries.text: tabak maaz kashmiri lamb ribs simmered soft in spiced milk, then fried crisp in ghee gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic mutton / lamb milk water ghee turmeric powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) asafoetida (hing) black cardamom green cardamom cloves cinnamon bay leaf black pepper salt put the ribs in a wide pan with the milk, water, turmeric, fennel powder, dry ginger, hing, both cardamoms, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaf and 1 tsp salt. bring to a bare simmer and hold it there, uncovered, for about 60 minutes. the ribs are ready when the meat has shrunk back from the bone ends and almost all the liquid has gone, leaving a thick coating. lift the ribs onto a rack and leave them to cool and dry for at least 30 minutes. heat the ghee in a heavy frying pan over medium heat until it shimmers. fry the ribs in a single layer, 4 minutes on the first side, until the edges are deep gold and audibly crisp. turn once and give them 3 minutes on the second side, pressing lightly with a spatula so the whole face colours. drain on paper, scatter with salt and the black pepper, and serve hot as a starter with green chutney or plain.

entries.title: Ada Pradhaman
entries.snippet: rice ada simmered in jaggery and thick coconut milk, the sadya finale
entries.text: ada pradhaman kerala rice ada simmered in jaggery and thick coconut milk, the sadya finale vegetarian gluten-free rice flour jaggery coconut milk ghee green cardamom dry ginger powder (saunth) cumin powder (jeera) cashews raisins (kishmish) coconut (fresh or desiccated) water salt boil the ada squares in plenty of water for 5 minutes until soft and translucent. drain and rinse in cold water. heat 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy pan and fry the cashews until golden, then the raisins until they puff, then the coconut slivers until brown. lift each out separately. in the same pan pour in the strained jaggery syrup and boil 4 minutes until it thickens and coats a spoon. add the drained ada and cook in the syrup on low for 10 minutes, stirring, until each piece is glossy and has darkened to the colour of the jaggery. pour in the thin coconut milk and simmer gently for 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until it reduces by about a quarter. stir in the remaining 2 tbsp ghee and cook 3 minutes more. add the powdered cardamom, dry ginger, cumin powder and the pinch of salt. take the pan off the heat and stir in the thick coconut milk. do not return it to the boil. scatter over the fried cashews, raisins and coconut slivers and serve warm.

entries.title: Appam
entries.snippet: Lacy fermented rice pancakes with a soft, thick centre
entries.text: appam kerala lacy fermented rice pancakes with a soft, thick centre vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) coconut (fresh or desiccated) coconut milk rice (short/medium grain) sugar salt coconut oil grind the soaked rice with the grated coconut, cooked rice and enough water to make a smooth, pourable batter. add sugar, cover, and leave to ferment 8-10 hours until risen and faintly sour. stir in the coconut milk and salt. the batter should be thinner than dosa batter — like single cream. heat the appachatti, wipe with coconut oil, pour a ladle into the middle, then immediately lift the pan and swirl it once so batter climbs the sides. cover and cook 2-3 minutes on low. do not flip. lift out when the edges lift away on their own. serve with stew, kadala curry or sweetened coconut milk.

entries.title: Avial
entries.snippet: Mixed vegetables bound in coconut, cumin and yogurt, finished with raw coconut oil
entries.text: avial kerala mixed vegetables bound in coconut, cumin and yogurt, finished with raw coconut oil vegetarian gluten-free nut-free raw banana / plantain yam (suran) drumstick (moringa pod) carrot french beans ash gourd (petha) cucumber coconut (fresh or desiccated) cumin seeds green chilli turmeric powder yogurt / dahi curry leaves coconut oil salt cook the vegetables hardest-first in a wide pan with turmeric, salt and just enough water — yam and banana first, softer vegetables after. coarsely grind the coconut with cumin and green chilli. do not make it a smooth paste. fold the coconut mixture through the cooked vegetables and simmer 5 minutes. take the pan off the heat, then stir in the whisked yogurt. return briefly to very low heat but do not let it boil. crush the curry leaves between your palms and stir them in with the raw coconut oil. rest 10 minutes before serving. avial is served warm, not hot.

entries.title: Beef Ularthiyathu
entries.snippet: slow-fried beef in dark pepper masala with coconut slivers and a raft of curry leaves
entries.text: beef ularthiyathu kerala slow-fried beef in dark pepper masala with coconut slivers and a raft of curry leaves gluten-free dairy-free nut-free beef coconut (fresh or desiccated) shallots (small red onions) ginger garlic green chilli black pepper coriander powder red chilli powder turmeric powder fennel powder garam masala cloves cinnamon vinegar curry leaves coconut oil salt pressure cook the marinated beef with 1/2 cup water and the whole cloves and cinnamon for 4 whistles, then 15 minutes on low. release naturally. meanwhile, heat 2 tbsp coconut oil in a wide kadhai and fry the coconut slivers over medium heat for 3 minutes until golden. lift out and set aside. in the same oil add the shallots, ginger, garlic and green chillies. cook 8 minutes until the shallots are deep brown at the edges. add the fennel powder, garam masala and remaining pepper and fry 1 minute until the oil smells of fennel. tip in the cooked beef along with any liquid from the cooker. raise the heat and boil hard, stirring, for 8-10 minutes until the liquid has gone. add the remaining 2 tbsp coconut oil and turn the heat to medium-low. now fry the beef, stirring every couple of minutes, for 20-25 minutes. scrape the crust off the base of the pan back into the meat every few minutes — that is where the flavour is. throw in all four sprigs of curry leaves and the fried coconut slivers. fry 2 minutes more until the leaves crisp and shatter. rest off the heat 5 minutes and serve with kappa or porotta.

entries.title: Cabbage Thoran
entries.snippet: shredded cabbage tossed with crushed coconut, mustard and curry leaves
entries.text: cabbage thoran kerala shredded cabbage tossed with crushed coconut, mustard and curry leaves vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free cabbage coconut (fresh or desiccated) shallots (small red onions) green chilli garlic cumin seeds turmeric powder coconut oil mustard seeds dried red chillies curry leaves salt heat the coconut oil in a kadhai over medium heat until it thins and shimmers. add the mustard seeds and let them pop, about 30 seconds, then add the broken red chillies and curry leaves. stir in the chopped shallot and remaining slit chillies. cook 3 minutes until the shallot turns translucent and smells sweet. tip in the cabbage and salt. toss to coat in the oil. cover and cook on low for 5 minutes. the cabbage will release its own water — do not add any. uncover, raise the heat and stir-fry 2 minutes to drive off the moisture at the bottom of the pan. add the crushed coconut mixture and toss through for 2 minutes, until the coconut smells toasty and looks dry. taste for salt and take it off the heat while the cabbage still has bite.

entries.title: Chemmeen Manga Curry
entries.snippet: prawns and raw mango in a sharp red coconut gravy from the backwaters
entries.text: chemmeen manga curry kerala prawns and raw mango in a sharp red coconut gravy from the backwaters pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free prawns raw green mango coconut milk shallots (small red onions) ginger garlic green chilli kashmiri chilli powder turmeric powder fenugreek seeds (methi) mustard seeds curry leaves coconut oil salt heat the coconut oil in a wide pan and pop the mustard seeds, about 30 seconds. add the fenugreek seeds and let them darken for 15 seconds only. add the shallots, ginger, garlic, green chillies and 2 sprigs of curry leaves. cook 6 minutes until the shallots are soft and just starting to colour. turn the heat to low, add the kashmiri chilli and turmeric and fry 45 seconds until the oil runs red. add the mango slices, the thin coconut milk and salt. simmer 8 minutes until the mango is tender but still holding together. slide in the prawns and cook 3-4 minutes, just until they turn opaque and curl into loose c shapes. stir in the thick coconut milk and the last sprig of curry leaves. warm through 1 minute without boiling. take off the heat and rest covered for 10 minutes so the mango sourness spreads through the gravy.

entries.title: Idiyappam
entries.snippet: steamed rice string hoppers, soft and threadlike, served with coconut milk
entries.text: idiyappam kerala steamed rice string hoppers, soft and threadlike, served with coconut milk vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic rice flour water coconut (fresh or desiccated) coconut oil salt bring the water to a full rolling boil with the salt and 1 tsp of the coconut oil. pour the boiling water over the rice flour all at once, stirring hard with a wooden spoon until it comes together as a shaggy mass. cover and rest 5 minutes so the flour absorbs fully. oil your palms and knead the warm dough for 3-4 minutes until it is completely smooth, soft and non-sticky — like fresh play dough. grease the idiyappam plates and scatter a teaspoon of grated coconut on each. load the press and squeeze the dough onto the plates in tight overlapping spirals, about 1cm thick. scatter a little more coconut on top and stack the plates in a steamer over rapidly boiling water. steam 6-8 minutes, until the strings look glossy and set and no longer taste of raw flour. lift off and let them cool for 2 minutes before easing them off the plate, or they will tear.

entries.title: Kadala Curry
entries.snippet: black chickpeas in dark roasted coconut gravy, the breakfast partner to puttu
entries.text: kadala curry kerala black chickpeas in dark roasted coconut gravy, the breakfast partner to puttu vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free kala chana (brown chickpeas) coconut (fresh or desiccated) shallots (small red onions) onion ginger garlic coriander powder red chilli powder turmeric powder fennel seeds (saunf) garam masala coconut oil mustard seeds dried red chillies curry leaves salt pressure cook the soaked chickpeas with 3 cups water, the turmeric and 1 tsp salt for 5 whistles, then 10 minutes on low. release naturally and keep the cooking liquid. heat 1 tbsp coconut oil in a heavy pan and fry the sliced shallots for 4 minutes until browning at the edges. add the grated coconut and roast on medium-low, stirring constantly, for 10-12 minutes until it is a deep chocolate brown. add the coriander powder, chilli powder and fennel seeds and roast 1 minute more, until the spices darken and smell toasted. cool slightly, then blend with 1/2 cup water to a fine dark paste. in the same pan heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil, pop the mustard seeds, then add the broken red chillies, curry leaves, chopped onion, ginger and garlic. cook 6 minutes until the onion is soft and gold. stir in the ground coconut paste and fry 4 minutes until the oil begins to separate at the edges. add the cooked chickpeas with their liquid and the garam masala. simmer uncovered 12-15 minutes until the gravy thickens enough to coat a spoon. taste for salt and rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with puttu or appam.

entries.title: Kerala Meen Curry
entries.snippet: Fish simmered in coconut milk and kokum, tempered with curry leaves and coconut oil
entries.text: kerala meen curry kerala fish simmered in coconut milk and kokum, tempered with curry leaves and coconut oil gluten-free dairy-free nut-free pescatarian fish (firm fillets or steaks) coconut milk kokum shallots (small red onions) ginger garlic green chilli curry leaves turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder fenugreek seeds (methi) mustard seeds coconut oil salt heat the coconut oil. splutter the mustard seeds and fenugreek, then add the curry leaves, shallots, ginger, garlic and green chillies. fry until the shallots soften and turn pale gold. lower the heat, add the turmeric and kashmiri chilli and stir for 30 seconds only. powdered chilli scorches fast and turns bitter. add the soaked kokum with its water, the thin part of the coconut milk and salt. simmer 8 minutes to build the base. slide in the fish in a single layer. do not stir; shake the pan instead so the pieces stay whole. simmer 6-8 minutes until just opaque. pour in the thick coconut milk, swirl the pan and heat through without letting it boil. take it off the heat as soon as it steams. rest at least an hour before eating. this curry is markedly better after resting, and better still the next day.

entries.title: Meen Varuthathu
entries.snippet: chilli-and-pepper crusted fish shallow fried in coconut oil until the edges blister
entries.text: meen varuthathu kerala chilli-and-pepper crusted fish shallow fried in coconut oil until the edges blister pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder turmeric powder black pepper ginger garlic lemon / lime rice flour curry leaves coconut oil salt bring the marinated fish back to room temperature for 15 minutes if it has been in the fridge. dust each piece lightly with rice flour on both sides and shake off the excess. heat the coconut oil in a heavy tawa over medium-high until a pinch of flour dropped in sizzles instantly. slide in the fish, laying it away from you, and do not touch it for 4 minutes. turn once and fry the second side 3-4 minutes until the crust is deep brick red and the flesh at the slash is opaque. throw the curry leaves into the hot oil around the fish for the last 30 seconds until they crisp. lift onto a plate, scatter the crisped leaves over, and serve within minutes with rice and a wedge of lemon.

entries.title: Mutta Roast
entries.snippet: boiled eggs in a dark slow-fried onion masala, breakfast alongside appam
entries.text: mutta roast kerala boiled eggs in a dark slow-fried onion masala, breakfast alongside appam vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free eggs onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli red chilli powder kashmiri chilli powder coriander powder turmeric powder garam masala fennel powder black pepper curry leaves coconut oil salt heat 2 tbsp coconut oil in a kadhai and fry the scored eggs with a pinch of turmeric and salt for 2 minutes, turning, until blistered and gold. lift out. add the remaining oil, then the sliced onions, ginger, garlic, green chillies and 2 sprigs of curry leaves with a pinch of salt. cook on medium-low for 20-25 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the onions collapse to about a fifth of their volume and turn a deep glossy brown. add the chilli powder, kashmiri chilli, coriander powder, turmeric and pepper. fry 90 seconds with a splash of water so the spices do not catch. stir in the tomatoes and cook 8 minutes until they break down completely and the oil pools at the edges. add 1/4 cup water, the garam masala and fennel powder, and simmer 3 minutes into a thick clinging masala. return the fried eggs, roll them in the masala and cook 3 minutes on low so they take on the colour. scatter over the last sprig of curry leaves, cover and rest 5 minutes off the heat before serving with appam or bread.

entries.title: Nadan Chicken Stew
entries.snippet: pale peppery chicken and potato stew in coconut milk, the classic appam partner
entries.text: nadan chicken stew kerala pale peppery chicken and potato stew in coconut milk, the classic appam partner gluten-free dairy-free nut-free chicken potato carrot onion ginger garlic green chilli black pepper cinnamon cloves green cardamom coconut milk curry leaves coconut oil salt heat the coconut oil in a heavy pot over medium-low and add the cinnamon, cloves and cardamom. fry 30 seconds until fragrant. add the onion, ginger, garlic and green chillies with a pinch of salt. cook 6-8 minutes until soft and glassy. stir in the crushed pepper and fry 30 seconds. add the chicken and turn it in the aromatics for 3 minutes until the flesh turns opaque white. pour in the thin coconut milk, add the potato, carrot, curry leaves and salt, and bring to a bare simmer. cover and cook on low for 25 minutes, until the chicken pulls easily from the bone and the potato is soft at the centre. uncover and stir in the thick coconut milk. warm through for 2 minutes without letting it boil. taste for salt and pepper, then rest covered for 10 minutes off the heat before serving with appam.

entries.title: Olan
entries.snippet: ash gourd and cowpeas simmered in thin coconut milk, barely spiced on purpose
entries.text: olan kerala ash gourd and cowpeas simmered in thin coconut milk, barely spiced on purpose vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic ash gourd (petha) lobia (black-eyed peas) coconut milk green chilli curry leaves coconut oil salt boil the soaked cowpeas in 2 cups of water for 20-25 minutes until soft but still holding their shape. drain, keeping a little of the cooking water. put the ash gourd slices in a wide pan with the slit chillies, salt and just enough water to come halfway up. simmer uncovered 8 minutes until the gourd turns translucent at the edges and a knife slides through without resistance. add the cooked cowpeas and the thin coconut milk. bring to a bare simmer. cook 5 minutes on low, shaking the pan rather than stirring so the gourd slices stay whole. pour in the thick coconut milk and the curry leaves. warm through for 1 minute only. take off the heat, stir in the raw coconut oil and cover for 5 minutes before serving.

entries.title: Parippu Curry
entries.snippet: soft moong dal in coconut and cumin, the first course of a sadya
entries.text: parippu curry kerala soft moong dal in coconut and cumin, the first course of a sadya vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free moong dal coconut (fresh or desiccated) green chilli cumin seeds garlic turmeric powder shallots (small red onions) coconut oil mustard seeds dried red chillies curry leaves salt pressure cook the rinsed dal with 2.5 cups water and the turmeric for 3 whistles, then rest until the pressure drops. whisk the cooked dal smooth with a ladle, adding hot water until it is the consistency of thin cream. stir in the ground coconut paste and the salt. simmer on low for 6-8 minutes, stirring often, until the raw coconut smell disappears and it thickens slightly. heat the coconut oil in a small pan and pop the mustard seeds, about 30 seconds. add the sliced shallots, broken red chillies and curry leaves and fry 2 minutes until the shallots brown. pour the tempering over the dal and cover for 5 minutes so the curry leaf aroma settles in. serve over hot rice as the first course of the meal, with a papadam crushed over the top.

entries.title: Pazham Pori
entries.snippet: ripe plantain slices in a turmeric-gold batter, the four o'clock teashop snack
entries.text: pazham pori kerala ripe plantain slices in a turmeric-gold batter, the four o'clock teashop snack vegetarian vegan dairy-free nut-free raw banana / plantain plain flour (maida) rice flour turmeric powder sugar salt water cumin seeds coconut oil whisk the maida, rice flour, turmeric, sugar, salt and crushed cumin together in a bowl. add the water gradually, whisking, until you have a smooth lump-free batter. rest 10 minutes. peel the plantains and slice each lengthwise into 3-4 flat strips about 8mm thick. heat the oil in a kadhai to 175c — a drop of batter should rise and sizzle within 3 seconds without browning instantly. dip a strip into the batter, let the excess run off, and lower it gently into the oil. fry 3-4 at a time for 2 minutes, until the underside is set and pale gold. turn and fry a further 2 minutes until both sides are deep gold and the surface has stopped bubbling hard. lift onto a rack, not paper, so the underside stays crisp. repeat with the rest. serve hot with strong black tea.

entries.title: Pulissery
entries.snippet: soured yogurt and coconut curry, gently spiced and never boiled
entries.text: pulissery kerala soured yogurt and coconut curry, gently spiced and never boiled vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic yogurt / dahi ash gourd (petha) coconut (fresh or desiccated) green chilli cumin seeds turmeric powder coconut oil mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) dried red chillies curry leaves salt cook the ash gourd with the salt and 1/2 cup water in a wide pan, covered, for 8 minutes until soft and translucent. stir in the ground coconut paste and simmer 4 minutes on low, until the raw coconut smell has gone. take the pan off the heat completely and let it cool for 3 minutes. pour in the whisked yogurt, stirring as you go. return to the lowest possible heat and warm, stirring constantly, for 3-4 minutes until it just steams and thickens slightly. taste for salt and set aside covered. heat the coconut oil in a small pan, pop the mustard seeds, then add the fenugreek seeds, broken red chillies and curry leaves and fry 20 seconds. pour the tempering over the curry and cover for 5 minutes before serving with rice.

entries.title: Pumpkin Erissery
entries.snippet: mashed pumpkin and cowpeas under a lid of dark roasted coconut
entries.text: pumpkin erissery kerala mashed pumpkin and cowpeas under a lid of dark roasted coconut vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free pumpkin lobia (black-eyed peas) coconut (fresh or desiccated) green chilli cumin seeds turmeric powder red chilli powder garlic coconut oil mustard seeds dried red chillies curry leaves salt boil the soaked cowpeas in 2 cups water for 20 minutes until tender. do not drain. add the pumpkin cubes, chilli powder and salt to the same pan with a little more water if needed. cook covered 10 minutes until the pumpkin is soft enough to crush against the side of the pan. mash roughly with the back of a ladle, leaving some cubes whole for texture. stir in the ground coconut paste and simmer 5 minutes on low until it loses its raw smell and thickens. in a separate kadhai, heat the coconut oil and pop the mustard seeds, about 30 seconds. add the broken red chillies, curry leaves and the remaining cumin seeds and fry 20 seconds. add the reserved grated coconut and roast on medium-low, stirring constantly, for 5-6 minutes until it is a deep even brown and smells nutty. pour the roasted coconut tempering over the pumpkin, stir once, and rest 5 minutes before serving.

entries.title: Puttu
entries.snippet: steamed cylinders of rice flour layered with coconut, eaten hot with kadala curry
entries.text: puttu kerala steamed cylinders of rice flour layered with coconut, eaten hot with kadala curry vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic rice flour coconut (fresh or desiccated) water salt dissolve the salt in the warm water. sprinkle the salted water over the rice flour a tablespoon at a time, rubbing it through with your fingertips after each addition. stop when the flour feels like damp sand and holds a shape in your fist. you may not need all the water. pass the whole lot through a coarse sieve or break the lumps by rubbing between your palms, then rest 10 minutes. bring water to a rolling boil in the base of the puttu maker or steamer. load the mould: a tablespoon of grated coconut at the bottom, then loose flour to two-thirds, then coconut, then flour, finishing with coconut. do not press down. steam 7-8 minutes from when a steady plume comes out of the top. push the puttu out onto a plate with the handle of a wooden spoon and serve immediately with kadala curry or ripe banana.

entries.title: Amti
entries.snippet: toor dal made sweet, sour and dark with goda masala, tamarind and jaggery
entries.text: amti maharashtrian toor dal made sweet, sour and dark with goda masala, tamarind and jaggery vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free toor dal (pigeon pea) garam masala tamarind jaggery coconut (fresh or desiccated) groundnut oil mustard seeds cumin seeds curry leaves asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt pressure cook the soaked dal with the turmeric and 300ml water for 4 whistles until completely soft, then whisk it smooth. heat the oil in a pan, pop the mustard seeds, then add the cumin, curry leaves and hing and let them sizzle 10 seconds. add the kashmiri chilli and chilli powder and stir for 10 seconds off the heat so they bloom without burning. pour in the whisked dal and the remaining 200ml water and bring to a simmer. stir in the goda masala, tamarind pulp, jaggery and salt. simmer uncovered 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until the amti darkens and thins slightly and a skin no longer forms on top. taste and adjust: more jaggery if it bites, more tamarind if it tastes flat. finish with the grated coconut and coriander and serve with rice.

entries.title: Batata Bhaji
entries.snippet: soft turmeric-yellow potatoes with mustard seeds, curry leaves and green chilli
entries.text: batata bhaji maharashtrian soft turmeric-yellow potatoes with mustard seeds, curry leaves and green chilli vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free potato onion green chilli groundnut oil mustard seeds cumin seeds curry leaves turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) sugar water lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) salt boil the potatoes whole in their skins until a knife goes through easily, about 20 minutes, then cool, peel and break into rough 3cm pieces. heat the oil and pop the mustard seeds, then add the cumin, curry leaves and hing. add the green chilli and sliced onion and cook 5 minutes until the onion is soft and translucent. stir in the turmeric and let it cook 20 seconds in the oil. add the potato, salt and sugar and turn everything over gently until the pieces are evenly yellow. pour in the water, cover and steam on low heat for 5 minutes. squeeze over the lemon, fold through the coriander and serve with pooris, chapati or as the filling for vada pav.

entries.title: Bharli Vangi
entries.snippet: baby aubergines stuffed with roasted peanut, coconut and goda masala, simmered in their own gravy
entries.text: bharli vangi maharashtrian baby aubergines stuffed with roasted peanut, coconut and goda masala, simmered in their own gravy vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free eggplant / brinjal peanuts dried coconut (copra) sesame seeds onion garlic ginger garam masala coriander powder red chilli powder turmeric powder tamarind jaggery groundnut oil water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt dry-roast the grated dried coconut over low heat for 4 minutes until it is a deep golden brown, then tip it straight out of the pan. grind the roasted coconut, peanut and sesame with one chopped onion, the garlic and the ginger to a coarse, thick masala using 3 tbsp water. mix the masala with the goda masala, coriander powder, chilli powder, turmeric, half the tamarind pulp, the jaggery and salt. drain the aubergines, pat dry and pack about a tablespoon of masala into each slit, keeping the fruit whole. reserve the leftover masala. heat the oil in a wide pan and lay the stuffed aubergines in a single layer. fry 6 minutes, turning them by shaking the pan, until the skins blister and dull. lift the aubergines out, add the second onion, sliced, and cook 5 minutes until soft. stir in the reserved masala and fry 4 minutes until it darkens and oil separates at the edges. add the water and the remaining tamarind, return the aubergines to the pan, cover and simmer 20 minutes over low heat. check that a knife slides into an aubergine without resistance, and that the gravy is thick and rust-coloured with oil floating on top. scatter with coriander and rest 10 minutes before serving with bhakri or rice.

entries.title: Jowar Bhakri
entries.snippet: an unleavened sorghum flatbread patted out by hand, nutty and slightly coarse
entries.text: jowar bhakri maharashtrian an unleavened sorghum flatbread patted out by hand, nutty and slightly coarse vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic jowar (sorghum) flour water salt rice flour bring the water to a rolling boil with the salt. put the flour in a wide bowl and pour in about three quarters of the boiling water, mixing with the handle of a wooden spoon until it comes together in a shaggy mass. as soon as it is cool enough to touch, knead firmly for 5 minutes with the heel of your hand until the dough is smooth and shows no cracks when you press it. divide into 6 balls and keep them covered with a damp cloth. dust the counter with jowar flour, flatten a ball with your palm, then pat it out into a 15cm disc by pressing and rotating with the flat of your fingers. brush the loose flour off, lift the bhakri on your palm and lay it onto the hot tawa. smear the top surface with water using your fingers and cook 1 minute, until the wet film dries and the underside shows pale brown patches. flip and cook the second side 1 minute, then flip once more and press around the edges with a folded cloth until it puffs up like a balloon. stack the finished bhakris in a cloth-lined basket and serve hot with zunka, pithla or usal.

entries.title: Kanda Poha
entries.snippet: flattened rice steamed soft with onion, peanuts and curry leaves, breakfast in fifteen minutes
entries.text: kanda poha maharashtrian flattened rice steamed soft with onion, peanuts and curry leaves, breakfast in fifteen minutes vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free poha (flattened rice) onion peanuts groundnut oil mustard seeds cumin seeds green chilli curry leaves turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) sugar potato lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) coconut (fresh or desiccated) salt rinse the poha in a colander until the grains soften, then leave it to drain and swell for 10 minutes. toss the drained poha with the turmeric, sugar and salt so every grain turns yellow. do this with your fingertips, not a spoon. fry the peanuts in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes until they darken and smell toasted, then lift them out. into the same oil add the mustard seeds and wait for them to pop, then the cumin, green chilli, curry leaves and hing. add the diced potato, if using, cover and cook 6 minutes until tender. add the onion and cook 4 minutes until soft and translucent but not browned. fold in the poha and the fried peanuts, lower the heat, cover and steam 3 minutes. turn off the heat, squeeze over the lemon and scatter with coriander and grated coconut. serve at once.

entries.title: Kolhapuri Chicken Rassa
entries.snippet: thin, fiery red chicken curry built on roasted coconut and dagad phool
entries.text: kolhapuri chicken rassa maharashtrian thin, fiery red chicken curry built on roasted coconut and dagad phool gluten-free dairy-free nut-free chicken onion dried coconut (copra) coconut (fresh or desiccated) garlic ginger kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder stone flower (dagad phool) poppy seeds (khus khus) sesame seeds coriander powder cumin seeds black pepper cloves cinnamon black cardamom bay leaf turmeric powder groundnut oil water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt grind the ginger and garlic to a paste and rub half of it into the chicken with the turmeric and salt. leave 30 minutes. dry-roast the grated dried coconut over low heat for 5 minutes until it is dark brown and smells toasted, then tip it out immediately. in the same pan, dry-roast the cumin, black pepper, cloves, cinnamon, black cardamom, stone flower, poppy seeds and sesame for 2 minutes until fragrant. cool completely. fry 2 sliced onions in 2 tbsp of the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until deep brown, then cool. grind the roasted coconut, roasted spices, fried onion, kashmiri chilli, chilli powder and coriander powder with 100ml water to a smooth dark masala. heat the remaining oil in a heavy pan with the bay leaf, add the last onion, finely chopped, and cook 8 minutes until golden. add the remaining ginger-garlic paste, fry 1 minute, then add the chicken and sear over high heat for 5 minutes until the pieces are opaque all over. stir in the ground masala and fry over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes, scraping the base, until it darkens and oil pools at the sides. pour in the water, season with salt, bring to a boil then simmer uncovered 25 minutes until the chicken is tender and a red film of oil floats on the surface. stir in the fresh coconut, if using, check the salt and finish with coriander. rest 10 minutes off the heat and serve with bhakri or chapati and raw onion.

entries.title: Matki Usal
entries.snippet: sprouted moth beans in a thin dark gravy of onion, roasted coconut and goda masala
entries.text: matki usal maharashtrian sprouted moth beans in a thin dark gravy of onion, roasted coconut and goda masala vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free sprouted moth/matki beans onion garlic ginger dried coconut (copra) garam masala red chilli powder kashmiri chilli powder coriander powder turmeric powder mustard seeds cumin seeds curry leaves asafoetida (hing) jaggery tamarind groundnut oil water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt grind the roasted dried coconut with half the onion, the garlic and the ginger to a coarse paste with 3 tbsp water. heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds, then add the cumin, curry leaves and hing. add the remaining chopped onion and cook 6 minutes until golden at the edges. stir in the coconut paste and fry 5 minutes over medium heat until it darkens and stops smelling raw. add the chilli powder, kashmiri chilli, coriander powder, turmeric and goda masala and fry 1 minute. tip in the sprouts, turn them through the masala and cook 3 minutes. add the water, salt, jaggery and tamarind, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 18 minutes until the beans are soft but still hold their shape. uncover and check the gravy: it should be thin, dark and slick with red oil on top. loosen with hot water if it has tightened. finish with coriander and serve with bhakri, or with pav and chopped onion.

entries.title: Misal Pav
entries.snippet: Sprouted beans under a fiery kat, topped with farsan and eaten with pav
entries.text: misal pav maharashtrian sprouted beans under a fiery kat, topped with farsan and eaten with pav vegetarian vegan dairy-free sprouted moth/matki beans onion tomato coconut (fresh or desiccated) garlic ginger red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) turmeric powder garam masala mustard seeds curry leaves peanuts sesame seeds pav / soft bread rolls lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) groundnut oil salt pressure cook the sprouts with turmeric and salt until just tender, 2 whistles. they should hold their shape. for the kat masala, dry roast the coconut, peanut and sesame until deep brown, then blend with two onions, tomato, garlic and ginger to a paste. heat oil, splutter the mustard seeds and curry leaves, add the remaining chopped onion, then the ground paste. fry until the oil separates. add the chilli powder, coriander, cumin and garam masala and cook a further 2 minutes. add 3 cups of hot water and simmer 15 minutes. the kat should be thin and carry a visible layer of red oil. to serve, spoon the usal into bowls, ladle the kat over, and top with farsan, raw onion, coriander and lemon. pav alongside.

entries.title: Pav Bhaji
entries.snippet: mashed vegetables cooked down red and buttery, eaten with griddled pav
entries.text: pav bhaji maharashtrian mashed vegetables cooked down red and buttery, eaten with griddled pav vegetarian nut-free potato cauliflower peas capsicum / bell pepper tomato onion garlic ginger kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder garam masala coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) turmeric powder amchur (dry mango powder) butter pav / soft bread rolls water lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) salt boil the potato, cauliflower and peas in salted water until completely soft, about 15 minutes, then drain and keep the pan warm. melt 40g of the butter on a large tawa or wide pan and cook the chopped onion over medium heat until soft and translucent, about 6 minutes. add the garlic and ginger and fry 1 minute, until the raw edge disappears. stir in the capsicum and cook 3 minutes, just until it loses its squeak. add the tomato and cook down for 10 minutes, pressing it against the pan, until the mass darkens and oil beads at the edges. add the kashmiri chilli, garam masala, coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric, amchur and chilli powder and fry 1 minute. tip in the drained vegetables and mash them straight into the pan with a potato masher until no lumps remain. pour in the water, season with salt, and simmer 10 minutes, mashing and stirring, until the bhaji is thick and glossy and a spoon leaves a trail. stir 20g of butter through the bhaji off the heat and scatter with coriander. split the pav, griddle them cut side down in the remaining butter with a pinch of the masala until the edges are crisp and red, about 2 minutes. serve the bhaji with the hot pav, raw chopped onion and lemon wedges.

entries.title: Pithla
entries.snippet: loose gram flour curry slackened with sour buttermilk, garlicky and made in ten minutes
entries.text: pithla maharashtrian loose gram flour curry slackened with sour buttermilk, garlicky and made in ten minutes vegetarian gluten-free nut-free besan (gram flour) buttermilk (chaas) garlic green chilli onion groundnut oil mustard seeds cumin seeds curry leaves turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt whisk the besan into the cold buttermilk with the turmeric and salt until completely smooth, then whisk in the water. heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds, then add the cumin, curry leaves and hing. add the garlic and green chilli and fry 1 minute until the garlic smells sweet but has not coloured. add the onion, if using, and cook 4 minutes until soft. pour in the besan slurry in a slow stream, stirring continuously. bring to a gentle boil and simmer 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon and the raw besan smell is gone. check the salt, fold through the coriander and pour into bowls. serve immediately with hot jowar bhakri, raw onion and a green chilli.

entries.title: Puran Poli
entries.snippet: a soft flatbread stuffed with sweet chana dal and jaggery, scented with cardamom and nutmeg
entries.text: puran poli maharashtrian a soft flatbread stuffed with sweet chana dal and jaggery, scented with cardamom and nutmeg vegetarian nut-free no-onion-garlic chana dal jaggery green cardamom nutmeg atta (wholewheat flour) plain flour (maida) turmeric powder ghee rice flour water salt knead the atta, maida, turmeric, salt, 2 tbsp ghee and enough water into a very soft, sticky dough, working it for 8 minutes until it stretches without tearing. coat the dough with a spoon of ghee, cover and rest at least 1 hour. pressure cook the soaked chana dal with 500ml water for 4 whistles until soft but not disintegrating, then drain it thoroughly in a colander for 10 minutes. mash or pass the drained dal through a sieve until completely smooth. cook the mashed dal with the jaggery in a heavy pan over medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring constantly, until the mixture pulls away from the sides and holds a line when you drag a spoon through it. stir in the cardamom and nutmeg and let the puran cool completely — it should be firm enough to roll into balls. divide both dough and puran into 8 portions each, with the puran balls slightly larger than the dough balls. flatten a dough ball in your palm, sit a puran ball in the middle, gather the edges over the top and pinch them shut, then flatten gently. dust with rice flour and roll out very gently to about 18cm, turning often and using almost no pressure. cook on a medium-hot tawa for about 1 minute a side until pale brown spots appear, smearing each side with ghee as you turn it. serve warm with a spoon of ghee poured over, and katachi amti alongside.

entries.title: Sabudana Khichdi
entries.snippet: tapioca pearls turned glassy in ghee with crushed peanuts and green chilli, the fasting-day standby
entries.text: sabudana khichdi maharashtrian tapioca pearls turned glassy in ghee with crushed peanuts and green chilli, the fasting-day standby vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic sabudana (tapioca pearls) peanuts potato ghee cumin seeds green chilli curry leaves sugar lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) salt check the soaked pearls: one should crush to a smooth paste between thumb and finger with no hard white centre. drain in a colander for 10 minutes. toss the drained sabudana with the ground peanut, sugar and salt until every pearl is coated and the mix looks dry and loose. heat the ghee, add the cumin and let it darken for 20 seconds, then add the green chilli and curry leaves. add the diced potato and fry 2 minutes until the edges catch a little gold. tip in the sabudana, stir once to combine, then cook over medium heat for 5 to 7 minutes, turning it over gently every minute. cover, take the pan off the heat and let it stand 2 minutes. squeeze over the lemon, fold through the coriander and serve hot, with a spoonful of plain yogurt alongside if you are not fasting.

entries.title: Sol Kadhi
entries.snippet: pink kokum and coconut milk drink, sour and cooling, drunk at the end of a coastal meal
entries.text: sol kadhi maharashtrian pink kokum and coconut milk drink, sour and cooling, drunk at the end of a coastal meal vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free kokum coconut milk garlic green chilli cumin seeds water coriander leaves (cilantro) sugar salt soak the kokum in the warm water 20 minutes, squeezing the petals every few minutes, until the water is a deep pink. squeeze the petals dry and discard them, keeping the pink extract. crush the garlic, green chilli and cumin to a rough paste with a pinch of salt. whisk the coconut milk with the remaining 300ml water until completely smooth and lump-free. stir the kokum extract into the coconut milk a little at a time, tasting as you go, until it is as sour as you want and a pale rose colour. stir in the crushed garlic paste, salt and sugar, and let it stand 10 minutes for the garlic to bloom. chill 30 minutes, stir, scatter with coriander and serve in glasses, or poured over plain rice at the end of the meal.

entries.title: Thalipeeth
entries.snippet: a savoury multigrain flatbread patted out by hand, spiced through and eaten with white butter
entries.text: thalipeeth maharashtrian a savoury multigrain flatbread patted out by hand, spiced through and eaten with white butter vegetarian nut-free jowar (sorghum) flour bajra (pearl millet) flour besan (gram flour) rice flour atta (wholewheat flour) onion coriander leaves (cilantro) green chilli ginger garlic cumin seeds coriander powder turmeric powder red chilli powder carom seeds (ajwain) sesame seeds groundnut oil water butter yogurt / dahi salt combine the jowar, bajra, besan, rice flour and atta in a wide bowl with the salt. add the onion, coriander, green chilli, ginger, garlic, cumin, coriander powder, turmeric, chilli powder, ajwain and sesame and rub everything through the flour. pour in the warm water a little at a time and bring it together into a soft dough, softer than chapati dough and only just short of sticky. cover and rest the dough 10 minutes, then divide into 6 balls. oil a square of parchment lightly, put a ball on it and pat it out with wet fingertips into a disc about 15cm across and 5mm thick. poke a hole through the middle with your finger and two or three smaller ones around it. invert the disc onto a hot tawa, peel away the parchment, and drizzle a teaspoon of oil into the centre hole and around the rim. cover and cook 3 minutes over medium heat, then flip and cook a further 3 minutes uncovered until both sides carry dark brown spots. serve hot off the tawa with a lump of white butter melting on top and thick yogurt on the side.

entries.title: Ukadiche Modak
entries.snippet: Steamed rice-flour dumplings filled with coconut and jaggery, made for Ganpati
entries.text: ukadiche modak maharashtrian steamed rice-flour dumplings filled with coconut and jaggery, made for ganpati vegetarian gluten-free nut-free rice flour coconut (fresh or desiccated) jaggery green cardamom nutmeg poppy seeds (khus khus) ghee water salt for the filling, cook the coconut and jaggery together over medium heat until the jaggery melts and the mixture comes together but is still moist, 8-10 minutes. add cardamom, nutmeg and poppy seeds. cool. boil the water with a pinch of salt and a teaspoon of ghee. take it off the heat, tip in the rice flour all at once and stir hard until no dry flour remains. cover 5 minutes. turn out and knead while hot, greasing your palm with ghee, until completely smooth. take a lime-sized ball, flatten into a cup with your fingers, pleat the edge into 9-11 folds, fill, then gather the pleats to a point and seal. steam 10-12 minutes until the shells turn glossy and translucent. serve warm with a spoon of ghee over the top.

entries.title: Vada Pav
entries.snippet: Mumbai's potato fritter in a bun, with garlic chutney and fried chillies
entries.text: vada pav maharashtrian mumbai's potato fritter in a bun, with garlic chutney and fried chillies vegetarian nut-free potato besan (gram flour) pav / soft bread rolls garlic green chilli ginger mustard seeds turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) curry leaves coriander leaves (cilantro) peanuts red chilli powder coconut (fresh or desiccated) lemon / lime neutral oil salt for the dry chutney, dry roast the peanuts, coconut and 6 garlic cloves separately until fragrant, then grind coarsely with the chilli powder and salt. set aside. crush the remaining garlic, the green chillies and ginger to a coarse paste. heat 2 tbsp oil, splutter the mustard seeds, add the asafoetida and curry leaves, then the garlic-chilli paste. fry 1 minute, add the turmeric, then fold through the mashed potato, coriander, lemon and salt. cool and shape into 8 balls. whisk the besan with a pinch of turmeric, salt and enough water to make a thick, smooth coating batter. rest it 10 minutes. heat the frying oil to 180c. dip each ball in batter, let the excess drip off and lower it in. fry 4-5 minutes until pale gold and crisp, turning once. drain on a rack, not paper. split the pav without cutting all the way through, spread the dry chutney generously inside, press in a hot vada and serve at once with the fried chillies.

entries.title: Varan Bhaat
entries.snippet: plain toor dal with ghee and a touch of jaggery over hot rice, the first course of every festive meal
entries.text: varan bhaat maharashtrian plain toor dal with ghee and a touch of jaggery over hot rice, the first course of every festive meal vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic toor dal (pigeon pea) rice (short/medium grain) turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) ghee jaggery cumin seeds lemon / lime water salt rinse and soak the toor dal 20 minutes, then drain. pressure cook the dal with 500ml water and the turmeric for 4 whistles, or simmer covered 40 minutes, until it collapses at a touch. cook the rice in the remaining water until soft, about 15 minutes, and keep it covered and hot. open the cooker and whisk the dal smooth with a ladle, adding the remaining 200ml water until it pours easily. bring it back to a simmer with the salt, jaggery and hing and cook 5 minutes. heat the ghee, crackle the cumin seeds if using, and pour it into the dal. squeeze in the lemon off the heat and taste for salt. serve a ladle of varan over a mound of hot rice with a spoon of raw ghee on top, and eat it first, before anything else on the plate.

entries.title: Zunka
entries.snippet: dry crumbled gram flour cooked with onion and garlic, sharp with green chilli
entries.text: zunka maharashtrian dry crumbled gram flour cooked with onion and garlic, sharp with green chilli vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free besan (gram flour) onion garlic green chilli groundnut oil mustard seeds cumin seeds curry leaves turmeric powder red chilli powder asafoetida (hing) water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt dry-roast the besan in the pan over low heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until it turns a shade darker and smells nutty. tip it out and let it cool. heat the oil, add the mustard seeds and wait for them to pop, then the cumin, curry leaves and hing. add the onion and cook 5 minutes over medium heat until soft and translucent — soft, not browned. stir in the garlic and green chilli and fry 1 minute. add the turmeric, chilli powder and salt, then pour in the hot water and bring it to a boil. lower the heat and sprinkle the roasted besan over the surface in a thin stream with one hand while stirring hard with the other. cover and cook on the lowest heat for 5 minutes without stirring, then take the lid off and break the mass up with a fork into a coarse crumble. drizzle over a spoonful of raw oil, fold through the coriander and serve with jowar bhakri and raw onion.

entries.title: Aloo Pitika
entries.snippet: mashed potato sharpened with raw mustard oil and onion, the plate-partner to every assamese meal
entries.text: aloo pitika northeast indian mashed potato sharpened with raw mustard oil and onion, the plate-partner to every assamese meal vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free potato mustard oil onion green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime salt water boil the whole potatoes in well-salted water 20 minutes, until a knife slides to the centre with no push. drain and peel them while still hot — the skins slip off between your fingers. mash with your hand or a fork while warm, leaving a little texture. do not use a blender. pour the raw mustard oil straight over the warm mash and work it in until the mash looks glossy and smells sharp. fold in the onion, green chilli, coriander and salt. add the lemon juice, taste, and correct the salt — it needs more than you think against the plain rice it is eaten with. shape into a low mound on the plate and let it stand 5 minutes so the onion softens into the potato.

entries.title: Axone Pork
entries.snippet: naga pork belly stewed to spoon-softness with fermented funk and raw chilli heat
entries.text: axone pork northeast indian naga pork belly stewed to spoon-softness with fermented funk and raw chilli heat gluten-free dairy-free nut-free pork dried fish dried red chillies green chilli ginger garlic onion tomato bamboo shoot (fermented or fresh) spring onion salt water put the pork cubes in a heavy dry pot over medium heat with 2 tbsp of the water and cook 10 minutes, turning, until the fat has rendered and the cubes are browning in their own fat. add the onion, garlic and half the ginger and fry 5 minutes in the rendered fat, until the onion has gone soft and translucent. stir in the torn dried chillies and the roasted dried fish and fry 2 minutes, until the whole pot smells sharp and savoury. add the tomato, if using, and cook 3 minutes until it breaks down. pour in the rest of the water, add salt, cover and simmer very gently 45 minutes. check at 30 minutes and add a splash if it looks dry. add the bamboo shoot and the green chillies and simmer uncovered 10 minutes more. the pork is ready when a piece of skin gives completely under a spoon and the gravy has reduced to a thick, glossy few centimetres in the base. stir in the remaining ginger julienne and the spring onion, rest 5 minutes off the heat, and serve with plain sticky rice.

entries.title: Bai
entries.snippet: the mizo pot of greens and pumpkin, barely seasoned and softened with an alkaline pinch
entries.text: bai northeast indian the mizo pot of greens and pumpkin, barely seasoned and softened with an alkaline pinch vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic mustard greens (sarson) pumpkin french beans bamboo shoot (fermented or fresh) colocasia (arbi) baking soda green chilli ginger salt water bring the water to a boil in a wide pot with the salt, slit chillies and ginger. add the colocasia, if using, and boil 10 minutes — it takes longer than everything else and must be cooked right through. add the pumpkin and boil 6 minutes, until the edges have just started to soften. add the beans and bamboo shoot and cook 4 minutes. pile in the mustard greens, push them under the liquid and cook 4 minutes, until they have collapsed and turned dark. stir in the baking soda and simmer 3 minutes more. the greens will soften noticeably and the broth thickens a little. crush a few pieces of pumpkin against the side of the pot to thicken the liquid, taste for salt, and serve hot with rice and a chilli chutney.

entries.title: Chamthong
entries.snippet: the manipuri everyday vegetable stew, clear and light and lifted by fermented fish
entries.text: chamthong northeast indian the manipuri everyday vegetable stew, clear and light and lifted by fermented fish pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free pumpkin potato french beans cabbage amaranth greens (chaulai) dried fish onion ginger green chilli spring onion neutral oil salt water dry-roast the dried fish 3 minutes over low heat until brittle and toasty, then break it into rough pieces. bring the water to a boil in a wide pot with the onion, ginger, green chillies, roasted fish and salt. boil 5 minutes. add the potato and pumpkin and boil 8 minutes, uncovered, until the potato is nearly done. add the beans and cook 4 minutes. add the cabbage and cook 3 minutes, until it has just wilted but still has a bite. stir in the amaranth greens and the tablespoon of oil and cook 2 minutes more. taste for salt, scatter over the spring onion and serve hot in bowls alongside rice.

entries.title: Doh Khleh
entries.snippet: khasi pork salad — boiled meat tossed hot with onion, chilli and a lot of lemon
entries.text: doh khleh northeast indian khasi pork salad — boiled meat tossed hot with onion, chilli and a lot of lemon gluten-free dairy-free nut-free pork onion green chilli ginger lemon / lime black pepper sesame seeds coriander leaves (cilantro) bay leaf salt water bring the water to a boil with the bay leaf and a generous tablespoon of salt, lower in the pork and simmer 35 minutes. test it with a skewer — it should go in easily but the meat should still hold together, not shred. meanwhile toss the sliced onion with a big pinch of salt and leave it in a bowl for 20 minutes. roast the sesame in a dry pan 2 minutes, until it pops and smells toasted, then grind it coarsely. lift the pork out, rest it 5 minutes, then cut it into 1.5cm dice, fat and all. while it is still warm, toss the pork with the onion and any liquid in its bowl, the ginger, green chilli and crushed black pepper. add the lemon juice and check the salt — the boiling water has seasoned the meat already, so taste before adding more. fold in the ground sesame and coriander and serve at room temperature, on its own or with plain rice.

entries.title: Eromba
entries.snippet: manipuri mash of boiled vegetables, fierce chilli and fermented fish, eaten with rice
entries.text: eromba northeast indian manipuri mash of boiled vegetables, fierce chilli and fermented fish, eaten with rice pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free potato eggplant / brinjal french beans dried fish dried red chillies spring onion coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water dry-roast the dried fish in a small pan over low heat for 3 minutes, turning, until it smells toasty and goes brittle. crumble it and set aside. roast the dried red chillies in the same pan 40 seconds a side, until they darken and puff slightly. pound them to a coarse paste with a pinch of salt. boil the potato in the water for 8 minutes. add the eggplant and beans and boil 8 minutes more, until everything is completely tender and the potato is starting to fall apart. drain, keeping about 100ml of the cooking water. mash the vegetables roughly in the pot with the back of a ladle, leaving some lumps. work in the crumbled fish, the chilli paste and salt, adding the reserved water a spoon at a time until it is thick and scoopable. fold in the spring onion and coriander off the heat and serve at room temperature with hot rice.

entries.title: Hanhor Mangkho
entries.snippet: assamese duck stewed slowly with ash gourd, peppery and lean rather than creamy
entries.text: hanhor mangkho northeast indian assamese duck stewed slowly with ash gourd, peppery and lean rather than creamy gluten-free dairy-free nut-free duck ash gourd (petha) mustard oil onion ginger garlic black pepper bay leaf cinnamon cloves black cardamom turmeric powder green chilli salt water put the duck pieces in a dry heavy pot over medium heat and cook 6 minutes, turning, until fat pools in the base. pour that fat off and set the duck aside. heat the mustard oil in the same pot until it smokes, cool it a minute, then fry the bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves and black cardamom for 30 seconds until fragrant. add the sliced onion and cook 12 minutes over medium heat, until deep gold and shrunk to a third of its volume. stir in the ginger and garlic paste and fry 3 minutes, until the raw smell goes and the oil starts to separate at the edges. add the turmeric and crushed black pepper, stir for 20 seconds, then return the duck and toss to coat every piece. fry the duck in the masala 8 minutes, scraping the base as it catches, until the pieces are browned all over. pour in the hot water, add salt, cover and simmer very gently 45 minutes, until a skewer goes into the thigh with no resistance. add the ash gourd and green chillies and simmer uncovered 15 minutes more, until the gourd is translucent and the gravy has reduced to a coating consistency. rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Jadoh
entries.snippet: khasi rice cooked through with pork, ginger and black pepper, meghalaya's one-pot meal
entries.text: jadoh northeast indian khasi rice cooked through with pork, ginger and black pepper, meghalaya's one-pot meal gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) pork onion ginger garlic black pepper turmeric powder bay leaf green chilli neutral oil spring onion salt water heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the diced pork over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, until it has rendered its fat and the edges are browned and crisp. add the bay leaves and sliced onion and cook 8 minutes in the pork fat, until the onion is gold and sticky. stir in the ginger and garlic and fry 2 minutes, until the raw edge has gone. add the turmeric and crushed black pepper and stir for 30 seconds. tip in the drained rice and toss gently for 3 minutes, until every grain is coated and glossy and the rice smells toasted. pour in the hot water, add the green chillies and salt, and bring to a fast boil. as soon as the water level drops to the surface of the rice, cover tightly, drop the heat to its lowest and cook 12 minutes undisturbed. take it off the heat and rest, still covered, 10 minutes. fluff with a fork, scatter over the spring onion and serve.

entries.title: Masor Tenga
entries.snippet: assam's daily sour fish curry, thin and lemon-bright rather than rich
entries.text: masor tenga northeast indian assam's daily sour fish curry, thin and lemon-bright rather than rich pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) mustard oil tomato fenugreek seeds (methi) turmeric powder green chilli potato lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat the mustard oil in a wide pan until it smokes, take it off the heat for a minute, then fry the fish steaks 2 minutes a side until the edges are golden. lift them out onto a plate. in the same oil, crackle the fenugreek seeds for about 10 seconds, until they darken a shade and smell nutty. slide in the potato wedges and fry 4 minutes, until the cut edges look translucent. add the tomato, the rest of the turmeric, the slit chillies and salt. cook 5 minutes, pressing the tomato with the back of the spoon, until it slumps and gives up its water. pour in the water, bring to a boil and simmer 10 minutes uncovered, until the potato gives easily to a knife. slide the fish back in, spoon broth over each piece and simmer 4 minutes more. shake the pan rather than stirring. take the pan off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and coriander, and let it sit 5 minutes before serving over plain rice.

entries.title: Momos
entries.snippet: Steamed dumplings with a juicy filling, eaten with a fiery tomato-chilli chutney
entries.text: momos northeast indian steamed dumplings with a juicy filling, eaten with a fiery tomato-chilli chutney dairy-free nut-free plain flour (maida) chicken cabbage onion spring onion garlic ginger black pepper dried red chillies tomato neutral oil salt knead the flour with water and a pinch of salt into a firm, smooth dough. rest 30 minutes covered. mix the filling ingredients with the oil and pepper. salt it only when you are ready to fill. roll the dough very thin and cut 8cm rounds, keeping the edges thinner than the centre. place a spoon of filling in each, then pleat and seal into a half-moon or a gathered purse. steam in a greased steamer for 10-12 minutes. the wrappers turn translucent and stop looking floury. for the chutney, boil the tomatoes and dried chillies, then blend with garlic and salt. serve alongside.

entries.title: Muya Awandru
entries.snippet: tripura's oil-free bamboo shoot pot, thickened with rice flour and pungent with dried fish
entries.text: muya awandru northeast indian tripura's oil-free bamboo shoot pot, thickened with rice flour and pungent with dried fish pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free bamboo shoot (fermented or fresh) dried fish rice flour potato french beans green chilli ginger garlic coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water rinse the bamboo shoot twice, cover with fresh water, boil 5 minutes and drain. dry-roast the dried fish in a small pan over low heat 3 minutes, until brittle and toasty, then break it into pieces. bring the 800ml of water to a boil with the crushed ginger, garlic, green chillies, roasted fish and salt. boil 5 minutes so the broth takes on the flavours. add the drained bamboo shoot and the potato and simmer 12 minutes, uncovered. add the beans and cook 5 minutes, until the potato is soft enough to break with a spoon. stir the rice flour into 4 tbsp cold water until completely smooth, with no dry specks. pour the slurry into the simmering pot in a thin stream, stirring the whole time, and cook 4 minutes until the liquid turns glossy and coats the back of a spoon. taste for salt and heat, stir in the coriander and serve hot with plain rice.

entries.title: Naga Smoked Pork with Bamboo Shoot
entries.snippet: Smoked pork simmered with fermented bamboo shoot and raja mircha
entries.text: naga smoked pork with bamboo shoot northeast indian smoked pork simmered with fermented bamboo shoot and raja mircha gluten-free dairy-free nut-free pork bamboo shoot (fermented or fresh) green chilli ginger garlic onion tomato coriander leaves (cilantro) salt rinse the fermented bamboo shoot in two changes of water and drain. put the smoked pork in a pot with the ginger, garlic, chillies and just enough water to cover. bring to a boil. simmer covered 45-60 minutes until the pork is tender and the water has reduced by half. add the bamboo shoot and the onion and tomato if using, and cook a further 15 minutes. season with salt only at the end; smoked pork is already salty. serve with plain rice and a raw chilli on the side.

entries.title: Omita Khar
entries.snippet: the alkaline assamese opener — raw papaya simmered soft, plain and cleansing
entries.text: omita khar northeast indian the alkaline assamese opener — raw papaya simmered soft, plain and cleansing vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free raw green papaya baking soda mustard oil whole urad (sabut urad) green chilli turmeric powder coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat the mustard oil in a heavy pan until it smokes, then let it cool for a minute. fry the drained urad 2 minutes until deep gold and lift it out with a slotted spoon. keep it for the end. drop in the slit chillies and let them blister 30 seconds. add the papaya, turmeric and salt and toss 3 minutes, until the cut edges look glassy. pour in the water, cover and simmer 12 minutes, until a fork goes through a cube with no resistance. stir in the baking soda and simmer uncovered 5 minutes. it will foam up and settle, and the liquid turns faintly silky. crush four or five cubes against the side of the pan to thicken the broth, then scatter over the fried urad and coriander and serve at once.

entries.title: Singju
entries.snippet: manipur's raw-vegetable salad bound with roasted gram flour and loud with chilli
entries.text: singju northeast indian manipur's raw-vegetable salad bound with roasted gram flour and loud with chilli pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free cabbage radish (mooli) spring onion besan (gram flour) sesame seeds dried fish dried red chillies coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime salt dry-roast the besan over low heat for 4 minutes, stirring constantly, until it turns a shade darker and smells nutty. tip it straight out of the pan. roast the sesame in the same pan 2 minutes until the seeds start popping, then grind them coarsely. roast the dried red chillies 40 seconds a side until they darken, and pound them coarse. roast the dried fish 3 minutes over low heat until brittle, then crumble it fine. toss the cabbage, radish and spring onion in a wide bowl with the salt and leave 5 minutes. squeeze the vegetables gently with your hands and pour off any water that has come out. scatter over the roasted besan, ground sesame, crumbled fish and pounded chilli, and mix with your fingers until every shred is coated and the flour has stopped looking powdery. add the lemon juice and coriander, toss once more and serve immediately as a side or an evening snack.

entries.title: Thukpa
entries.snippet: sikkim's hand-torn noodle soup, chicken broth thick with vegetables and pepper
entries.text: thukpa northeast indian sikkim's hand-torn noodle soup, chicken broth thick with vegetables and pepper dairy-free nut-free plain flour (maida) chicken onion garlic ginger tomato carrot cabbage spinach spring onion black pepper turmeric powder red chilli powder neutral oil coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water mix the maida with 1/2 tsp salt and enough water — about 120ml — to make a firm, slightly stiff dough. knead 8 minutes until smooth, then cover and rest 30 minutes. heat the oil in a large pot and fry the onion, garlic and ginger 5 minutes over medium heat, until the onion is soft and the garlic smells sweet. add the chicken strips and fry 5 minutes, until they have lost their pink and picked up a little colour at the edges. stir in the turmeric, chilli powder and crushed black pepper for 20 seconds, then add the tomato and cook 5 minutes until it collapses. pour in the 1.2 litres of water, add salt, and simmer 15 minutes with the lid ajar. while it simmers, roll the rested dough out to about 2mm and cut or tear it into ribbons roughly 2cm wide and 10cm long. dust them with flour and keep them separate. add the carrot to the simmering broth and cook 3 minutes. drop the noodles in a few at a time, stirring so they do not clump, and boil 4 minutes until they float and turn from chalky to translucent. add the cabbage and spinach and cook 2 minutes more, until the spinach has just wilted. taste for salt and pepper, ladle into deep bowls and finish with spring onion and coriander.

entries.title: Aloo Potala Rasa
entries.snippet: potato and pointed gourd in a thin, cumin-scented tomato gravy, made without onion or garlic
entries.text: aloo potala rasa odia potato and pointed gourd in a thin, cumin-scented tomato gravy, made without onion or garlic vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic pointed gourd (parwal) potato tomato ginger green chilli cumin seeds bay leaf turmeric powder cumin powder (jeera) coriander powder red chilli powder garam masala mustard oil salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then lower the flame for 30 seconds. fry the halved pointed gourd on medium for 5 minutes, turning, until blistered and lightly browned. lift out and set aside. in the same oil add the bay leaf and cumin seeds and let them sizzle 15 seconds. add the grated ginger and slit green chillies and fry 1 minute. add the potato quarters and fry 4 minutes until the edges are golden. pour in the tomato puree with the turmeric, cumin powder, coriander powder, chilli powder and salt. fry 6-8 minutes until the oil beads at the edges. add the water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 12 minutes until the potato is tender. return the fried pointed gourd and simmer uncovered 5 minutes. the gravy should stay thin — this is a rasa, not a thick curry. stir in the garam masala, scatter the coriander leaves and rest 5 minutes off the heat before serving with rice.

entries.title: Besara
entries.snippet: mixed vegetables in a sharp ground-mustard gravy, pungent enough to make your eyes water
entries.text: besara odia mixed vegetables in a sharp ground-mustard gravy, pungent enough to make your eyes water vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free mustard seeds garlic green chilli potato eggplant / brinjal pumpkin raw banana / plantain drumstick (moringa pod) panch phoron dried red chillies turmeric powder mustard oil salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) grind the soaked mustard seeds, garlic, 2 green chillies and a pinch of salt to a smooth paste with 4 tbsp water. set aside. heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then lower the flame for 30 seconds. add the panch phoron and broken dried red chillies. when the seeds pop and the chillies darken, about 20 seconds, add the slit green chilli. add the potato and raw banana and fry 3 minutes, stirring, until the surfaces turn matte. add the pumpkin, eggplant and drumstick with the turmeric and salt. fry 2 minutes more. pour in the water, bring to a boil, cover and simmer 12 minutes until the potato is nearly tender. lower the flame to its weakest setting and stir in the mustard paste. do not let it boil hard from here on. simmer uncovered on low for 6-8 minutes, until the raw smell of the mustard has gone and the gravy coats a spoon. taste for salt, stir in the coriander leaves and take off the heat. rest 5 minutes before serving with rice.

entries.title: Chhena Poda
entries.snippet: Odisha's baked cheesecake: fresh chhena and sugar caramelised until the top is almost burnt
entries.text: chhena poda odia odisha's baked cheesecake: fresh chhena and sugar caramelised until the top is almost burnt vegetarian milk lemon / lime sugar rava / sooji (semolina) green cardamom cashews raisins (kishmish) ghee sugar curdle the milk with lemon juice, strain through muslin and rinse briefly. hang only 20 minutes — it should stay moist. knead the chhena smooth, then work in the sugar, rava, cardamom, nuts and raisins. rest 15 minutes so the rava swells. caramelise the 2 tbsp sugar in a ghee-greased tin and let it set at the bottom. pour in the batter and bake at 180c for 50-60 minutes, until the top is deep brown to nearly black and a skewer comes out clean. cool completely in the tin — at least 2 hours — before turning out. serve at room temperature in wedges.

entries.title: Chhena Tarkari
entries.snippet: soft fresh cheese in a light gingered tomato gravy, no onion, no garlic, straight out of the temple kitchen
entries.text: chhena tarkari odia soft fresh cheese in a light gingered tomato gravy, no onion, no garlic, straight out of the temple kitchen vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic paneer tomato ginger green chilli cumin seeds bay leaf turmeric powder cumin powder (jeera) coriander powder garam masala ghee milk sugar salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) heat the ghee in a kadhai and add the bay leaf and cumin seeds. they should sizzle on contact and smell toasty in about 15 seconds. add the grated ginger and slit green chillies and fry 1 minute, until the raw ginger smell lifts. pour in the tomato puree with the turmeric, cumin powder and coriander powder. stand back — it will spit. fry the puree on medium heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring, until it darkens to brick red and the ghee separates at the edges. add the water and salt, bring to a boil, then simmer 5 minutes. slide in the paneer cubes, add the sugar, and simmer very gently for 6 minutes, spooning gravy over them. stir in the milk and the garam masala and warm through for 1 minute without boiling. take off the heat, scatter the coriander leaves and rest 5 minutes before serving with rice or roti.

entries.title: Chungdi Malai
entries.snippet: prawns simmered in coconut milk, mildly spiced and faintly sweet, Odisha's most coaxing curry
entries.text: chungdi malai odia prawns simmered in coconut milk, mildly spiced and faintly sweet, odisha's most coaxing curry pescatarian gluten-free nut-free prawns coconut milk onion ginger garlic ghee bay leaf cinnamon green cardamom cloves turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder garam masala green chilli sugar salt heat 1 tbsp ghee in a kadhai and sear the prawns on high for 45 seconds a side, until they just turn pink. lift them out at once. add the remaining 2 tbsp ghee and drop in the bay leaves, cinnamon, cardamom and cloves. fry 30 seconds until fragrant. add the onion paste and fry on medium for 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until it turns pale gold and stops smelling raw. stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and cook 2 minutes more. add the turmeric, kashmiri chilli and salt with 2 tbsp water and fry 1 minute so the spices do not scorch. lower the flame and pour in the coconut milk. add the sugar and slit green chillies. simmer gently, uncovered, for 6-8 minutes until the gravy thickens enough to coat a spoon. return the prawns with any juices, add the garam masala, and simmer 2 minutes only. take off the heat and rest 5 minutes covered before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Dahi Pakhala
entries.snippet: Odia fermented rice in water with yogurt, eaten cold in the hot months
entries.text: dahi pakhala odia odia fermented rice in water with yogurt, eaten cold in the hot months vegetarian gluten-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) yogurt / dahi water ginger green chilli curry leaves mustard seeds dried red chillies asafoetida (hing) lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil salt put the cooled rice in a bowl, add the water and lightly crush some of the grains with your fingers to cloud the liquid. for the traditional version, this is where you leave it overnight. whisk the yogurt smooth and stir it through with salt, the ginger and green chilli. it should be soupy, not thick; add more water if needed. heat the oil in a small pan. splutter the mustard seeds, then add the dried chilli, curry leaves and asafoetida. pour the tempering over the pakhala, add a squeeze of lemon and scatter with coriander. chill at least 30 minutes before eating. serve with something fried and salty alongside; fried fish, badi chura or a simple potato bharta are the usual partners.

entries.title: Dalma
entries.snippet: Odia lentils simmered with vegetables, finished with roasted cumin and coconut
entries.text: dalma odia odia lentils simmered with vegetables, finished with roasted cumin and coconut vegetarian gluten-free nut-free toor dal (pigeon pea) raw banana / plantain pumpkin potato drumstick (moringa pod) tomato turmeric powder cumin seeds dried red chillies ginger coconut (fresh or desiccated) bay leaf ghee salt pressure cook the toor dal with turmeric, the ginger and 3 cups of water for 3 whistles, or simmer covered in a pot for about 35 minutes until completely soft. add the potato, raw banana, pumpkin and drumstick with a little more hot water and salt. cook a further 2 whistles, or 12-15 minutes in a pot, until the vegetables are tender but not collapsing. meanwhile, dry roast half the cumin seeds and one dried chilli in a small pan over medium heat until the cumin darkens a shade and smells toasty, about 90 seconds. cool, then grind to a coarse powder. heat the ghee in a small pan. add the bay leaf, the remaining cumin seeds and the remaining dried chilli. when the cumin sizzles and turns fragrant, pour the whole tempering into the dal. stir in the grated coconut and the roasted cumin powder. simmer 2 minutes so the flavours settle, then taste and adjust salt.

entries.title: Ghanta Tarkari
entries.snippet: a big pot of mixed vegetables and chana dal with coconut, cooked for festivals without onion or garlic
