entries.text: ghanta tarkari odia a big pot of mixed vegetables and chana dal with coconut, cooked for festivals without onion or garlic vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic chana dal pumpkin yam (suran) raw banana / plantain potato colocasia (arbi) drumstick (moringa pod) coconut (fresh or desiccated) cumin seeds panch phoron ginger green chilli bay leaf turmeric powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala ghee salt water boil the soaked chana dal in 400ml water with 1/2 tsp turmeric for 15 minutes, until it is just tender but still holds its shape. do not drain. meanwhile heat the ghee in a large kadhai and add the bay leaves, whole cumin seeds and panch phoron. let them crackle 20 seconds. add the remaining grated ginger and the slit green chillies and fry 1 minute. add the yam, colocasia and potato and fry 4 minutes until the cut faces turn golden. add the pumpkin, raw banana and drumstick with the remaining turmeric, the cumin powder and salt. toss 2 minutes. pour in the remaining 500ml water, bring to a boil, cover and simmer 15 minutes. tip in the boiled chana dal with its water and the coconut-cumin paste. stir gently from the bottom. simmer uncovered 10 minutes until the gravy thickens and the yam is completely soft. mash a few pieces of pumpkin against the pan to bind the gravy, then stir in the garam masala. scatter the reserved fresh coconut over the top and rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with rice.

entries.title: Khaja
entries.snippet: layered flaky pastry fried and dipped in sugar syrup, sold in stacks outside the Puri temple
entries.text: khaja odia layered flaky pastry fried and dipped in sugar syrup, sold in stacks outside the puri temple vegetarian plain flour (maida) ghee rice flour sugar water green cardamom salt neutral oil rub the melted ghee and salt into the maida for 3 minutes, then add the 150ml water a little at a time to make a firm, tight dough. knead 6 minutes. cover with a damp cloth and rest 30 minutes. beat the 3 tbsp ghee with the rice flour to a smooth, spreadable white paste. divide the dough in two. roll each half into a thin rectangle about 2mm thick and spread the sata paste evenly right to the edges. roll each rectangle up tightly into a log, pressing as you go to expel air pockets. cut each log into 2cm slices. lay each slice cut-side up and press it flat with your palm, then roll very lightly into an oval about 8cm long — you should see the spiral of layers on the face. boil the 350g sugar with 200ml water and the cardamom for 8-10 minutes to a one-thread syrup, then keep it warm on the lowest flame. heat the oil in a kadhai to low-medium — a scrap of dough should take a full 30 seconds to float up. fry the khaja in small batches for 7-9 minutes, turning often, until they are pale gold and the layers have visibly fanned open. drain briefly, then dip each hot khaja in the warm syrup for 30 seconds, turning once, and lift onto a rack. leave to set for 30 minutes until the syrup coating turns matte and crisp.

entries.title: Macha Besara
entries.snippet: rohu steaks in a hot, sour ground-mustard gravy, the Sunday fish curry of coastal Odisha
entries.text: macha besara odia rohu steaks in a hot, sour ground-mustard gravy, the sunday fish curry of coastal odisha pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) mustard seeds garlic green chilli tomato panch phoron turmeric powder red chilli powder mustard oil salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) grind the soaked mustard, garlic, green chillies and a pinch of salt to a smooth paste with 4 tbsp water. set aside. heat 4 tbsp mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes. fry the turmeric-rubbed fish in one layer, 3 minutes a side, until a light crust forms. lift the fish out onto a plate. pour off all but about 1 tbsp of the oil. add the panch phoron to the hot oil and let it crackle 20 seconds, then add the sliced garlic and 2 slit green chillies. add the chopped tomato with 1/2 tsp turmeric, the chilli powder and salt. cook 6 minutes, mashing, until the tomato collapses and the oil separates. pour in the water and bring to a boil, then simmer 5 minutes. drop the flame to its lowest and stir in the mustard paste. simmer uncovered 5 minutes without letting it boil. slide the fried fish back in, spoon gravy over each piece, and simmer 4 minutes more. take off the heat, scatter the coriander leaves and rest 10 minutes before serving. the fish keeps absorbing gravy as it stands.

entries.title: Mahura
entries.snippet: yam, pumpkin and colocasia in mustard with crumbled badi, the festival curry of western Odisha
entries.text: mahura odia yam, pumpkin and colocasia in mustard with crumbled badi, the festival curry of western odisha vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic yam (suran) pumpkin colocasia (arbi) raw banana / plantain potato urad dal (black gram) mustard seeds green chilli cumin seeds panch phoron turmeric powder jaggery mustard oil salt water heat 1 tbsp mustard oil and fry the crushed badi over medium heat for 2 minutes until deep brown and smelling nutty. lift out and reserve. add the remaining 2 tbsp oil to the same kadhai and heat until it smokes, then lower the flame. add the panch phoron and let it crackle 20 seconds. add the yam, colocasia, potato and raw banana. fry 4 minutes, turning, until the cut faces are lightly golden. add the pumpkin, slit green chilli, turmeric and salt and toss for 2 minutes. pour in the water, bring to a boil, cover and simmer 15 minutes until the yam is tender to a knife. turn the flame to its lowest, stir in the mustard paste and the jaggery, and simmer uncovered 8 minutes. return the fried badi, stir once and simmer 3 minutes more so they drink up the gravy but keep their bite. rest 5 minutes off the heat before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Rasabali
entries.snippet: fried chhena discs soaked in thick cardamom milk, the offering sweet of Kendrapara
entries.text: rasabali odia fried chhena discs soaked in thick cardamom milk, the offering sweet of kendrapara vegetarian nut-free paneer milk sugar rava / sooji (semolina) green cardamom black pepper ghee water saffron reduce the 1.5 litres of milk in a heavy pan over medium-low heat, scraping the sides down, for about 30 minutes until it has halved and thickened to a pourable rabri. stir 100g sugar, the crushed cardamom, the pepper and the saffron milk into the reduced milk. simmer 3 minutes and take off the heat. separately dissolve 50g sugar in 300ml water and bring to a boil to make a thin syrup. keep it warm. knead the crumbled paneer with the rava for 8 minutes until smooth and dough-like, with no grains visible. rest 10 minutes covered. divide into 12 balls and flatten each into a disc about 5cm across and 1cm thick, with smooth unbroken edges. heat the ghee in a kadhai to medium-low — a scrap of dough should rise slowly and take 20 seconds to colour. fry the discs in batches, 4-5 minutes, turning once, until they are an even deep reddish-brown. they will puff slightly. drop each fried disc straight into the warm syrup and leave 10 minutes to soften and swell. lift the discs out, squeeze them very gently against the side of the bowl to shed excess syrup, and slide them into the warm rabri. rest at least 2 hours so the discs drink the milk all the way through. serve cool, not chilled.

entries.title: Saga Bhaja
entries.snippet: amaranth greens stir-fried hard in mustard oil with garlic and dried chilli, done in ten minutes
entries.text: saga bhaja odia amaranth greens stir-fried hard in mustard oil with garlic and dried chilli, done in ten minutes vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free amaranth greens (chaulai) garlic dried red chillies green chilli mustard seeds turmeric powder mustard oil salt heat the mustard oil in a wide kadhai until it smokes, then lower the flame for 30 seconds. add the mustard seeds and let them pop, about 15 seconds. add the sliced garlic and broken red chillies and fry until the garlic is pale gold at the edges, about 1 minute. throw in the chopped stems and the slit green chillies and fry 2 minutes on high. add the leaves in two handfuls, letting the first wilt before the second goes in. keep the flame high. add the turmeric and stir-fry 4-5 minutes uncovered, tossing often, until the water the leaves throw off has cooked away. salt to taste, toss once more and take off the heat immediately.

entries.title: Saja Pakhala
entries.snippet: same-day watered rice with lemon, ginger and a mustard tempering, eaten cool on the hottest afternoons
entries.text: saja pakhala odia same-day watered rice with lemon, ginger and a mustard tempering, eaten cool on the hottest afternoons vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic rice (short/medium grain) water lemon / lime ginger green chilli curry leaves mustard seeds cumin seeds mustard oil salt coriander leaves (cilantro) boil the washed rice in 1.5 litres of water for 12-14 minutes, uncovered, until the grains are soft and just starting to swell open. drain off the excess starch water into a bowl and keep it. spread the rice in a wide dish. let the rice cool to room temperature, about 40 minutes. do not rush it in the fridge. add 700ml cold water plus the reserved starch water to the rice, along with the salt. it should be soupy, with the grains floating loose. stir in the lemon juice, half the julienned ginger and the slit green chillies. heat the mustard oil in a small pan until it smokes, then lower the flame for 30 seconds. add the mustard seeds, cumin seeds and curry leaves. when the mustard pops and the leaves crisp, about 20 seconds, pour the whole tempering over the rice. stir once, scatter over the remaining ginger and the coriander leaves, and let it sit 15 minutes before eating.

entries.title: Santula
entries.snippet: barely-spiced mixed vegetables stewed in their own water, the plainest good thing in an Odia kitchen
entries.text: santula odia barely-spiced mixed vegetables stewed in their own water, the plainest good thing in an odia kitchen vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic potato eggplant / brinjal pumpkin raw banana / plantain drumstick (moringa pod) raw green papaya tomato green chilli panch phoron turmeric powder mustard oil salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it just smokes, then lower the flame and let it settle for 30 seconds. add the panch phoron and let it crackle for about 20 seconds, until the fenugreek darkens a shade. add the slit green chillies and the potato and raw banana. stir 2 minutes until the edges look chalky. add the pumpkin, eggplant, papaya, drumstick and tomato with the turmeric and salt. toss to coat. pour in the water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes. uncover and check the potato with a knife tip; it should give with no resistance. simmer uncovered 5 minutes more to thicken. mash three or four pieces of pumpkin against the side of the pan and stir through. that is what makes the broth cling. take off the heat, stir in the coriander leaves and rest 5 minutes before serving with rice.

entries.title: Tomato Khajuri Khatta
entries.snippet: sweet-sour tomato and date relish tempered with panch phoron, served at the end of every Odia meal
entries.text: tomato khajuri khatta odia sweet-sour tomato and date relish tempered with panch phoron, served at the end of every odia meal vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic tomato dates raisins (kishmish) jaggery panch phoron dried red chillies turmeric powder mustard oil salt water lemon / lime heat the mustard oil in a small pan until it smokes, then lower the flame for 30 seconds. add the panch phoron and the broken red chillies. let them crackle for 20 seconds until the fenugreek turns tan. tip in the chopped tomato with the turmeric and salt. stir once and cover. cook covered on medium for 8 minutes, until the tomatoes have completely collapsed. add the dates, raisins and water. simmer uncovered 6 minutes so the dates plump and soften. stir in the jaggery and cook 6-8 minutes more, stirring now and then, until the mixture is glossy and a spoon dragged through leaves a track that closes slowly. taste. add the lemon juice if it needs sharpening, and adjust salt. cool to room temperature before serving alongside rice and dal.

entries.title: Akuri
entries.snippet: soft-scrambled eggs loose with onion, chilli and coriander, eaten on buttered pav
entries.text: akuri parsi soft-scrambled eggs loose with onion, chilli and coriander, eaten on buttered pav vegetarian gluten-free nut-free eggs onion tomato green chilli ginger coriander leaves (cilantro) butter milk turmeric powder cumin powder (jeera) black pepper salt beat the eggs with the milk, black pepper and salt just until streaky — about 15 strokes. melt the butter in a small kadhai over medium-low heat until it foams but does not brown. add the onion and cook 4 minutes until soft and translucent, with no colour on it at all. stir in the ginger and green chilli and cook 1 minute until fragrant. add the turmeric and cumin powder, then the tomato, and cook 2 minutes until the tomato slumps but still holds shape. drop the heat to its lowest setting and pour in the eggs. push the eggs slowly from the edges to the centre with a flat spoon for 3 to 4 minutes, forming large soft curds. fold through the coriander leaves off the heat and serve immediately on buttered pav or toast.

entries.title: Berry Pulao
entries.snippet: saffron rice layered over spiced chicken, studded with sharp sour-sweet dried fruit
entries.text: berry pulao parsi saffron rice layered over spiced chicken, studded with sharp sour-sweet dried fruit gluten-free basmati rice chicken yogurt / dahi onion ginger garlic green chilli mint coriander leaves (cilantro) garam masala cinnamon cloves green cardamom bay leaf black pepper saffron milk ghee cashews raisins (kishmish) dried apricots (khubani) lemon / lime salt water fry the sliced onion in 4 tbsp ghee over medium heat for 15 minutes until dark brown and crisp, drain on paper, and set a third aside for the garnish. fry the cashews in the same ghee for 1 minute until golden and set aside. add the marinated chicken to the pan with two thirds of the fried onion and cook uncovered 20 minutes over medium heat until the yogurt tightens around the meat. stir in half the mint and coriander and cook 3 minutes more, then set the chicken aside off the heat. bring 3 litres of water to a rolling boil with the cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, bay leaf, black pepper and 2 tbsp salt. add the drained rice and boil 4 to 5 minutes, until a grain crushes between your fingers but still has a hard white core. drain the rice immediately and spread it on a tray to stop the cooking. layer the chicken in a heavy pot, then the rice, then the lemon-soaked raisins and apricots, the reserved fried onion, cashews and the rest of the herbs. drizzle over the saffron milk and the remaining 1 tbsp ghee, seal the pot with a tight lid or foil, and cook on the lowest heat 20 minutes, or in a 160c oven for 25. rest 10 minutes sealed, then open and lift the pulao from the sides with a flat spoon so the layers stay visible.

entries.title: Dhansak
entries.snippet: sunday mutton simmered into a purée of four dals and gourds, sour and gently hot
entries.text: dhansak parsi sunday mutton simmered into a purée of four dals and gourds, sour and gently hot gluten-free dairy-free nut-free mutton / lamb toor dal (pigeon pea) masoor dal (red lentil) chana dal moong dal pumpkin eggplant / brinjal fenugreek leaves (methi) onion tomato garlic ginger green chilli coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) turmeric powder red chilli powder garam masala cinnamon cloves green cardamom black pepper tamarind jaggery mint coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil salt water pressure cook the drained dals with the pumpkin, eggplant, methi leaves, chopped onion, tomato, turmeric and 1 litre of water for 5 whistles, about 20 minutes. meanwhile heat 3 tbsp oil in a heavy pan and brown the mutton in two batches over high heat, 5 minutes a batch. pound the garlic, ginger and green chilli to a coarse paste and fry it in the same pan for 2 minutes, until the raw smell lifts. add the cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, black pepper, coriander powder, cumin powder, chilli powder and garam masala and fry 90 seconds, splashing in 2 tbsp water when it catches. return the mutton, add 200ml water, cover and simmer 45 minutes until a knife slides into the meat with no resistance. cool the dal mixture slightly, fish out any large spice pieces, and blend to a smooth, pourable purée. pour the purée over the mutton, add the tamarind extract, jaggery and salt, and simmer uncovered 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes. taste and balance — it should land sour first, then sweet, then hot. add tamarind or jaggery a teaspoon at a time. fry the sliced onion in the remaining 2 tbsp oil until dark brown and crisp, about 10 minutes over medium heat. rest the dhansak 10 minutes off the heat, then top with the fried onion, mint and coriander leaves.

entries.title: Kolmi no Patio
entries.snippet: prawns in a thick red tamarind masala that is fiery, sour and sweet at once
entries.text: kolmi no patio parsi prawns in a thick red tamarind masala that is fiery, sour and sweet at once pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free prawns onion tomato garlic ginger dried red chillies kashmiri chilli powder cumin seeds turmeric powder coriander powder tamarind jaggery vinegar curry leaves coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil salt grind the soaked chillies, garlic, ginger, cumin seeds, kashmiri chilli and 2 tbsp of the soaking water to a smooth red paste. heat the oil in a kadhai and fry the curry leaves for 20 seconds until they crackle and go translucent. add the onion and cook 10 minutes over medium heat until soft and pale gold. add the ground masala and fry 6 to 8 minutes, stirring constantly, until the oil pools around the edges and the raw garlic smell disappears. stir in the turmeric, coriander powder and tomato and cook 6 minutes until the tomato has collapsed completely. add the tamarind extract, jaggery, vinegar and salt and simmer 5 minutes to a thick, glossy masala. taste and balance the three points — sour, sweet, hot. it should be assertive on all three, since the prawns will mute it. slide in the prawns, stir to coat, and cook 3 to 4 minutes only, until they curl and turn opaque. rest 5 minutes off the heat, scatter with coriander leaves, and serve with plain rice or rotli.

entries.title: Lagan nu Custard
entries.snippet: the dense baked wedding custard, caramel-topped and heavy with nutmeg and cardamom
entries.text: lagan nu custard parsi the dense baked wedding custard, caramel-topped and heavy with nutmeg and cardamom vegetarian gluten-free milk condensed milk eggs sugar green cardamom nutmeg rose water almonds pistachios ghee boil the milk in a wide heavy pan and simmer 30 minutes, stirring often, until reduced to about 600ml. stir in the condensed milk and sugar and simmer 5 minutes more, then take off the heat and cool to lukewarm. beat the eggs until just smooth, with no strands of white remaining. pour a ladle of the warm milk into the eggs while whisking, then repeat twice before adding the eggs back into the pan. whisk in the ground cardamom, nutmeg and rose water. strain the mixture through a fine sieve into a ghee-rubbed baking dish about 25cm across. scatter the slivered almonds and pistachios over the surface. bake at 160c for 45 to 55 minutes, until the edges are set and the centre wobbles like a soft jelly when nudged. if the top has not browned, run it under a hot grill for 2 minutes until patched with dark caramel spots. cool completely at room temperature, at least 3 hours, before cutting into squares.

entries.title: Papeta par Eeda
entries.snippet: eggs baked on a bed of soft spiced potatoes, the everyday parsi supper
entries.text: papeta par eeda parsi eggs baked on a bed of soft spiced potatoes, the everyday parsi supper vegetarian gluten-free nut-free potato eggs onion green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) turmeric powder cumin powder (jeera) red chilli powder black pepper ghee salt water heat the ghee in a wide kadhai and fry the sliced onion 6 minutes until soft and lightly golden. add the green chilli and cook 1 minute. stir in the turmeric, cumin powder and chilli powder and fry 30 seconds. add the potato matchsticks with 1 tsp salt and toss until every strand is coated yellow. sprinkle over 3 tbsp water, cover, and cook 12 to 14 minutes on low, shaking the pan every few minutes. uncover and check — a matchstick should give completely under a spoon but the mass should still be loose, not sticky. fold in half the coriander leaves, then flatten the potato into an even bed and make five shallow wells with the back of a spoon. crack one egg into each well, season with salt and black pepper, cover, and cook on the lowest heat 6 to 8 minutes. scatter the remaining coriander over and bring the pan straight to the table with pav or rotli.

entries.title: Patra ni Machhi
entries.snippet: pomfret packed in green coconut chutney and steamed in a leaf until it flakes
entries.text: patra ni machhi parsi pomfret packed in green coconut chutney and steamed in a leaf until it flakes pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) coconut (fresh or desiccated) coriander leaves (cilantro) mint green chilli garlic cumin seeds sugar lemon / lime vinegar turmeric powder salt blend the coconut, coriander, mint, green chilli, garlic, cumin seeds, sugar, turmeric, remaining lemon juice, vinegar and salt to a thick paste. taste the chutney and correct it now — it should be sharp, sweet and hot all at once, and it will taste milder once steamed. cut the softened banana leaf into rectangles roughly twice the size of each fillet. spread a spoon of chutney on the leaf, lay the fish on it, then blanket the fish with a thick layer of chutney on top and sides. fold the leaf over into a snug parcel and tie with kitchen string or secure with a toothpick. set the parcels in a steamer over rapidly boiling water, cover, and steam 12 minutes for fillets or 18 for whole fish. open one parcel at the edge and press the thickest part — the flesh should part into flakes with no translucent centre. rest the parcels 3 minutes off the heat, then serve them closed so each person opens their own.

entries.title: Ravo
entries.snippet: birthday-morning semolina pudding, soft and milky with cardamom and fried raisins
entries.text: ravo parsi birthday-morning semolina pudding, soft and milky with cardamom and fried raisins vegetarian rava / sooji (semolina) milk ghee sugar eggs green cardamom nutmeg raisins (kishmish) almonds rose water salt heat 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy pan and fry the raisins for 30 seconds until they puff, then lift them out. fry the slivered almonds in the same ghee for 45 seconds until pale gold and set them aside with the raisins. add the remaining ghee and the semolina and roast over low heat for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring constantly, until it smells nutty and turns the colour of pale sand. pour in the hot milk in a thin stream, whisking hard the whole time. add the pinch of salt and simmer 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until the semolina swells and the mixture coats the back of a spoon. stir in the sugar and cook 3 minutes more; it will loosen at first and then thicken again. take the pan off the heat, let it cool for 2 minutes, then whisk in the beaten egg quickly and return to very low heat for 2 minutes. stir in the cardamom, nutmeg and rose water, and thin with a splash of hot milk if it has gone past pourable. spoon into bowls, top with the fried raisins and almonds, and serve warm.

entries.title: Sali Boti
entries.snippet: mutton in a sweet-sour tomato gravy under a haystack of crisp potato straws
entries.text: sali boti parsi mutton in a sweet-sour tomato gravy under a haystack of crisp potato straws gluten-free dairy-free nut-free mutton / lamb onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder turmeric powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala vinegar jaggery dried apricots (khubani) potato neutral oil coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water pound the ginger and garlic to a smooth paste and use half for the marinade, keeping half for the pan. heat 4 tbsp oil and fry the sliced onion over medium heat for 15 minutes until evenly deep brown. add the reserved ginger-garlic paste and green chilli and fry 2 minutes. stir in the kashmiri chilli, chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder and fry 1 minute until the oil takes on colour. tip in the tomato purée and cook 12 minutes until the oil separates and pools at the edges. add the marinated mutton and sear 6 minutes, stirring, until every cube is coated and no pink shows. pour in 400ml water, cover, and simmer 45 minutes, or pressure cook 4 whistles, until the mutton is tender. stir in the jaggery, remaining vinegar, garam masala, soaked apricots and salt and simmer uncovered 10 minutes. drain and dry the potato straws thoroughly, then fry in 500ml hot oil in two batches for 3 minutes each until pale gold and crisp. drain the sali on paper, salt lightly, and pile over the mutton just before serving.

entries.title: Salli Marghi
entries.snippet: chicken in a tangy tomato-onion gravy crowned with matchstick potatoes
entries.text: salli marghi parsi chicken in a tangy tomato-onion gravy crowned with matchstick potatoes gluten-free dairy-free nut-free chicken onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala cinnamon cloves vinegar jaggery potato neutral oil coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat 3 tbsp oil with the cinnamon and cloves until the spices swell, about 40 seconds. add the sliced onion and fry 12 minutes over medium heat to a deep even brown. add the ginger-garlic paste and green chilli and fry 2 minutes until the raw edge is gone. stir in the turmeric, kashmiri chilli, chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder and fry 45 seconds. add the tomato and cook 10 minutes, mashing with the spoon, until it breaks down and the oil separates. add the marinated chicken and turn it in the masala over high heat for 5 minutes until it is sealed all over. pour in 300ml water, cover, and simmer 20 minutes until the chicken pulls easily from the bone. stir in the jaggery, remaining vinegar, garam masala and salt and simmer uncovered 5 minutes to a gravy that just coats a spoon. fry the dried potato matchsticks in 500ml hot oil in two batches, 3 minutes each, until pale gold, then drain and salt. scatter the coriander leaves over the chicken and heap the salli on top at the table.

entries.title: Aloo Gobi
entries.snippet: dry-cooked potato and cauliflower, browned at the edges and heavy on ginger
entries.text: aloo gobi punjabi dry-cooked potato and cauliflower, browned at the edges and heavy on ginger vegan vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free cauliflower potato onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli mustard oil cumin seeds turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder amchur (dry mango powder) garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) salt heat 3 tbsp of the oil in a wide kadhai until it shimmers and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds. fry the potato cubes on medium-high for 6 minutes, undisturbed for the first 3, until they are gold on several faces, then lift them out. add the cauliflower to the same pan with the remaining oil and fry 6 minutes until browned in patches. push the cauliflower aside, add the onion, and fry 5 minutes until soft and gold. stir in the grated ginger, garlic and green chillies and fry 90 seconds. add the turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder, stir 20 seconds, then add the tomato and 1 tsp salt. cook 6 minutes until the tomato has broken down into a coating masala rather than a gravy. return the potatoes, stir to coat everything, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 10 minutes, shaking the pan every few minutes. check that a knife slides into both potato and stalk with no resistance; give it 5 minutes more if not. uncover, stir in the amchur and garam masala, and cook 2 minutes to dry it off. finish with the julienned ginger and coriander and serve with roti.

entries.title: Aloo Paratha
entries.snippet: wholewheat flatbread stuffed with spiced potato and griddled in ghee
entries.text: aloo paratha punjabi wholewheat flatbread stuffed with spiced potato and griddled in ghee vegetarian nut-free atta (wholewheat flour) water potato onion green chilli ginger coriander leaves (cilantro) amchur (dry mango powder) cumin seeds red chilli powder garam masala carom seeds (ajwain) ghee butter salt mix the atta with 1/2 tsp salt and 1 tbsp ghee, then add the water gradually and knead 8 minutes to a soft, smooth dough. cover with a damp cloth and rest 30 minutes. mash the cold potatoes and mix in the onion, green chilli, ginger, coriander, amchur, crushed cumin, chilli powder, garam masala, ajwain and 1 tsp salt. taste the filling and correct the salt and sour — it should taste slightly over-seasoned on its own. divide dough and filling into 8 each, and roll both into balls. flatten a dough ball into a 4-inch disc, cup it in your palm, place a filling ball in the middle, and gather the edges over the top, pinching them shut. press the sealed ball flat, dust with flour, and roll gently to a 7-inch disc, working from the centre outward and turning as you go. lay it on a hot tawa and cook 60 seconds until the surface bubbles and the underside has pale spots. flip, brush the cooked side with ghee, and cook 60 seconds. flip once more, brush again, and press the edges down with a cloth until both sides are freckled deep brown, about 45 seconds. stack in a covered dish and serve hot with butter, yogurt and pickle.

entries.title: Amritsari Fish
entries.snippet: ajwain-spiked gram flour batter fried crisp around soft white fish
entries.text: amritsari fish punjabi ajwain-spiked gram flour batter fried crisp around soft white fish pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) besan (gram flour) rice flour ginger garlic carom seeds (ajwain) kashmiri chilli powder turmeric powder black pepper lemon / lime salt water neutral oil chaat masala rub the fish pieces with the lemon juice, 1/2 tsp salt and the turmeric, and set aside 10 minutes. whisk the besan, rice flour, ginger, garlic, crushed ajwain, kashmiri chilli, black pepper and remaining salt in a bowl. add the water a tablespoon at a time until you have a batter the thickness of double cream. fold the fish through the batter, cover, and rest 30 minutes in the fridge. heat the oil in a kadhai to 170c — a drop of batter should sink briefly, then rise and sizzle steadily. lower in 4 or 5 pieces at a time, without crowding, and fry 4 minutes until pale gold. lift onto the rack and let all the fish rest 5 minutes. raise the oil to 190c and fry the pieces a second time for 60 to 90 seconds until deep gold and crackling. drain on the rack, dust with chaat masala, and serve at once with lemon wedges and sliced onion.

entries.title: Baingan Bharta
entries.snippet: fire-roasted aubergine mashed rough with onion and tomato, smoky throughout
entries.text: baingan bharta punjabi fire-roasted aubergine mashed rough with onion and tomato, smoky throughout vegan vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free eggplant / brinjal onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli mustard oil cumin seeds turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) salt set the aubergines directly on a medium gas flame and roast 15 to 20 minutes, turning every few minutes with tongs. if you have no gas flame, roast at 240c for 45 minutes, turning twice, then blacken briefly under the grill. put the roasted aubergines in a covered bowl for 10 minutes — the steam loosens the skin. peel off every scrap of charred skin, then chop and mash the flesh roughly with a fork. heat the oil in a kadhai and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds. add the onion and fry on medium-high for 10 minutes until deep gold. stir in the ginger, minced garlic and green chillies and fry 2 minutes. add the tomato, turmeric, coriander powder, chilli powder and 1 tsp salt, and cook 10 minutes until the tomato disappears into a thick masala and oil separates. fold in the mashed aubergine and cook 8 minutes on medium, pressing and stirring, until the mixture pulls away from the sides of the pan. stir in the garam masala and most of the coriander, taste for salt, and finish with the rest of the coriander.

entries.title: Bhindi Masala
entries.snippet: sliced okra fried dry until it loses all its slime, then tossed with onion and amchur
entries.text: bhindi masala punjabi sliced okra fried dry until it loses all its slime, then tossed with onion and amchur vegan vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free okra / bhindi onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli neutral oil cumin seeds fennel seeds (saunf) turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder amchur (dry mango powder) garam masala salt coriander leaves (cilantro) heat 4 tbsp of the oil in a wide kadhai until it shimmers. add the okra in a single layer and fry on medium-high for 10 minutes, stirring only every 2 or 3 minutes. keep frying until the pieces are browned in patches and no thread follows the spoon, about 4 minutes more. lift the okra out onto a plate and set aside. add the last tablespoon of oil to the pan and crackle the cumin and crushed fennel for 20 seconds. add the onion and fry 7 minutes on medium-high until soft with brown edges. stir in the ginger, garlic and green chillies and fry 90 seconds. add the turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder, stir 20 seconds, then add the tomato wedges and 1 tsp salt. cook 5 minutes, just until the tomato softens but still holds its shape. return the okra, fold everything together gently, and cook 3 minutes uncovered. stir in the amchur and garam masala, scatter the coriander, and serve immediately.

entries.title: Butter Chicken
entries.snippet: Murgh makhani: charred chicken in a tomato and cream gravy, mild and fenugreek-scented
entries.text: butter chicken punjabi murgh makhani: charred chicken in a tomato and cream gravy, mild and fenugreek-scented gluten-free nut-free chicken yogurt / dahi ginger garlic kashmiri chilli powder garam masala tomato butter cream kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) green cardamom cashews sugar lemon / lime salt marinate the chicken with the yogurt, half the ginger and garlic, the kashmiri chilli, 1 tsp garam masala, lemon juice and salt. leave at least 30 minutes, ideally 4 hours refrigerated. grill, broil or pan-sear the chicken in a very hot pan until the edges char in places and it is just cooked. do not cook it through to dryness; it finishes in the sauce. set aside with any resting juices. simmer the tomatoes with the remaining ginger and garlic, the cardamom and a splash of water, covered, for 20 minutes until completely collapsed. blend the tomato mixture smooth with the soaked cashews if using, then pass it through a sieve. the sieve is what separates a silky makhani from a rustic curry. return the puree to the pan with the butter and cook 10 minutes over medium-low heat, stirring, until it darkens and thickens and the butter shows at the edges. add the chicken with its juices, the cream, the sugar and the remaining garam masala. simmer 5 minutes. crush the kasuri methi between your palms and stir it through. taste for salt and lemon.

entries.title: Chana Masala
entries.snippet: everyday chickpeas in a dark, sour-edged onion-tomato masala
entries.text: chana masala punjabi everyday chickpeas in a dark, sour-edged onion-tomato masala vegan vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free chickpeas (kabuli chana) water onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli neutral oil cumin seeds bay leaf black cardamom coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) turmeric powder red chilli powder garam masala anardana (dried pomegranate seeds) amchur (dry mango powder) asafoetida (hing) salt coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime drain the soaked chickpeas and pressure cook with 5 cups fresh water, the black cardamom and 1 tsp salt for 20 minutes at full pressure. heat the oil in a heavy pan, crackle the cumin seeds and bay leaf for 20 seconds, then add the asafoetida. add the onion and fry on medium for 14 minutes, stirring often, until uniformly dark brown. stir in the garlic, grated ginger and green chillies and fry 2 minutes. add the coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric and chilli powder and stir for 20 seconds. pour in the tomato puree and cook 12 minutes until the masala is thick, glossy and pulling away from the pan with oil at the edges. add the cooked chickpeas with 2 cups of their cooking liquid and simmer uncovered 20 minutes. mash a ladleful of chickpeas against the side of the pan and stir them back in to thicken the gravy. stir in the crushed anardana, amchur and garam masala, and simmer 5 minutes more. taste and push the sour and salt until it makes you sit up, then top with julienned ginger, coriander and lemon wedges.

entries.title: Chole
entries.snippet: Punjabi chickpea curry, dark and tangy with pomegranate and dried mango
entries.text: chole punjabi punjabi chickpea curry, dark and tangy with pomegranate and dried mango vegetarian vegan gluten-free nut-free dairy-free chickpeas (kabuli chana) onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder garam masala cumin seeds bay leaf black cardamom lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil salt pressure cook the soaked chickpeas with salt and the black cardamom in fresh water for 5-6 whistles, until a chickpea crushes easily between finger and thumb. reserve the cooking liquid. heat the oil in a heavy pan. add the cumin seeds and bay leaf, and when the cumin sizzles, add the onion. fry patiently over medium heat until genuinely brown, 10-12 minutes; this is most of the flavour. add the ginger and garlic and cook for a minute until the raw smell goes, then add the tomato puree, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder. cook the masala down until the oil separates and pools at the edges of the pan, 8-10 minutes. do not rush this. add the drained chickpeas with a cup of the reserved cooking liquid. simmer uncovered 15 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy. stir in the garam masala, a good squeeze of lemon and the coriander leaves. rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving; chole improves noticeably in that time.

entries.title: Dal Makhani
entries.snippet: black urad simmered for hours until it turns silky and smoky-sweet with butter
entries.text: dal makhani punjabi black urad simmered for hours until it turns silky and smoky-sweet with butter vegetarian gluten-free nut-free whole urad (sabut urad) rajma (kidney beans) water tomato ginger garlic butter cream neutral oil kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder garam masala kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) salt coriander leaves (cilantro) drain the soaked beans, put them in the pressure cooker with 5 cups water, half the crushed ginger and 1 tsp salt, and cook 25 minutes at full pressure. release the pressure and check: a bean should collapse to paste when pressed against the pot with a spoon. if not, give it another 10 minutes. heat the oil in a heavy pan, add the garlic paste and remaining crushed ginger and fry 90 seconds until the raw smell lifts. add the tomato puree, both chillies and 1/2 tsp salt, and fry on medium until the mixture darkens and oil beads at the edges, about 12 minutes. tip the cooked beans in with all their liquid and stir well to break some of them up against the side of the pan. simmer uncovered on the lowest heat for 45 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes and scraping the base. stir in half the butter, a cube at a time, letting each melt before the next goes in. add the cream, garam masala and crushed kasuri methi, and simmer 10 minutes more until the dal coats a spoon thickly. taste for salt, then rest off the heat for 10 minutes so it thickens and settles. serve topped with the remaining butter, the julienned ginger and the coriander.

entries.title: Dal Tadka
entries.snippet: everyday yellow dal finished with a loud garlic and chilli tempering
entries.text: dal tadka punjabi everyday yellow dal finished with a loud garlic and chilli tempering vegetarian gluten-free nut-free toor dal (pigeon pea) moong dal water turmeric powder tomato onion ginger garlic green chilli ghee cumin seeds dried red chillies asafoetida (hing) kashmiri chilli powder garam masala lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) salt pressure cook the drained dals with 3.5 cups water, the turmeric, half the chopped tomato and 1/2 tsp salt for 8 minutes at full pressure. let the pressure drop naturally, then whisk the dal briskly for 30 seconds until it is smooth and pourable. keep the dal on the lowest simmer while you make the tempering. heat the ghee in a small pan until it shimmers, then add the cumin seeds and let them crackle and darken, about 20 seconds. add the sliced garlic and fry 60 seconds until the slices are gold at the edges. add the onion and fry 5 minutes until soft and browning. add the ginger, green chillies, broken red chillies and asafoetida and fry 30 seconds. add the remaining tomato and cook 4 minutes until it slumps and the ghee separates. take the pan off the heat, stir in the kashmiri chilli, and immediately pour the whole thing over the dal. stir once, add the garam masala, lemon juice and coriander, and taste for salt. cover and rest 5 minutes before serving with rice.

entries.title: Gajar ka Halwa
entries.snippet: grated winter carrots cooked down in milk and ghee until dark, dense and cardamom-scented
entries.text: gajar ka halwa punjabi grated winter carrots cooked down in milk and ghee until dark, dense and cardamom-scented vegetarian gluten-free carrot milk sugar ghee khoya / mawa green cardamom cashews almonds raisins (kishmish) pistachios fry the cashews, almonds and raisins in 1 tbsp of the ghee for 2 minutes until the nuts are gold and the raisins puff, then lift them out. add 2 tbsp ghee to the pan and fry the grated carrot on medium for 10 minutes until it darkens and smells sweet. pour in the milk and bring to a boil, then drop to medium-low. simmer uncovered 40 to 45 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes and scraping the base and sides. keep going until the milk is almost entirely gone and the mass pulls together when you draw the spoon through it. add the sugar and stir — the mixture will go loose again as the sugar melts. cook 10 minutes more on medium until that liquid has gone too. stir in the crumbled khoya and the remaining 2 tbsp ghee and cook 8 minutes until the halwa is glossy and leaves the sides of the pan. fold in the crushed cardamom and most of the fried nuts and raisins. take off the heat, rest 10 minutes, and serve warm topped with the pistachios and remaining nuts.

entries.title: Makki di Roti
entries.snippet: coarse, crumbly winter flatbread patted out by hand and eaten hot with saag
entries.text: makki di roti punjabi coarse, crumbly winter flatbread patted out by hand and eaten hot with saag vegetarian gluten-free nut-free maize flour (makki ka atta) water salt carom seeds (ajwain) ghee butter mix the flour, salt and ajwain in a wide bowl. pour in the hot water a little at a time, mixing with a spoon at first, then knead 5 minutes with the heel of your hand into a smooth, pliable dough. cover and rest 10 minutes. divide into 8 balls. roll one between your palms until it has no cracks on the surface. flatten it between two sheets of paper, pressing outward with your fingertips to a rough disc 5 inches across and about 5mm thick. heat the tawa on medium until a drop of water skitters across it. peel the top sheet off, invert the roti onto your palm, and lay it on the tawa. cook 90 seconds until the underside has pale brown freckles. flip and cook the second side 90 seconds, pressing the edges down with a cloth so it puffs slightly. smear generously with ghee, flip once more for 20 seconds, and stack in a covered dish while you make the rest. serve immediately with butter melting on top and a bowl of saag.

entries.title: Matar Paneer
entries.snippet: peas and paneer in a straightforward onion-tomato gravy, the weeknight standard
entries.text: matar paneer punjabi peas and paneer in a straightforward onion-tomato gravy, the weeknight standard vegetarian gluten-free nut-free paneer peas onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli ghee cumin seeds bay leaf turmeric powder coriander powder kashmiri chilli powder garam masala kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) sugar salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) blend the onion, tomato, ginger, garlic and green chillies to a smooth paste with 2 tbsp water. heat the ghee in a kadhai, add the bay leaf and cumin seeds, and let them crackle 20 seconds. pour in the blended paste — stand back, it spits — and cook on medium for 15 minutes. stir in the turmeric, coriander powder and kashmiri chilli and fry 1 minute. add 1.5 cups water, 1 tsp salt and the sugar, and bring to a simmer. add the peas and simmer 8 minutes for fresh, 4 minutes for frozen, until tender. slide in the paneer cubes and simmer 4 minutes on low. crush in the kasuri methi and add the garam masala. rest off the heat 5 minutes so the paneer takes up the gravy, then taste for salt. scatter the coriander and serve with roti or rice.

entries.title: Methi Malai Matar
entries.snippet: bitter fenugreek leaves and sweet peas in a mild white cream gravy
entries.text: methi malai matar punjabi bitter fenugreek leaves and sweet peas in a mild white cream gravy vegetarian gluten-free fenugreek leaves (methi) peas cashews onion ginger garlic green chilli cream milk ghee cumin seeds green cardamom white pepper garam masala sugar salt water salt, rest and squeeze the methi leaves as in the prep notes, then chop them roughly. boil the onion, ginger, garlic and green chillies in 1 cup water for 8 minutes until soft. blend the boiled mixture with the drained cashews to a completely smooth paste. heat the ghee in a kadhai and fry the cumin seeds and cardamom for 30 seconds until fragrant. add the chopped methi and fry on medium for 6 minutes until it darkens and the raw green smell turns nutty. stir in the cashew-onion paste and cook 8 minutes on low, stirring constantly so it does not catch. add the peas, milk, white pepper, sugar and 1 tsp salt, and simmer 8 minutes until the peas are tender. turn the heat off and stir in the cream and garam masala. rest 5 minutes covered, taste for salt and sugar, and serve with naan or paratha.

entries.title: Palak Paneer
entries.snippet: soft paneer in a bright green spinach gravy, mild and creamy
entries.text: palak paneer punjabi soft paneer in a bright green spinach gravy, mild and creamy vegetarian gluten-free nut-free spinach paneer onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli ghee cumin seeds coriander powder turmeric powder garam masala kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) cream salt water boil a large pan of water, drop in the spinach and green chillies, and blanch for exactly 90 seconds. lift the spinach straight into the iced water, leave 1 minute, then drain and squeeze out most of the liquid. blend the spinach and chillies to a coarse puree with 2 tbsp water and set aside. heat the ghee in a kadhai and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds. add the onion and fry 8 minutes until soft and light gold at the edges. stir in the ginger and garlic and fry 90 seconds until fragrant. add the tomato, coriander powder, turmeric and 3/4 tsp salt, and cook 8 minutes until the tomato breaks down and oil shows at the edges. pour in the spinach puree with 1/2 cup water and simmer just 5 minutes. slide in the paneer cubes, stir gently, and simmer 3 minutes so they warm through and take on the seasoning. crush in the kasuri methi, add the garam masala, and swirl in the cream off the heat. taste for salt and serve hot with roti or jeera rice.

entries.title: Paneer Tikka
entries.snippet: charred cubes of paneer and capsicum off a skewer, smoky and sharp with chaat masala
entries.text: paneer tikka punjabi charred cubes of paneer and capsicum off a skewer, smoky and sharp with chaat masala vegetarian gluten-free nut-free paneer yogurt / dahi besan (gram flour) capsicum / bell pepper onion ginger garlic kashmiri chilli powder garam masala kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) chaat masala mustard oil lemon / lime salt dry-roast the besan in a small pan on low for 3 minutes until it smells like toasted nuts, then cool. whisk the hung yogurt with the roasted besan, ginger-garlic paste, kashmiri chilli, garam masala, crushed kasuri methi, oil and salt into a thick paste. fold in the paneer, capsicum and onion petals, coating everything evenly, and refrigerate 1 hour. heat the oven to 230c with a rack in the upper third. thread the paneer and vegetables alternately onto skewers, leaving a small gap between pieces. set the skewers on a wire rack over a foil-lined tray and roast 12 minutes. turn the skewers and roast another 6 to 8 minutes, until the edges are blackened in patches and the marinade has set dry. rest 3 minutes, then dust with chaat masala and squeeze over lemon. serve hot with sliced onion and mint chutney.

entries.title: Punjabi Chana Dal
entries.snippet: nutty split gram dal cooked to just-holding grains under a garlic tadka
entries.text: punjabi chana dal punjabi nutty split gram dal cooked to just-holding grains under a garlic tadka vegetarian gluten-free nut-free chana dal water onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli ghee cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder garam masala amchur (dry mango powder) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt pressure cook the drained dal with 3 cups water and the turmeric for 12 minutes at full pressure, then let the pressure fall on its own. heat 2 tbsp of the ghee in a pan, add the cumin seeds and let them crackle for 20 seconds, then add the asafoetida. add the onion and fry 7 minutes until soft and gold at the edges. stir in the ginger, half the garlic and the green chillies, and fry 90 seconds. add the tomato, coriander powder, chilli powder and 1 tsp salt, and cook 8 minutes until the tomato collapses and oil pools at the sides. tip in the cooked dal with its liquid, add 1/2 cup hot water, and simmer 12 minutes so the flavours settle in. stir in the garam masala and amchur and taste for salt. heat the last tablespoon of ghee in a small pan and fry the remaining garlic slices until deep gold, about 90 seconds. pour the garlic ghee over the dal, scatter the coriander, and serve with roti.

entries.title: Punjabi Kadhi Pakora
entries.snippet: tangy yogurt and gram flour gravy simmered thick, with soft onion fritters dropped in
entries.text: punjabi kadhi pakora punjabi tangy yogurt and gram flour gravy simmered thick, with soft onion fritters dropped in vegetarian gluten-free nut-free yogurt / dahi besan (gram flour) water onion green chilli ginger garlic turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder fenugreek seeds (methi) cumin seeds mustard seeds asafoetida (hing) dried red chillies ghee neutral oil kashmiri chilli powder salt coriander leaves (cilantro) whisk the sour yogurt with 6 tbsp besan, the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and 1 tsp salt until completely smooth, then whisk in 4 cups water. heat 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy pot, crackle the fenugreek and cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then add the asafoetida, half the ginger, the garlic and half the green chillies. pour in the yogurt mixture and bring it to a boil on medium, stirring constantly in one direction. once it boils, drop to the lowest heat and simmer uncovered 40 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes. meanwhile make the pakora batter: mix the remaining besan with the sliced onion, remaining ginger and chilli, 1/2 tsp salt and just enough water to bind, about 4 tbsp. heat the oil in a kadhai to 175c and drop in rough spoonfuls of batter, 6 at a time. fry 4 minutes, turning, until deep gold and firm, then drain on a rack. loose, craggy spoonfuls fry lighter than neat balls. slide the pakoras into the simmering kadhi and cook 8 minutes more so they drink up the gravy but keep their shape. taste for salt — sour kadhi needs a firm hand with it. for the final tempering, heat the last tablespoon of ghee, take it off the heat, stir in the kashmiri chilli and broken red chillies, and pour it over the kadhi. scatter the coriander and serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Rajma Chawal
entries.snippet: soft kidney beans in a thick onion-tomato gravy, eaten over plain rice
entries.text: rajma chawal punjabi soft kidney beans in a thick onion-tomato gravy, eaten over plain rice vegan vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rajma (kidney beans) basmati rice onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli neutral oil cumin seeds bay leaf turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder garam masala amchur (dry mango powder) salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) pressure cook the drained rajma with 4 cups fresh water, the bay leaf and 1 tsp salt for 20 minutes at full pressure, then let the pressure fall naturally. while it cooks, heat the oil in a heavy pan and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds. add the onion and fry on medium-high, stirring often, until evenly deep brown — a full 12 to 14 minutes. stir in the ginger, garlic and green chillies and fry 2 minutes until the sharpness goes. add the turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder, stir for 20 seconds, then pour in the tomato puree. cook the masala down for 10 to 12 minutes until it darkens and oil separates at the sides. scoop out a ladle of cooked beans, mash them to a paste, and stir that back in with the rest of the beans and their liquid. simmer uncovered 20 minutes until the gravy is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. add hot water if it tightens too far. meanwhile boil the rice in 3 cups water with 1/2 tsp salt, covered, on the lowest heat for 11 minutes, then rest 5 minutes off the heat and fork through. finish the rajma with garam masala and amchur, taste for salt, and scatter over the coriander. serve the rajma ladled over the hot rice.

entries.title: Sarson ka Saag
entries.snippet: slow-cooked mustard greens, bitter and buttery, thickened with a little coarse flour
entries.text: sarson ka saag punjabi slow-cooked mustard greens, bitter and buttery, thickened with a little coarse flour vegetarian gluten-free nut-free mustard greens (sarson) spinach fenugreek leaves (methi) maize flour (makki ka atta) ginger garlic green chilli onion ghee butter salt water put the mustard greens, spinach, methi, chopped ginger, garlic, green chillies, 1 tsp salt and 1.5 cups water in the pressure cooker and cook 15 minutes at full pressure. let the pressure drop, then uncover — the greens should be army-green and completely collapsed. blend to a coarse puree, or crush with a wooden masher for the traditional rough texture. return the puree to the pan and bring to a bare simmer. whisk in the flour slurry in a thin stream and cook 25 minutes on low, stirring every few minutes. meanwhile heat the ghee in a small pan and fry the chopped onion until golden brown, about 8 minutes. add the julienned ginger to the onion and fry 1 minute more. pour the tempering into the saag, scraping the pan clean, and simmer 10 minutes more. taste for salt — greens need more than you expect — and finish with the butter melting on top.

entries.title: Shahi Paneer
entries.snippet: paneer in a pale, mildly sweet cashew and cream gravy scented with cardamom
entries.text: shahi paneer punjabi paneer in a pale, mildly sweet cashew and cream gravy scented with cardamom vegetarian gluten-free paneer cashews melon seeds (magaz) onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli ghee green cardamom cinnamon cloves black cardamom cream milk kashmiri chilli powder garam masala sugar kewra water salt water simmer the sliced onion, ginger, garlic and green chilli in 1 cup water for 10 minutes until completely soft, then cool slightly. blend the boiled onion mixture with the drained cashews and melon seeds to a silky paste, adding a little of the cooking water. blend the tomato separately to a puree and set aside. heat the ghee in a kadhai and fry the cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and black cardamom for 40 seconds until fragrant. add the tomato puree and cook 8 minutes until it thickens and the ghee separates. stir in the cashew-onion paste and cook 10 minutes on low, stirring constantly. add the kashmiri chilli, sugar, 1 tsp salt and the milk, and simmer 5 minutes to a gravy that coats a spoon. slide in the paneer cubes and simmer 3 minutes on the lowest heat. turn off the heat, stir in the cream and garam masala, and add the kewra water. rest 5 minutes covered, then fish out the whole spices and serve with naan or pulao.

entries.title: Tandoori-Style Chicken
entries.snippet: yogurt and chilli marinated chicken charred hard at the edges, done in a home oven
entries.text: tandoori-style chicken punjabi yogurt and chilli marinated chicken charred hard at the edges, done in a home oven gluten-free nut-free chicken yogurt / dahi ginger garlic kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder garam masala cumin powder (jeera) coriander powder black salt (kala namak) kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) lemon / lime mustard oil salt butter rub the chicken with the lemon juice, 1 tsp salt and 1 tsp of the kashmiri chilli, and leave 20 minutes. whisk the hung yogurt with the ginger-garlic paste, remaining chillies, garam masala, cumin, coriander, black salt, crushed kasuri methi, cooled mustard oil and remaining salt. coat the chicken thoroughly, working the marinade into every slash, then cover and refrigerate overnight. heat the oven to its maximum, at least 240c, with a rack set near the top and a tray of water on the floor of the oven. arrange the chicken on a wire rack over a foil-lined tray, shaking off pooled marinade. roast 20 minutes, until the surface is dry and starting to blacken at the edges. turn the pieces, baste with melted butter, and roast another 15 minutes. test the thickest thigh: the juices should run clear and the meat pull easily from the bone. rest 5 minutes, then finish under a hot grill for 3 minutes for extra char if you want it. serve with lemon wedges, raw onion rings and green chutney.

entries.title: Aloo Pyaaz ki Sabzi
entries.snippet: everyday dry potato and onion stir-fry, sharp with amchur and hing
entries.text: aloo pyaaz ki sabzi rajasthani everyday dry potato and onion stir-fry, sharp with amchur and hing vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free potato onion neutral oil cumin seeds mustard seeds asafoetida (hing) green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder amchur (dry mango powder) kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt heat the oil until it shimmers, then crackle the mustard seeds, followed by the cumin. add the hing and slit green chillies and fry 15 seconds. tip in the sliced onion and cook 6-7 minutes over medium-high heat until the edges brown but the pieces still have bite. take the pan off the heat, add the turmeric, chilli and coriander powders, and stir for 10 seconds in the residual heat. return to the flame, add the cubed potato and salt, and toss to coat every piece. fry 8 minutes over medium heat, turning only every couple of minutes, until the potatoes take on crisp golden faces. crush in the kasuri methi and sprinkle over the amchur, then toss and cook 1 more minute. stir through the coriander leaves and serve hot with methi bajra puri or plain roti.

entries.title: Bajre ki Roti
entries.snippet: thick hand-patted millet flatbread, nutty and earthy, eaten hot with ghee
entries.text: bajre ki roti rajasthani thick hand-patted millet flatbread, nutty and earthy, eaten hot with ghee vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic bajra (pearl millet) flour water salt ghee mix the flour and salt, then pour in the hot water a little at a time, stirring with a spoon until too hot to handle comfortably. knead 4-5 minutes with the heel of your hand while it is still warm, until smooth and pliable with no cracks. divide into 6 balls and keep them covered with a damp cloth. flatten one ball between your palms, then pat it out on a greased sheet of plastic or a damp cloth, rotating as you go, into a 15cm disc about 5mm thick. lift it onto a medium-hot tawa and cook 2 minutes until the underside is speckled and dry. flip and cook the second side 2 minutes, pressing the edges gently with a cloth so it cooks evenly. lift the roti with tongs and hold it directly over the flame for 15-20 seconds a side until it puffs and chars in patches. smear with ghee and serve immediately with ker sangri, gatte ki sabzi or plain garlic chutney.

entries.title: Besan ki Chakki
entries.snippet: dense granular fudge of ghee-roasted gram flour, sweet and toasty
entries.text: besan ki chakki rajasthani dense granular fudge of ghee-roasted gram flour, sweet and toasty vegetarian gluten-free besan (gram flour) ghee sugar water milk green cardamom pistachios saffron boil the sugar and water together and cook 6-7 minutes to a one-string consistency — a drop between finger and thumb should pull a single short thread. keep it warm. in a heavy kadhai melt the ghee over low heat and add the besan. roast on low, stirring constantly, for 20-25 minutes. it will go from crumbly to pasty to loose and flowing, and turn the colour of peanut butter. when it smells strongly nutty, sprinkle over the warm milk — it will hiss and foam violently. keep stirring. keep roasting 5 more minutes as the mixture breaks into loose granules and the ghee visibly separates. take off the heat, wait 1 minute, then pour in the hot syrup in a thin stream, stirring hard. return to low heat for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until the mixture thickens and starts pulling away from the sides of the pan. stir in the cardamom and saffron milk, pour into the greased tray and level the top with the back of a spoon. scatter the pistachios, press them in lightly, and cool 45 minutes before cutting into squares or diamonds.

entries.title: Dal Baati Churma
entries.snippet: Baked wheat balls drowned in ghee, with a five-lentil dal and sweet crushed churma
entries.text: dal baati churma rajasthani baked wheat balls drowned in ghee, with a five-lentil dal and sweet crushed churma vegetarian atta (wholewheat flour) rava / sooji (semolina) ghee carom seeds (ajwain) toor dal (pigeon pea) chana dal moong dal urad dal (black gram) masoor dal (red lentil) onion tomato ginger garlic cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder garam masala jaggery green cardamom almonds salt make a stiff dough from atta, rava, ajwain, salt and 4 tbsp ghee with as little water as possible. rest 20 minutes. shape into balls, press a dimple into each, and bake at 200c for 35-40 minutes, turning once, until cracked and deep golden. meanwhile pressure cook the mixed dals with turmeric and salt until soft, 4 whistles. temper cumin and asafoetida in ghee, add ginger, garlic and onion, then tomato and the powdered spices. cook until the fat separates, then fold into the dal and simmer 10 minutes. for the churma, crush a few baatis coarsely and work in jaggery, cardamom, chopped almonds and hot ghee. to serve, dunk each hot baati in melted ghee, break it open into the dal, and eat with churma on the side.

entries.title: Gatte ki Sabzi
entries.snippet: steamed gram-flour dumplings simmered in a tangy yogurt gravy
entries.text: gatte ki sabzi rajasthani steamed gram-flour dumplings simmered in a tangy yogurt gravy vegetarian gluten-free nut-free besan (gram flour) yogurt / dahi ghee carom seeds (ajwain) cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder dried red chillies garam masala kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) coriander leaves (cilantro) water salt knead the besan with 2 tbsp ghee, the ajwain, 1/2 tsp salt and about 4 tbsp yogurt into a stiff, smooth dough. it should feel like firm putty, not sticky. rest the dough 10 minutes, then roll into 4 ropes about 1.5cm thick. slide the ropes into rolling boiling water and cook 12-14 minutes, until they float and the surface looks matte rather than shiny. lift out, cool 5 minutes, and cut into 2cm pieces. save 250ml of the cooking water — it is the body of the gravy. heat the remaining 2 tbsp ghee, crackle the cumin, add the hing and broken red chilli, and let them darken for 10 seconds. pour in the spiced yogurt and stir continuously on low heat for 4-5 minutes until it stops looking grainy and a film of ghee shows at the edge. add the reserved cooking water and salt, and simmer 8 minutes until the gravy coats a spoon. slip in the gatte and simmer another 5 minutes so they drink up the gravy. crush in the kasuri methi, sprinkle the garam masala and coriander leaves, and rest 5 minutes off the heat before serving with bajre ki roti.

entries.title: Haldi ki Sabzi
entries.snippet: winter curry of fresh turmeric root and peas cooked down in yogurt and ghee
entries.text: haldi ki sabzi rajasthani winter curry of fresh turmeric root and peas cooked down in yogurt and ghee vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic turmeric powder peas yogurt / dahi ghee ginger green chilli cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) coriander powder red chilli powder garam masala cream coriander leaves (cilantro) water salt heat 4 tbsp ghee on low and add the grated turmeric. fry gently for 12-15 minutes, stirring often, until the raw earthy smell turns sweet and the ghee runs clear orange at the sides. push the turmeric aside, add the remaining 2 tbsp ghee and crackle the cumin, then the hing, ginger and green chillies. stir in the coriander and chilli powders off the heat for 10 seconds. take the pan right off the flame, add the whisked yogurt, then return to the lowest heat and stir continuously 5-6 minutes until it thickens and the ghee separates. add the peas, salt and water, cover and simmer 10 minutes until the peas are tender and the gravy is thick. stir in the cream and garam masala and cook 2 more minutes. rest 5 minutes, scatter the coriander leaves and serve with bajre ki roti and a spoonful of jaggery on the side.

entries.title: Ker Sangri
entries.snippet: dry desert-style beans and berries, tart with amchur and hot with whole red chilli
entries.text: ker sangri rajasthani dry desert-style beans and berries, tart with amchur and hot with whole red chilli vegetarian gluten-free nut-free cluster beans (guar) raisins (kishmish) dried apricots (khubani) yogurt / dahi mustard oil dried red chillies cumin seeds carom seeds (ajwain) asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder amchur (dry mango powder) water salt boil the cluster beans in salted water 8 minutes, until just yielding but still squeaky. drain well and pat dry. heat the mustard oil until it smokes, take it off the flame for 30 seconds, then return it to medium heat. crackle the cumin and ajwain, add the whole red chillies and hing, and fry 20 seconds until the chillies swell and darken. stir in the turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder off the heat for 5 seconds so they bloom without burning. add the drained beans and toss over high heat 4-5 minutes until they take on brown blistered patches. fold in the raisins and apricot, add the water and salt, cover and cook 8 minutes on low. lower the heat right down, stir in the whisked yogurt and cook 4 minutes until it clings to the beans and no liquid pools at the base. finish with the amchur, toss once, and serve dry alongside bajre ki roti and a spoon of ghee.

entries.title: Laal Maas
entries.snippet: fiery mutton curry stained deep red by whole chillies and slow-cooked in ghee
entries.text: laal maas rajasthani fiery mutton curry stained deep red by whole chillies and slow-cooked in ghee gluten-free nut-free mutton / lamb kashmiri chilli powder dried red chillies yogurt / dahi ghee onion garlic ginger coriander powder turmeric powder cumin seeds cloves cinnamon black cardamom bay leaf garam masala water salt heat the ghee and fry the whole spices — cloves, cinnamon, black cardamom, bay leaf and cumin — for 30 seconds until they smell toasted. add the sliced onion and cook 12-14 minutes over medium heat until deep gold and collapsed. stir in the garlic and ginger pastes and fry 3 minutes until the raw smell goes. add the mutton and brown over high heat 8 minutes, turning the pieces so they seize on all sides. turn the heat to low, add the yogurt-and-chilli paste with the coriander powder and turmeric, and bhuno for 12-15 minutes, stirring, until the ghee separates and pools red at the edges. add the whole dried red chillies, salt and water, and pressure-cook 5 whistles, or cover and simmer 60 minutes, until the meat pulls off the bone. uncover and reduce 10 minutes until the gravy is glossy and clings to the meat. optional dhungar: set a small steel bowl in the pan, drop in a red-hot coal, pour a teaspoon of ghee over it and cover for 4 minutes to smoke the curry. sprinkle the garam masala, rest 10 minutes, and serve with bajre ki roti or plain rice.

entries.title: Malpua
entries.snippet: fennel-scented pancakes fried in ghee and steeped in cardamom syrup
entries.text: malpua rajasthani fennel-scented pancakes fried in ghee and steeped in cardamom syrup vegetarian nut-free plain flour (maida) khoya / mawa milk rava / sooji (semolina) sugar water fennel seeds (saunf) green cardamom ghee saffron boil the sugar and water 5-6 minutes to a sticky syrup just short of one string, add the saffron and cardamom, and keep warm. mash the grated khoya with 4 tbsp of the milk until lump-free. whisk in the maida, rava and crushed fennel, then the rest of the milk, a little at a time, into a smooth pouring batter. rest the batter 45 minutes, then check it — it should coat a spoon and drip in a ribbon. loosen with milk if needed. heat 2cm of ghee in a shallow kadhai over medium heat until a drop of batter sizzles immediately. pour a small ladleful into the centre of the pan. do not spread it — let it settle into a 8cm disc with frilled edges. fry 2 minutes, spooning hot ghee over the top, until the edges are deep gold and lacy, then flip and fry 1 minute more. lift out, drain for a few seconds, and drop straight into the warm syrup. soak 3-4 minutes, then lift onto a plate. repeat with the rest of the batter, frying two at a time, and serve warm with rabri or on their own.

entries.title: Mawa Kachori
entries.snippet: jodhpur's sweet kachori — khoya and nuts in flaky pastry, drowned in syrup
entries.text: mawa kachori rajasthani jodhpur's sweet kachori — khoya and nuts in flaky pastry, drowned in syrup vegetarian plain flour (maida) ghee khoya / mawa sugar water green cardamom almonds cashews pistachios raisins (kishmish) dried coconut (copra) saffron salt rub the 60ml ghee into the maida with the pinch of salt for 3 minutes, then add water gradually to a soft dough. cover and rest 30 minutes. roast the grated khoya in a dry pan over low heat 6-8 minutes until it smells nutty and turns pale gold. spread on a plate and cool fully. mix the cold khoya with the powdered sugar, cardamom, almonds, cashew, half the pistachios, raisins and dried coconut. boil the 350g sugar with 175ml water 6 minutes to a one-string syrup, add the saffron, and keep it warm. divide the dough into 8. roll each into a 9cm disc, thicker in the middle than at the rim. place a heaped tablespoon of filling in the centre, gather the edges up over it, pinch tightly shut and twist off the excess dough. flatten each gently with your palm into a 7cm disc and rest them seam-down for 10 minutes. heat the frying ghee to a low 140c — a kachori should take a good 10 seconds to float up. fry 4 at a time for 12-14 minutes on low, spooning ghee over them, until blistered and pale gold all over. drain briefly, then dip each hot kachori in the warm syrup for 30 seconds and lift onto a plate. crack open the top, spoon a little extra syrup inside, scatter the remaining pistachios and serve warm.

entries.title: Methi Bajra Puri
entries.snippet: millet and fenugreek puris, crisp-edged and faintly bitter
entries.text: methi bajra puri rajasthani millet and fenugreek puris, crisp-edged and faintly bitter vegetarian vegan dairy-free nut-free bajra (pearl millet) flour atta (wholewheat flour) fenugreek leaves (methi) neutral oil carom seeds (ajwain) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder sesame seeds water salt squeeze the salted methi dry and put it in a bowl with both flours, ajwain, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, sesame and salt. rub in the 2 tbsp oil, then add warm water a little at a time to make a stiff dough, firmer than chapati dough. knead 5 minutes until smooth, cover and rest 15 minutes. divide into 16 balls and roll each into a 10cm disc on a lightly oiled surface, about 3mm thick. heat the oil to 180c. a scrap of dough should rise to the surface in about 2 seconds. slide in one puri, press it under with the back of a slotted spoon for 3 seconds until it puffs. flip and fry the second side 30-40 seconds until the edges are crisp and the colour is deep brown-green. drain upright in a colander so the oil runs off, and serve hot with aloo pyaaz ki sabzi or plain yogurt.

entries.title: Mirchi Vada
entries.snippet: jodhpur's fat green chillies stuffed with spiced potato and fried in gram-flour batter
entries.text: mirchi vada rajasthani jodhpur's fat green chillies stuffed with spiced potato and fried in gram-flour batter vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic green chilli potato besan (gram flour) neutral oil cumin seeds fennel seeds (saunf) asafoetida (hing) ginger turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder amchur (dry mango powder) coriander leaves (cilantro) carom seeds (ajwain) baking soda water salt heat 2 tbsp oil, crackle the cumin and fennel, add the hing and grated ginger, and fry 30 seconds. add the turmeric, chilli and coriander powders off the heat, then fold in the mashed potato and salt. cook 4 minutes over medium heat, then stir in the amchur and coriander leaves and cool completely. whisk the besan with the ajwain, baking soda, a pinch of salt and enough water to make a batter that thickly coats a spoon and does not run off it. pack each chilli firmly through its slit with the potato filling and press the slit closed. heat the frying oil to 175c — a drop of batter should rise steadily and sizzle without browning instantly. dip each stuffed chilli in the batter, turning to coat completely including the ends, and lower it into the oil. fry 4-5 minutes, turning once, until the crust is pale gold and crisp. do no more than three at a time. drain on paper and serve hot with tamarind or mint chutney, or pushed into a soft bun as jodhpur does.

entries.title: Panchmel Dal
entries.snippet: five lentils cooked together and finished with a ghee, hing and red chilli tadka
entries.text: panchmel dal rajasthani five lentils cooked together and finished with a ghee, hing and red chilli tadka vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic toor dal (pigeon pea) chana dal moong dal urad dal (black gram) masoor dal (red lentil) ghee cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) dried red chillies bay leaf cloves ginger green chilli tomato turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder garam masala amchur (dry mango powder) coriander leaves (cilantro) water salt drain the soaked dals and pressure-cook with the turmeric, 1 tbsp ghee and 900ml water for 4 whistles, then let the pressure drop naturally. whisk the cooked dal briefly — it should be soft but the chana dal still recognisable, not a puree. heat 2 tbsp ghee in a separate pan, crackle 1 tsp cumin with the bay leaf and cloves. add the ginger and green chilli and fry 1 minute until fragrant. stir in the coriander powder, chilli powder and half the hing off the heat for 10 seconds, then add the tomato and cook 4 minutes until it breaks down. pour this into the dal with the salt and the remaining water, and simmer 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until it thickens to a pouring consistency. stir in the amchur and garam masala and taste for salt and sourness. for the final tadka, heat the last 2 tbsp ghee, crackle the remaining cumin, add the broken red chillies and the rest of the hing, and pour it over the dal while it is still foaming. scatter the coriander leaves and serve with baati or bajre ki roti.

entries.title: Pyaaz Kachori
entries.snippet: Flaky fried pastry with a spiced onion filling, from the sweet shops of Jodhpur
entries.text: pyaaz kachori rajasthani flaky fried pastry with a spiced onion filling, from the sweet shops of jodhpur vegetarian nut-free plain flour (maida) ghee onion besan (gram flour) fennel seeds (saunf) coriander powder cumin seeds nigella seeds (kalonji) red chilli powder turmeric powder garam masala amchur (dry mango powder) asafoetida (hing) neutral oil salt rub the ghee into the flour with salt until it holds together when squeezed, then add water a little at a time to make a firm dough. rest 30 minutes. fry the cumin, fennel, nigella and asafoetida, add the onion and cook until soft and just golden, not brown. add the besan and the powdered spices and cook 4-5 minutes until dry and crumbly. add amchur, cool completely. roll small dough balls into cups, fill, gather and seal, then flatten very gently to about 1cm. fry in oil kept at a low 130-140c for 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally, until pale gold and covered in blisters. drain on a rack. serve warm with tamarind and coriander chutneys.

entries.title: Pyaaz Kachori
entries.snippet: flaky fried pastry packed with a dark, heavily spiced onion and besan filling
entries.text: pyaaz kachori rajasthani flaky fried pastry packed with a dark, heavily spiced onion and besan filling vegetarian vegan dairy-free nut-free plain flour (maida) neutral oil onion besan (gram flour) fennel seeds (saunf) cumin seeds coriander powder red chilli powder turmeric powder garam masala amchur (dry mango powder) asafoetida (hing) ginger green chilli nigella seeds (kalonji) water salt rub the 60ml oil into the maida with 1/2 tsp salt for 3 minutes, then add water a little at a time to make a soft, smooth dough. cover and rest 30 minutes. heat 3 tbsp oil in a kadhai and crackle the cumin, fennel and nigella, then add the hing. add the chopped onion and cook 12-15 minutes over medium heat until it loses all its water and turns light brown. stir in the ginger, green chilli and besan and roast 4 minutes until the besan smells nutty. add the ground spices, amchur and salt and bhuno 3 more minutes, then spread the filling on a plate to cool. divide the dough into 8, roll each into a ball, and flatten into a 8cm disc thicker at the centre than the edge. place a heaped tablespoon of filling in the middle, gather the edges over it, pinch shut and pull off the excess knot of dough. flatten each stuffed ball gently with your palm into a 7cm disc. rest them 10 minutes, seam down. heat the frying oil to just 140c, low enough that a kachori dropped in takes 8-10 seconds to float. slide in 3 or 4. fry very slowly, 12-14 minutes, spooning oil over the tops, until they are covered in blisters and pale gold. raise the heat for the last 2 minutes to crisp them. drain and serve warm, cracked open with tamarind chutney poured in.

entries.title: Rajasthani Kadhi
