entries.snippet: thin, sour buttermilk kadhi sharpened with a chilli and hing tempering
entries.text: rajasthani kadhi rajasthani thin, sour buttermilk kadhi sharpened with a chilli and hing tempering vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic besan (gram flour) buttermilk (chaas) ghee cumin seeds mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) asafoetida (hing) dried red chillies green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder curry leaves coriander leaves (cilantro) salt whisk the besan, turmeric, chilli powder and salt into the buttermilk until completely smooth. strain it if you can see any lumps. pour into a heavy pan and bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly in one direction. as soon as it boils, drop the heat to low and simmer 15 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes, until it thickens slightly and loses its raw besan smell. add the slit green chillies and cook another 2 minutes. in a small pan heat the ghee, crackle the mustard seeds, then the cumin, then the fenugreek seeds for 10 seconds. add the broken red chillies, curry leaves and hing, and pull off the heat the moment the chillies darken. pour the tempering over the kadhi, cover for 2 minutes to trap the aroma, then stir through with the coriander leaves. serve loose and pourable over steamed rice, or with bajre ki roti.

entries.title: Safed Maas
entries.snippet: pale, creamy mutton braised with cashew, yogurt and white pepper instead of red chilli
entries.text: safed maas rajasthani pale, creamy mutton braised with cashew, yogurt and white pepper instead of red chilli gluten-free mutton / lamb cashews almonds poppy seeds (khus khus) melon seeds (magaz) yogurt / dahi cream ghee onion garlic ginger white pepper green chilli green cardamom cloves cinnamon mace (javitri) kewra water water salt heat the ghee on medium and fry the cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and mace 30 seconds, without letting them colour. add the ginger and garlic pastes and cook 2 minutes until the raw edge goes but no colour develops. stir in the boiled onion paste and cook 5 minutes on low, stirring, until it thickens and smells sweet. add the mutton and turn it in the paste 6 minutes over medium heat — sealing, not browning. take the pan off the heat, stir in the whisked yogurt, then return to the lowest flame and cook 8 minutes until it thickens and the ghee edges out. add the nut paste, white pepper, green chillies, salt and water. pressure-cook 5 whistles, or cover and simmer 60 minutes until the meat is tender. uncover and simmer 8 minutes to reduce until the gravy coats the back of a spoon. stir in the cream and kewra water, warm through 2 minutes without boiling, and rest 10 minutes before serving.

entries.title: Aloo Tuk
entries.snippet: twice-fried smashed potatoes, crisp outside and floury within, dusted with amchur
entries.text: aloo tuk sindhi twice-fried smashed potatoes, crisp outside and floury within, dusted with amchur vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free potato neutral oil amchur (dry mango powder) chaat masala red chilli powder black salt (kala namak) black pepper salt heat the oil to medium — a potato piece dropped in should bubble steadily around the edges, not fizz furiously. fry the potatoes in two batches for 8-10 minutes each, until pale gold and a skewer slides in easily. they should be cooked through but not coloured much. lift them out onto a rack and let them cool for 10 minutes. flatten each piece with the heel of your hand or the flat of a knife to about 1.5cm, so the edges crack open. raise the oil to high, until a scrap of potato surfaces immediately. fry the flattened pieces again in batches, 3-4 minutes, until deep golden and audibly crisp when knocked against the ladle. drain on a rack rather than paper so the undersides do not steam soft. while still very hot, toss with the spice mix and taste for salt. serve at once, alongside sindhi kadhi and rice as tradition has it, or on their own with tea.

entries.title: Bhee Patata
entries.snippet: rhizome and potato braised down in a dry onion-tomato masala until the edges catch
entries.text: bhee patata sindhi rhizome and potato braised down in a dry onion-tomato masala until the edges catch vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free lotus stem (nadru/bhee) potato onion tomato garlic ginger green chilli turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder cumin seeds amchur (dry mango powder) coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil water salt heat the oil in a kadhai and crackle the cumin seeds, about 20 seconds. fry the par-boiled lotus stem coins and the potato fingers on medium-high for 8 minutes, turning once or twice, until patched with gold. lift them out. in the same oil, fry the onion 8-10 minutes until properly brown at the edges, not merely soft. add the garlic, ginger and green chilli and fry 1 minute, until the raw garlic smell goes. stir in the tomato, turmeric, coriander powder, chilli powder and salt and cook 6-8 minutes, until the mass darkens and oil pools at the sides. return the vegetables, turn them through the masala, add the water and cover. cook on low 12-15 minutes, shaking the pan rather than stirring, until the potato is tender and almost no liquid remains. uncover, raise the heat and let it fry dry for 2-3 minutes so the underside catches and crusts. sprinkle over the amchur and coriander leaves, toss once and take it off the heat.

entries.title: Bhuga Chawal
entries.snippet: brown onion rice, sweet and savoury at once, the plate that sindhi kadhi is poured over
entries.text: bhuga chawal sindhi brown onion rice, sweet and savoury at once, the plate that sindhi kadhi is poured over vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free basmati rice onion neutral oil cumin seeds bay leaf cinnamon cloves black pepper water salt heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onion over medium heat, stirring often. keep going 18-20 minutes. the onions will go translucent, then straw, then a deep mahogany brown and sticky-sweet. push the onions aside, add the cumin, bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves and peppercorns and let them sizzle 20 seconds. add the drained rice and turn it gently through the onions and oil for 2 minutes, until every grain is glossy and faintly brown. pour in the hot water, add the salt and bring to a hard boil. as soon as the water level drops to the surface of the rice, about 5 minutes, cover tightly and drop the heat to its lowest setting. cook undisturbed 12 minutes, then take the pot off the heat and let it stand, still covered, 10 minutes. fluff with a fork from the edges inward and serve with sindhi kadhi ladled over.

entries.title: Dal Pakwan
entries.snippet: soft chana dal under a shower of chaat masala with crisp fried maida discs to break over it
entries.text: dal pakwan sindhi soft chana dal under a shower of chaat masala with crisp fried maida discs to break over it vegetarian vegan dairy-free nut-free chana dal turmeric powder plain flour (maida) rava / sooji (semolina) carom seeds (ajwain) cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) green chilli ginger tomato red chilli powder amchur (dry mango powder) chaat masala black salt (kala namak) onion coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime neutral oil water salt knead the maida, rava, 1/2 tsp ajwain, 1/2 tsp salt and 4 tbsp oil with about 3/4 cup water into a firm, smooth dough. cover and rest 30 minutes. pressure cook the drained dal with the turmeric, 1/2 tsp salt and 4 cups water for 2 whistles, then 4 minutes on low. the grains should be soft but still separate, not a puree. heat 3 tbsp oil in a small pan, crackle the remaining cumin and ajwain, add the hing, green chilli and half the ginger. add the tomato, chilli powder and amchur and cook 3 minutes until the oil separates, then pour the whole tempering into the dal. simmer the dal 8-10 minutes, mashing a ladleful against the side to thicken it. it should be spoonable, like loose porridge. divide the dough into 12. roll each into a thin 12cm disc and prick it all over with a fork — 20 or 30 holes, right through. heat the frying oil to medium — a scrap of dough should rise slowly, not race to the top. fry each pakwan 2-3 minutes a side until pale gold and rigid. drain the pakwan upright in a colander so they stay crisp rather than steaming on kitchen paper. ladle the hot dal into bowls, top with chopped onion, remaining ginger, coriander, chaat masala and black salt, and squeeze over lemon. serve at once with the pakwan alongside, to be cracked and dipped.

entries.title: Koki
entries.snippet: thick crumbly onion flatbread cooked twice on the tawa, the Sindhi breakfast bread
entries.text: koki sindhi thick crumbly onion flatbread cooked twice on the tawa, the sindhi breakfast bread vegetarian nut-free atta (wholewheat flour) onion green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) anardana (dried pomegranate seeds) carom seeds (ajwain) cumin seeds red chilli powder ghee water salt rub 4 tbsp ghee into the atta with your fingertips until the flour clumps when squeezed. this moyan is what makes koki crumbly rather than chewy. mix in the squeezed onion, green chilli, coriander, anardana, ajwain, cumin, chilli powder and salt. add water a spoonful at a time and knead to a stiff, tight dough. cover and rest 15 minutes. divide into 4 balls. roll each one about 1cm thick and 12cm across — much thicker than a roti. cook the first side on a medium-hot tawa, dry, for about 1 minute, until it turns opaque and speckles lightly. flip and give the other side 1 minute. lift the half-cooked disc off, let it cool a minute, then roll it again to about 7mm thick. prick all over with a fork. return it to the tawa on low-medium heat, spoon a tablespoon of ghee around the edge and cook 3-4 minutes a side, pressing with a cloth, until deep gold with brown blisters. repeat with the remaining dough and serve hot with plain yogurt, mango pickle or sweet tea.

entries.title: Mitho Lolo
entries.snippet: sweet fennel-scented ghee flatbread, made for Cheti Chand and eaten with plain yogurt
entries.text: mitho lolo sindhi sweet fennel-scented ghee flatbread, made for cheti chand and eaten with plain yogurt vegetarian nut-free atta (wholewheat flour) jaggery ghee fennel seeds (saunf) green cardamom black pepper milk water salt rub 4 tbsp ghee into the atta with your fingertips for a couple of minutes, until the flour holds its shape when pressed in a fist. mix in the fennel, ground cardamom, cracked pepper and salt. pour in the strained jaggery water and the milk and bring it together into a stiff dough — softer than pastry, firmer than roti dough. add flour by the spoonful if it sticks. cover and rest 20 minutes. divide into 6 balls. roll each to about 8mm thick and 12cm across, dusting with flour — thicker than a paratha, and no need to be neat. cook on a medium-low tawa for about 2 minutes, until the surface dries and small blisters appear. flip. spoon a tablespoon of ghee around the edge and cook 2-3 minutes a side, pressing gently with a cloth, until both faces are freckled deep brown. stack the cooked lolos under a cloth so they steam and soften, and serve warm with plain yogurt or a glass of milk.

entries.title: Sai Bhaji
entries.snippet: spinach and chana dal cooked down with vegetables into a soft green mash, eaten with rice most weeknights
entries.text: sai bhaji sindhi spinach and chana dal cooked down with vegetables into a soft green mash, eaten with rice most weeknights vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free spinach dill (suva) chana dal potato eggplant / brinjal carrot tomato onion garlic ginger green chilli turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder cumin seeds neutral oil water salt heat the oil in the pressure cooker and crackle the cumin seeds, about 20 seconds. add the onion, garlic, ginger and green chilli and fry 4 minutes, until the onion is translucent — you are not browning it. stir in the tomato, turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder and cook 3 minutes until the oil beads at the edges. add the drained chana dal, potato, eggplant and carrot and turn everything through the masala for a minute. pile in the spinach and dill with the water and salt. it will look impossibly full; press it down and it collapses within a minute. close the cooker and cook on high for 3 whistles, then lower the heat and give it 5 minutes more. let the pressure drop on its own. open up and mash everything against the side of the pot with the back of a ladle until it is coarse and green, not smooth. simmer uncovered 5-8 minutes, stirring, until it holds its shape on a spoon. check the salt. serve hot with steamed rice, a spoon of raw onion and a wedge of lemon.

entries.title: Seyal Bhaji
entries.snippet: potato and cauliflower smothered in a wet green coriander masala, quick and everyday
entries.text: seyal bhaji sindhi potato and cauliflower smothered in a wet green coriander masala, quick and everyday vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free potato cauliflower peas coriander leaves (cilantro) onion tomato garlic ginger green chilli turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder cumin seeds lemon / lime neutral oil water salt heat the oil in a kadhai and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds. add the onion and fry 6-7 minutes, until soft and just turning gold at the edges. add the garlic, ginger and green chilli and fry 1 minute until fragrant. stir in the tomato, turmeric, coriander powder, chilli powder and salt and cook 5 minutes until pulpy and oil-flecked. tip in the chopped coriander and cook 3-4 minutes, stirring, until it wilts right down and the masala turns dark green. add the potato, cauliflower and peas and turn them through until every piece is coated green. add the water, cover and cook on low 15 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally, until the potato gives to a knife. uncover, raise the heat and cook 3 minutes more to dry off any loose liquid. squeeze over the lemon, check the salt and serve with phulka or plain rice.

entries.title: Sindhi Biryani
entries.snippet: sharply sour, chilli-hot mutton biryani layered with potato, yogurt and dried fruit
entries.text: sindhi biryani sindhi sharply sour, chilli-hot mutton biryani layered with potato, yogurt and dried fruit gluten-free nut-free mutton / lamb basmati rice yogurt / dahi onion tomato potato ginger garlic green chilli mint coriander leaves (cilantro) dried apricots (khubani) red chilli powder turmeric powder coriander powder garam masala cumin seeds bay leaf cinnamon cloves green cardamom black cardamom saffron kewra water ghee neutral oil water salt fry the sliced onion in the oil over medium heat, 15-18 minutes, stirring, until deep brown and shrunken. drain on paper and reserve. in the same oil, crackle the cumin, bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom and black cardamom for 30 seconds. add the marinated mutton and fry on high for 6-8 minutes, until the yogurt has dried onto the meat and the fat runs clear at the edges. stir in the tomato, coriander powder, half the green chilli, half the mint and coriander, and two-thirds of the birista. cook 5 minutes until the tomato collapses. add 1 cup water and salt, close the cooker and cook 4 whistles, then 12 minutes on low. release the pressure and boil off any thin liquid — the masala should be thick and clinging. fry the halved potatoes in a little oil until golden on the cut faces, then fold them into the meat with the dried apricot and cook 5 minutes. meanwhile bring 3 litres of well-salted water to a rolling boil, add the drained rice and cook 5-6 minutes only — a grain should snap in two when pressed, still white at the core. drain immediately. spread half the rice over the meat in a heavy pot, scatter the remaining birista, mint, coriander and green chilli, then the rest of the rice. drizzle over the saffron milk, kewra water and ghee. seal the pot with a tight lid, cook 2 minutes on high, then set it on the lowest possible heat (or a tawa under the pot) for 25 minutes. rest 10 minutes off the heat, then open and lift the rice from the sides with a flat spoon rather than stirring.

entries.title: Sindhi Kadhi
entries.snippet: roasted gram flour and tamarind curry thick with drumstick and okra, the Sunday lunch of every Sindhi house
entries.text: sindhi kadhi sindhi roasted gram flour and tamarind curry thick with drumstick and okra, the sunday lunch of every sindhi house vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free besan (gram flour) neutral oil fenugreek seeds (methi) cumin seeds mustard seeds curry leaves asafoetida (hing) tomato ginger green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder drumstick (moringa pod) cluster beans (guar) potato carrot okra / bhindi tamarind coriander leaves (cilantro) water salt heat 3 tbsp oil in a kadhai, crackle the fenugreek seeds and cumin, then the mustard seeds, curry leaves and hing. tip in the besan and roast on low heat, stirring constantly, 8-10 minutes until it is sandy-brown and smells like toasted biscuit. add the tomato, ginger and green chilli and cook 3 minutes until the tomato slumps. take the pan off the heat and pour in the hot water in a thin stream, whisking hard the whole time until smooth. return to the heat, add the turmeric, chilli powder and salt, and bring to a boil. simmer 10 minutes — it will thin out and then start to body up. add the drumstick and carrot and simmer 10 minutes. add the cluster beans and potato and simmer another 12-15 minutes, until a knife slides into the potato with no resistance. meanwhile fry the okra in the remaining 1 tbsp oil over high heat for 5-6 minutes, until the cut edges are dry and no longer ropy. stir in the tamarind pulp and the fried okra and simmer 5 minutes. taste: it should be assertively sour against the nutty besan. scatter the coriander over and let it stand 10 minutes off the heat before serving with plain rice or bhuga chawal.

entries.title: Beans Poriyal
entries.snippet: finely chopped french beans steamed dry and finished with fresh coconut
entries.text: beans poriyal south indian finely chopped french beans steamed dry and finished with fresh coconut vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic french beans coconut (fresh or desiccated) moong dal mustard seeds urad dal (black gram) chana dal green chilli dried red chillies curry leaves asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder coconut oil water salt heat the coconut oil and pop the mustard seeds. add the urad dal and chana dal and fry to a light gold, about 1 minute. add the red chilli, green chilli, curry leaves and hing and fry 15 seconds. tip in the chopped beans and drained moong dal with the turmeric and salt and toss to coat. add 4 tbsp water, cover, and cook on low heat for 8 minutes. uncover and check: the beans should be bright green and just tender, with no water left in the pan. if any liquid remains, raise the heat and toss for a minute until the pan is dry. turn off the heat, fold in the grated coconut, and serve with rice and rasam.

entries.title: Bisi Bele Bath
entries.snippet: karnataka's one-pot rice and dal with vegetables, tamarind and hot ghee
entries.text: bisi bele bath south indian karnataka's one-pot rice and dal with vegetables, tamarind and hot ghee vegetarian gluten-free rice (short/medium grain) toor dal (pigeon pea) tamarind sambar powder cinnamon cloves dried coconut (copra) carrot french beans peas onion turmeric powder jaggery asafoetida (hing) curry leaves mustard seeds dried red chillies cashews ghee water salt pressure cook the toor dal with 2 cups water and the turmeric for 4 whistles, then mash it smooth. separately cook the rice with 2.5 cups water until softer than you would want for plain rice. boil the carrot, beans, peas and onion in 1 cup salted water for 8 minutes, until a knife goes in with slight resistance. add the tamarind extract, sambar powder, cinnamon, clove powder, roasted coconut and salt to the vegetables. simmer this uncovered 8 minutes, until the raw tamarind edge disappears and the mixture darkens. fold in the mashed dal and the jaggery and cook 5 minutes more. stir in the cooked rice with the remaining water, a little at a time, until it flows like thick porridge. heat 3 tbsp ghee, pop the mustard seeds, fry the cashews to pale gold, then add the chilli, curry leaves and hing. pour the tempering in, stir once, and serve very hot with the remaining ghee spooned over each plate.

entries.title: Bottle Gourd Kootu
entries.snippet: gentle dal and gourd stew thickened with ground coconut and cumin
entries.text: bottle gourd kootu south indian gentle dal and gourd stew thickened with ground coconut and cumin vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic bottle gourd (lauki) moong dal coconut (fresh or desiccated) cumin seeds green chilli rice (short/medium grain) turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) coconut oil mustard seeds urad dal (black gram) dried red chillies curry leaves water salt pressure cook the moong dal with 1.5 cups water and the turmeric for 3 whistles, then mash it lightly. meanwhile simmer the cubed gourd in 1 cup water with a little salt for 8 minutes, covered. test it with a knife — it should give easily but still hold its cube shape. grind the coconut, 1 tsp cumin seeds, green chilli and raw rice with 1/2 cup water to a smooth paste. add the mashed dal to the gourd along with the salt and bring it to a simmer. stir in the ground coconut paste and the hing and cook 5 minutes on low heat. loosen with hot water until it is thicker than sambar but still spoonable. heat the coconut oil, pop the mustard seeds, add the urad dal, remaining cumin, red chilli and curry leaves. pour the tempering over the kootu and serve with rice and a poriyal.

entries.title: Cabbage Poriyal
entries.snippet: shredded cabbage cooked quick and sweet with coconut and split dals
entries.text: cabbage poriyal south indian shredded cabbage cooked quick and sweet with coconut and split dals vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free cabbage onion coconut (fresh or desiccated) mustard seeds urad dal (black gram) chana dal green chilli dried red chillies curry leaves turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) coconut oil salt heat the coconut oil and pop the mustard seeds until they finish jumping. add the urad dal and drained chana dal and fry until golden, about 1 minute. add the red chilli, green chilli and curry leaves and let them crackle 15 seconds. add the onion and cook 3 minutes until soft and translucent. tip in the cabbage with the turmeric, hing and salt and toss hard to coat everything. cook uncovered on high heat for 5 to 6 minutes, tossing every minute. stop while it still has a slight crunch and smells sweet rather than sharp. take it off the heat, fold in the grated coconut and serve warm.

entries.title: Coconut Chutney
entries.snippet: fresh white chutney of coconut and roasted gram with a mustard tempering
entries.text: coconut chutney south indian fresh white chutney of coconut and roasted gram with a mustard tempering vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free coconut (fresh or desiccated) chana dal green chilli ginger tamarind water coconut oil mustard seeds urad dal (black gram) dried red chillies curry leaves asafoetida (hing) salt put the coconut, roasted gram, green chilli, ginger, tamarind and salt in the blender jar. add 1/4 cup of the cold water and grind in short bursts, scraping down twice. add the rest of the water a spoon at a time until it grinds to a thick, just-pourable paste. grind 30 seconds more so it is smooth but still has a faint grain to it, then scrape into a bowl. heat the coconut oil in a small pan until it shimmers and pop the mustard seeds. add the urad dal and fry until it turns pale gold, about 40 seconds. add the red chilli, curry leaves and hing and let them crackle for 10 seconds. pour the tempering over the chutney and serve without stirring it in.

entries.title: Curd Rice
entries.snippet: cooling mashed rice set in yogurt with a mustard and chilli tempering
entries.text: curd rice south indian cooling mashed rice set in yogurt with a mustard and chilli tempering vegetarian gluten-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) yogurt / dahi milk green chilli ginger curry leaves mustard seeds urad dal (black gram) dried red chillies asafoetida (hing) neutral oil coriander leaves (cilantro) pomegranate salt mash the warm cooked rice against the side of the pot with the back of a ladle until no whole grains remain. stir in the milk and salt and let it stand 5 minutes to cool further. fold in the whisked yogurt, the minced ginger and green chilli. check the consistency — it should be loose and pourable, since it thickens as it sits. heat the oil in a small pan and pop the mustard seeds. add the urad dal, fry to pale gold, then add the red chilli, curry leaves and hing off the heat. pour the tempering over the curd rice and fold it through once. top with pomegranate seeds and coriander and serve cool, not chilled.

entries.title: Idli
entries.snippet: Steamed cakes of fermented rice and urad dal, the lightest thing in Indian breakfast
entries.text: idli south indian steamed cakes of fermented rice and urad dal, the lightest thing in indian breakfast vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) urad dal (black gram) fenugreek seeds (methi) poha (flattened rice) salt soak the rice in one bowl and the urad dal with fenugreek in another, for 5 hours. soak the poha for 20 minutes before grinding. grind the urad dal first with cold water until white, fluffy and doubled in volume. test it: a spoon of batter should float in water. grind the rice to a slightly grainy paste, then fold the two together by hand with salt. cover loosely and ferment 8-12 hours until risen and bubbly. grease the idli plates, fill three-quarters full, and steam 10-12 minutes. a skewer should come out clean. rest 3 minutes before unmoulding, then serve with sambar and coconut chutney.

entries.title: Lemon Rice
entries.snippet: yellow rice cut with lemon, peanuts and split dals for crunch
entries.text: lemon rice south indian yellow rice cut with lemon, peanuts and split dals for crunch vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free rice (short/medium grain) lemon / lime turmeric powder groundnut oil mustard seeds chana dal urad dal (black gram) peanuts dried red chillies green chilli curry leaves asafoetida (hing) ginger coriander leaves (cilantro) salt heat the oil and pop the mustard seeds. add the peanuts and fry 2 minutes until they darken a shade and smell roasted. add the chana dal and urad dal and fry until golden, about 1 minute. add the red chilli, green chilli, curry leaves and hing and let the leaves crackle for 15 seconds. stir in the turmeric and take the pan off the heat immediately. add the lemon juice and salt to the warm tempering and swirl to combine. tip in the cooled rice and fold gently with a flat spatula until every grain is yellow. rest 10 minutes off the heat for the flavour to soak in, then scatter the coriander and serve.

entries.title: Masala Dosa
entries.snippet: Fermented rice and lentil crepe with a spiced potato filling
entries.text: masala dosa south indian fermented rice and lentil crepe with a spiced potato filling vegetarian vegan gluten-free nut-free dairy-free rice (short/medium grain) urad dal (black gram) fenugreek seeds (methi) potato onion green chilli ginger turmeric powder mustard seeds chana dal curry leaves asafoetida (hing) coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil salt soak the rice in one bowl, and the urad dal with the fenugreek in another, for 6 hours. grind the urad dal first with a little cold water until very light and fluffy, then the rice to a slightly grainy paste. combine, add salt and mix with your hand for a minute; the warmth helps it start. cover loosely and leave in a warm place 8-14 hours until doubled, bubbly and faintly sour. stir gently before use and thin with water to a pouring consistency. for the filling, heat oil, splutter the mustard seeds with the chana dal, curry leaves and asafoetida, add the onion, chilli and ginger and cook until soft. add turmeric, then the crumbled potato, salt and coriander. keep warm. heat a flat tawa until a drop of water skitters across it. rub with a halved onion dipped in oil, pour a ladle of batter in the centre and spread outwards in a quick spiral. drizzle oil around the edge and cook until the underside is crisp and deep gold, 2-3 minutes. do not flip. place a scoop of potato in the centre, fold and serve straight away with coconut chutney and sambar.

entries.title: Medu Vada
entries.snippet: crisp-shelled urad dal doughnuts, cloud-soft inside, peppery with ginger
entries.text: medu vada south indian crisp-shelled urad dal doughnuts, cloud-soft inside, peppery with ginger vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free urad dal (black gram) black pepper cumin seeds ginger green chilli curry leaves coriander leaves (cilantro) rice flour asafoetida (hing) neutral oil salt grind the drained dal with 2 to 3 tbsp of ice-cold water, in short bursts, to a thick fluffy paste. beat the batter with your hand for 3 minutes until it lightens in colour and feels aerated. test it by dropping a pinch into a bowl of water — it should float within seconds. fold in the pepper, cumin, ginger, chilli, curry leaves, coriander, hing and salt. heat the oil to 170c — a drop of batter should rise steadily, not shoot to the surface. wet your palm, take a lime-sized ball of batter, flatten it and make a hole through the centre with a wet thumb. slide the vada off your palm into the oil from close to the surface, and fry 4 or 5 at a time. fry 4 to 5 minutes, turning once, until deep gold and the sizzle drops to a quiet crackle. drain on a rack rather than paper so the underside stays crisp, and serve immediately with coconut chutney.

entries.title: More Kuzhambu
entries.snippet: sour yogurt curry with ground coconut and cumin, never boiled
entries.text: more kuzhambu south indian sour yogurt curry with ground coconut and cumin, never boiled vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic yogurt / dahi ash gourd (petha) coconut (fresh or desiccated) cumin seeds green chilli rice (short/medium grain) toor dal (pigeon pea) turmeric powder mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) dried red chillies curry leaves asafoetida (hing) coconut oil salt simmer the ash gourd in 1 cup water with the turmeric and salt for 8 minutes, until translucent at the edges. grind the coconut, cumin, green chilli, soaked rice and toor dal with 1/2 cup water to a very smooth paste. add the paste to the cooked gourd and simmer 6 minutes, until the raw rice smell disappears. take the pan off the heat and let it stop bubbling completely, about 2 minutes. pour in the whisked yogurt, stirring constantly as it goes. return to the lowest possible heat and warm it only until steam rises and it thickens slightly. check the salt and take it off the heat entirely. heat the coconut oil, pop the mustard seeds, add the fenugreek, red chilli, curry leaves and hing. pour the tempering over and serve with hot rice and a dry poriyal.

entries.title: Mysore Pak
entries.snippet: porous gram flour fudge that dissolves in ghee as you bite it
entries.text: mysore pak south indian porous gram flour fudge that dissolves in ghee as you bite it vegetarian gluten-free nut-free besan (gram flour) ghee sugar water green cardamom dissolve the sugar in the water and boil until the syrup reaches one-string consistency, about 6 minutes. lower the heat and add the sifted besan in a thin stream, whisking hard so no lumps form. whisk until the mixture is smooth and glossy, about 1 minute. start adding the hot ghee one ladle at a time, stirring constantly and waiting until each ladle is absorbed. keep going for 12 to 15 minutes as the mixture froths, bubbles and rises in the pan. watch for the moment it turns porous and foamy and the last ghee refuses to be absorbed and pools at the sides. pour it into the greased tray immediately without scraping the pan and level the top with the back of a ladle. wait 4 minutes, then score it into diamonds while still hot. cool completely for an hour before lifting the pieces out.

entries.title: Paruppu Payasam
entries.snippet: moong dal pudding sweetened with jaggery and finished in coconut milk
entries.text: paruppu payasam south indian moong dal pudding sweetened with jaggery and finished in coconut milk vegetarian gluten-free moong dal jaggery coconut milk ghee cashews raisins (kishmish) coconut (fresh or desiccated) green cardamom dry ginger powder (saunth) water pressure cook the roasted dal with 2 cups water for 4 whistles until completely soft. mash the cooked dal lightly with a ladle, leaving some texture. melt the jaggery with 1/2 cup water on low heat, then strain out the sediment. add the strained jaggery syrup to the dal and simmer 8 minutes until it thickens and darkens. stir in the thin coconut milk and simmer 3 minutes more. take the pan off the heat and let it stop bubbling before adding the thick coconut milk. stir in the cardamom and dry ginger powder. heat the ghee in a small pan and fry the coconut slivers to gold, then the cashews, then the raisins until they puff. pour the ghee and fried garnish over the payasam and serve warm.

entries.title: Puliyodarai
entries.snippet: dark tamarind rice heavy with sesame oil, peanuts and roasted spice
entries.text: puliyodarai south indian dark tamarind rice heavy with sesame oil, peanuts and roasted spice vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free rice (short/medium grain) tamarind sesame oil (gingelly / til) mustard seeds chana dal urad dal (black gram) peanuts dried red chillies fenugreek seeds (methi) black pepper coriander powder sesame seeds turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) curry leaves jaggery salt heat 4 tbsp sesame oil in a heavy kadhai and pop the mustard seeds. add the peanuts, chana dal and urad dal and fry until all three are deep gold, about 3 minutes. add the red chillies, curry leaves and hing and fry 20 seconds until the chillies puff. pour in the tamarind extract with the turmeric, coriander powder, jaggery and salt — it will spit, so stand back. simmer on medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes until the paste thickens, darkens and the oil separates and pools at the edges. stir in the roasted fenugreek, pepper and sesame powder and cook 1 minute more, then take it off the heat. fold roughly half the paste into the cooled rice with the remaining 2 tbsp sesame oil. rest at least 30 minutes before serving so the rice takes on the colour evenly.

entries.title: Rasam
entries.snippet: thin peppery tamarind broth, sharp with tomato and crushed pepper
entries.text: rasam south indian thin peppery tamarind broth, sharp with tomato and crushed pepper vegetarian gluten-free nut-free tamarind tomato toor dal (pigeon pea) rasam powder black pepper cumin seeds garlic turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) curry leaves dried red chillies mustard seeds ghee coriander leaves (cilantro) water salt squash the tomatoes into the tamarind extract with your hand and add the turmeric, rasam powder and salt. simmer this uncovered on medium heat for 8 minutes, until the raw tamarind smell goes and the surface turns matte. stir in the crushed pepper and cumin and the garlic, and simmer 2 minutes more. pour in the mashed dal loosened with 2 cups of water and the dal cooking liquid. bring it to the point where a rim of froth rises at the edges, then take it straight off the heat. heat the ghee in a small pan, pop the mustard seeds, then add the red chilli, curry leaves and hing. pour the tempering over the rasam and cover for 2 minutes to trap the aroma. stir through the coriander leaves and serve over hot rice, or in a tumbler alongside.

entries.title: Rava Dosa
entries.snippet: lacy, brittle semolina crepe you pour rather than spread
entries.text: rava dosa south indian lacy, brittle semolina crepe you pour rather than spread vegetarian vegan dairy-free nut-free rava / sooji (semolina) rice flour plain flour (maida) cumin seeds black pepper green chilli ginger curry leaves coriander leaves (cilantro) onion water neutral oil salt whisk the rava, rice flour, maida and salt with 2 cups of water until completely lump-free. stir in the cumin, pepper, chilli, ginger, curry leaves, coriander and onion. add the remaining 2 cups of water and rest the batter 30 minutes. check the consistency — it should run off the ladle in a thin stream like full-cream milk. heat the tawa until quite hot, then lower the heat to medium — a drop of water should vanish instantly. pour the batter from a height in a ring around the outside, then fill the gaps with a few splashes. drizzle a teaspoon of oil around the edge and over the middle. cook undisturbed 2 to 3 minutes until the edges lift by themselves and the surface is dry and golden. flip and cook 45 seconds, or fold straight out of the pan if you like it very crisp. wipe the tawa with half an onion between dosas and stir the batter before each pour.

entries.title: Sambar
entries.snippet: Toor dal and vegetables in a tamarind broth, built on freshly ground sambar powder
entries.text: sambar south indian toor dal and vegetables in a tamarind broth, built on freshly ground sambar powder vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free toor dal (pigeon pea) tamarind drumstick (moringa pod) pumpkin okra / bhindi shallots (small red onions) tomato sambar powder turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) dried red chillies curry leaves coriander leaves (cilantro) jaggery coconut oil salt pressure cook the toor dal with turmeric until completely soft, then whisk it smooth. simmer the tamarind extract with the shallots, tomato and harder vegetables, the sambar powder and salt for 12-15 minutes. add quicker vegetables like okra for the last 5 minutes. stir in the whisked dal and enough hot water to reach a pourable consistency. simmer 8 minutes; do not boil hard. temper mustard seeds, fenugreek, dried chilli, curry leaves and asafoetida in oil and pour it in. add jaggery if the tamarind is sharp, finish with coriander, and rest 10 minutes before serving.

entries.title: Tomato Chutney
entries.snippet: deep red cooked chutney, tangy and hot, for idli and dosa
entries.text: tomato chutney south indian deep red cooked chutney, tangy and hot, for idli and dosa vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free tomato onion garlic dried red chillies urad dal (black gram) chana dal tamarind sesame oil (gingelly / til) mustard seeds curry leaves asafoetida (hing) salt heat 3 tbsp sesame oil and fry the urad dal and chana dal until golden, about 90 seconds. add the red chillies and fry 20 seconds until they darken and swell, then lift out the dals and chillies. in the same oil, cook the onion and garlic until the onion is soft and edged with brown, about 6 minutes. add the tomatoes, tamarind and salt and cook on medium heat for 10 minutes. keep going until the tomatoes lose all shape and the oil pools red at the sides of the pan. cool the mixture completely, then grind it with the reserved dals and chillies to a coarse paste, no water. heat the last 1 tbsp oil, pop the mustard seeds, then add the curry leaves and hing. pour the tempering over the chutney and stir it through.

entries.title: Tomato Pappu
entries.snippet: andhra everyday toor dal cooked soft with sour tomato and garlic
entries.text: tomato pappu south indian andhra everyday toor dal cooked soft with sour tomato and garlic vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free toor dal (pigeon pea) tomato onion green chilli garlic turmeric powder tamarind red chilli powder mustard seeds cumin seeds dried red chillies curry leaves asafoetida (hing) neutral oil coriander leaves (cilantro) water salt pressure cook the dal with the tomatoes, green chilli, turmeric and 2.5 cups water for 5 whistles. let the pressure drop naturally, open, and mash the dal against the side of the pot until smooth. add the salt, chilli powder and tamarind if using, with 1/2 cup water, and simmer 5 minutes. adjust with hot water until it pours thickly off the ladle. heat the oil in a small pan and pop the mustard seeds, then add the cumin. add the crushed garlic and fry until the cloves turn golden at the edges, about 1 minute. add the onion and fry 3 minutes until soft and lightly browned. add the red chilli, curry leaves and hing and let them crackle for 15 seconds. pour the tempering into the dal, stir once, scatter the coriander and serve over hot rice.

entries.title: Upma
entries.snippet: soft savoury semolina with crackling dal, ginger and curry leaves
entries.text: upma south indian soft savoury semolina with crackling dal, ginger and curry leaves vegetarian vegan dairy-free rava / sooji (semolina) water onion green chilli ginger curry leaves mustard seeds urad dal (black gram) chana dal cashews neutral oil coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime salt heat the oil and pop the mustard seeds until they jump and quieten. add the urad dal and chana dal and fry until both turn a light red-gold, about 90 seconds. add the cashews, green chilli, ginger and curry leaves and fry 30 seconds until the leaves crisp. add the onion and cook until soft and translucent, about 4 minutes — no browning. pour in the boiling water with the salt and let it come back to a rolling boil. lower the heat and add the roasted rava in a thin steady stream with one hand while stirring hard with the other. keep stirring for 2 minutes until the mixture pulls away from the sides of the pan. cover and steam on the lowest heat for 3 minutes, then turn off and rest 2 minutes. fluff with a fork, squeeze over the lemon and scatter the coriander.

entries.title: Uttapam
entries.snippet: thick fermented pancake with onion and tomato pressed into the top
entries.text: uttapam south indian thick fermented pancake with onion and tomato pressed into the top vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) urad dal (black gram) fenugreek seeds (methi) onion tomato green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) curry leaves sesame oil (gingelly / til) water salt grind the urad dal and fenugreek with about 3/4 cup cold water to a light, fluffy paste. grind the rice separately with 3/4 cup water to a batter with a fine sandy grain still in it. mix the two by hand with the salt, in wide circular strokes, for 2 minutes. cover and leave to ferment 8 to 12 hours until risen by half and smelling pleasantly sour. heat a tawa on medium until a flick of water dances and evaporates in about 2 seconds. pour a ladle of batter and spread it only slightly, to a thick round about 12cm across. scatter a handful of onion, tomato, chilli, coriander and curry leaves over the wet surface and press them in with the back of the ladle. drizzle a teaspoon of sesame oil around the edge and cook 3 minutes until the base is golden and the top has set matte. flip and cook 90 seconds on the topping side to caramelise the onion, then serve straight from the pan.

entries.title: Vatha Kuzhambu
entries.snippet: dark, oily tamarind gravy with shallots, spiked with fenugreek
entries.text: vatha kuzhambu south indian dark, oily tamarind gravy with shallots, spiked with fenugreek vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free tamarind shallots (small red onions) sesame oil (gingelly / til) sambar powder dried red chillies garlic mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) chana dal curry leaves asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder jaggery rice flour salt heat the sesame oil in a kadhai and pop the mustard seeds. add the fenugreek seeds and chana dal and fry 20 seconds until the fenugreek turns reddish. add the red chillies, curry leaves and hing and let them crackle. add the whole shallots and garlic and fry 5 minutes until the shallots are browned in patches and glossy. stir in the sambar powder and turmeric and fry 30 seconds in the oil. pour in the tamarind extract with the salt and jaggery and bring to a simmer. simmer uncovered on low heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally. it is done when the volume has dropped by a third and the sesame oil floats clear on top. if it is still thin after 25 minutes, stir in the slaked rice flour and cook 2 minutes more. rest 10 minutes off the heat and serve with rice, a spoon of sesame oil and a poriyal.

entries.title: Ven Pongal
entries.snippet: soft rice and moong dal loaded with ghee, black pepper and cumin
entries.text: ven pongal south indian soft rice and moong dal loaded with ghee, black pepper and cumin vegetarian gluten-free rice (short/medium grain) moong dal ghee black pepper cumin seeds ginger curry leaves cashews asafoetida (hing) water salt pressure cook the rice and roasted dal with 5 cups water and the salt for 5 whistles. let the pressure fall on its own, then open and mash the mixture with a ladle until it is soft and shapeless. keep it on the lowest heat while you make the tempering, stirring so the base does not catch. heat the ghee in a small pan and fry the cashews to pale gold, about 40 seconds. add the cumin seeds and crushed pepper and let them sizzle for 20 seconds. add the ginger, curry leaves and hing and fry until the leaves crisp. pour the whole tempering into the pongal and fold it through. check the consistency and loosen with hot water until it falls off the ladle in a thick sheet. serve immediately with the remaining ghee spooned over, alongside coconut chutney.
